c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A woman waiting at a railway station ticket counter realizes the clerk systematically overcharges foreign passengers while local fares remain unchanged

g.passage: Third in line at the ticket counter, Mira watched the clerk hand the elderly farmer ahead of her a fare card stamped with the posted price. For the German couple who stepped up next, however, he quoted a figure nearly double the one printed on the same card. The clerk, a thin man who kept a pencil tucked behind one ______ never once glanced up at the fare board hanging above his window, as though he had long since memorized two different sets of prices.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ear and hummed softly between customers,
ear and hummed softly between customers;
ear and hummed softly between customers—
ear and hummed softly between customers
g.explanation: "a thin man ... customers"는 주어 "The clerk"를 설명하는 비필수 동격 어구이고, 앞에서 쉼표로 열렸으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 주어와 동사 "never once glanced"가 이어진다. 그래서 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론은 두 독립절을 나누는 부호인데, 그러면 주어와 동사가 갈라지고 앞부분은 완전한 절이 되지 못한다. C의 대시는 동격 어구를 묶을 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫아 부호가 서로 맞지 않는다. D는 닫는 부호가 없어서 동격 어구가 어디서 끝나는지 알 수 없고, 동사 앞에서 삽입구가 끝나지 않은 채 남는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a thin man ... customers" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject "The clerk." It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma before the verb "never once glanced," which is why A is correct. B's semicolon is used to separate two independent clauses, but here it would split the subject from its verb and leave an incomplete clause before it. C's dash can set off an appositive, but this one opened with a comma, so closing it with a dash gives you mismatched punctuation. D has no closing punctuation, so the appositive never ends before the verb and runs straight into the main clause.
g.design: 긴 동격 어구 안에 관계절과 'and'로 이어진 동사 두 개를 넣어, 학생이 앞에 있는 여는 쉼표를 찾아야만 짝이 맞는 닫는 부호를 고를 수 있게 했다. 세미콜론과 대시 오답은 얼핏 그럴듯하지만, 문장 구조를 따져 봐야 배제된다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Two former collaborators encounter each other at a provincial museum opening, maintaining professional cordiality while avoiding discussion of their jointly abandoned research

g.passage: At the opening of the regional museum's new wing, Dr. Ilse Varga spotted Tomas Reyhani standing beside a case of Bronze Age loom weights. Reyhani, her coauthor on a study of ancient textile dyes that the two had quietly abandoned eight years earlier, raised his glass with practiced ______ returned the gesture and asked, with equal care, about the lighting in the gallery.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: politeness, she
politeness, and she
politeness and, she
politeness, and, she
g.design: The long appositive between the subject and "raised" hides the fact that the first part of the sentence is already an independent clause. To answer, students must first spot that clause and then see that a second independent clause starts with "she." The wrong answers all have part of the needed punctuation, with commas and the conjunction in the wrong places.
g.explanation: 긴 동격구(her coauthor ... earlier)를 빼고 보면 "Reyhani ... raised his glass with practiced politeness"는 이미 완전한 독립절이고, "she returned ..."도 또 하나의 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사로 이어야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 쉼표를 접속사 뒤에 두어 위치가 잘못되었다. D는 'and' 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 접속사와 주어 사이를 끊는다.
g.explanation_en: Set aside the long appositive (her coauthor ... earlier), and you can see that "Reyhani ... raised his glass with practiced politeness" is already a complete independent clause. "She returned ..." is a second independent clause. You join two independent clauses with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts the comma after the conjunction instead of before it. D adds an extra comma after "and" that separates the conjunction from the subject it introduces.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A translator working alone in a rented room discovers her client deliberately mistranslated contract terms in the previous drafts she must now correct

g.passage: Mirela spread the three earlier drafts across the narrow desk of her rented room, the radiator ticking behind her. At first she assumed the discrepancies were careless errors, but each altered clause, from the shortened delivery window to the vanished penalty for late payment, favored the same ______ the client had not misread the contract at all.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: party,
party, and
party:
party
g.design: 긴 삽입구(from ... to ...)가 주절을 끊어 경계를 흐리게 만들고, 뒤따르는 독립절이 앞 내용의 결론·설명임을 문맥으로 확인해야 콜론을 고를 수 있게 했다. 쉼표+and는 문법적으로 가능해 보이지만 논리 관계가 맞지 않는 매력적 오답이다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'each altered clause ... favored the same party'와 뒤 'the client had not misread the contract at all'은 모두 독립절이며, 뒤 절은 앞 절에서 끌어낸 결론(고의적 오역)을 설명한다. 따라서 설명·결론을 이끄는 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 문법적으로는 허용되지만 'and'가 뒤 절을 단순 추가 정보로 만들어, 앞 절의 증거에서 결론을 도출하는 관계를 드러내지 못한다. D는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("each altered clause ... favored the same party") and the text after it ("the client had not misread the contract at all") are both independent clauses, and the second one states the conclusion Mirela draws from the first: the mistranslations were deliberate. That's why C is correct, since a colon introduces an explanation or conclusion. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B is grammatically possible, but "and" presents the second clause as just another fact added on, so you lose the link between the evidence and what it reveals. D runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A lighthouse keeper observes a shipping company's vessel repeatedly entering restricted waters despite posted warnings, documenting each violation in his logbook

g.passage: From the gallery of the lighthouse, Elias Marr had watched the Halvard, a rust-streaked freighter owned by the Brennick Shipping Company and flying a flag he did not recognize, slip past the warning buoys four times that month______ he entered the hour, the bearing, and the state of the tide in his logbook, pressing so hard that the nib tore the paper.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , each time,
: and each time,
each time
; each time,
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격 수식어(a rust-streaked freighter ... recognize)를 지나 'Elias Marr had watched ... that month'로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'he entered ...'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있고, 도입 부사구 each time 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍을 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 오류(comma splice)다. B는 콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 붙였는데, 이런 조합은 표준 문장부호 규칙에 맞지 않는다. C는 두 독립절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: Once you look past the long appositive (a rust-streaked freighter ... recognize), the text before the blank is a complete independent clause ending with "that month." The text after the blank, "he entered ...," is also an independent clause. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, and a comma can follow the introductory phrase "each time," so D is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes it a comma splice. B puts the conjunction "and" after a colon, and that combination doesn't follow standard punctuation conventions. C has no punctuation between the two clauses at all, which makes it a run-on sentence.
g.design: This is a two-step item: first you have to skip the long appositive to find the main clause, then you have to check where the clause boundary falls. A and C are plausible because they look at first like they connect the adverbial phrase correctly, and B is tempting because it includes a conjunction.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A conservatory violin instructor notices a promising student's technique regressing after the student begins private lessons with a competing teacher across town

g.passage: Madame Okonjo had watched Teodor's bow arm for three years, and she knew its habits as well as her own. Now, in the second week of October, the wrist that had once floated loosely at the frog had stiffened into a rigid hinge, exactly the kind of correction favored by Viktor Halas, a teacher across town known for drilling his pupils through hour after hour of relentless scale exercises______ did not need to ask where her student had been spending his Saturday mornings.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: . She
, she
she
; and she
g.design: The clause boundary falls right after a long appositive phrase ("a teacher across town known for..."), so a fast reader might treat "she did not need to ask" as part of that modifier. The wrong answers include a comma splice, a fused sentence, and a semicolon wrongly paired with "and."
g.explanation: 'Now, in the second week ... scale exercises'는 주어 'the wrist'와 동사 'had stiffened'를 갖춘 독립절이고, 그 끝에는 Viktor Halas를 꾸미는 긴 동격구가 붙어 있다. 'she did not need to ask...'도 새로운 독립절이므로 두 절은 마침표로 나눠야 하고, 그래서 정답은 A이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 'and'를 함께 써서 관례에 맞지 않는다. 세미콜론은 그것만으로 절을 잇거나, 쉼표+and를 써야 한다.
g.explanation_en: The section from "Now, in the second week" through "scale exercises" is an independent clause. Its subject is "the wrist," its verb is "had stiffened," and it ends with a long appositive phrase describing Viktor Halas. "She did not need to ask..." is a second independent clause, so the two need to be split into separate sentences, and A is correct. B joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D pairs a semicolon with the conjunction "and," which isn't conventional. You should use either a semicolon alone or a comma plus "and."

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A cartographer realizes her publisher has altered territorial boundary lines on maps without consulting her original source materials or obtaining permission

g.passage: Spreading the printer's proofs across her drafting table, Ines traced the northern frontier with one finger and stopped. The border along the Varda River, a line she had copied stroke by stroke from the 1887 survey ledgers in the provincial archive, had once followed the water exactly ______ now it bent sharply east, swallowing a valley that none of her sources had ever assigned to either nation. No one at the publishing house had asked to see those ledgers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: exactly, now
exactly; now
exactly now
exactly, so that now
g.explanation: 긴 동격구(a line ... archive)를 지나면 주절의 동사가 had once followed라는 것을 찾아야 하고, 빈칸 뒤 now it bent ...도 독립절이다. 독립절 두 개는 세미콜론으로 연결하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호가 없어 두 절이 붙어 버리고, 'exactly now'가 '바로 지금'처럼 읽혀 뜻이 흐려진다. D는 so that 때문에 결과를 나타내는 절이 되어, 처음에 강을 따랐기 때문에 지금 휘었다는 엉뚱한 인과가 생긴다.
g.explanation_en: Once you get past the long appositive (a line ... archive), you'll find that the main verb is "had once followed." The words after the blank, "now it bent ...," also form an independent clause. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, so B is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C has no punctuation at all, so the clauses run together, and "exactly now" misleadingly reads as a single phrase meaning "right now." D's "so that" turns the second part into a result clause, which suggests the border bent because it once followed the river. That cause-and-effect relationship makes no sense.
g.design: The appositive is long, so you have to find the main clause's verb first. Then you have to confirm that two independent clauses meet at the blank. The wrong choices are a comma splice, a fused sentence that could be misread, and a subordinating conjunction that creates a false cause-and-effect relationship.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A retired postal worker attends a community meeting where officials propose closing the rural mail sorting facility she worked in for thirty-two years

g.passage: Marguerite Alder, who had sorted mail at the Ridgefield facility for thirty-two years and could still recite every rural route by the name of its carrier, sat in the third row of folding chairs and listened as the regional director explained why the building would close in the spring______ the moment he paused for questions, she was already on her feet.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , then,
—while
g.explanation: 긴 비필수 관계절을 걷어내면 'Marguerite Alder ... sat ... and listened ... spring'이 독립절이고, 'the moment he paused ..., she was already on her feet'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 부사 then을 쉼표로만 연결해 comma splice가 되고, B도 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. D는 while 뒤에 'the moment ...'와 이어지는 절이 와서 종속절 구조가 무너지고, 의미상으로도 '동시에'가 '이미 일어서 있었다'와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Set aside the long nonessential "who" clause, and you're left with "Marguerite Alder ... sat ... and listened ... spring," which is an independent clause. What follows the blank, "the moment he paused for questions, she was already on her feet," is also an independent clause. You can join two independent clauses with a semicolon, so C is correct. A uses "then" with only commas around it, and that creates a comma splice. B joins the two clauses with just a comma, which is also a comma splice. D puts "while" right before "the moment...," which breaks the sentence structure. "While" also suggests that the two actions happened at the same time, but the second clause says she was already standing after he paused.
g.design: There is a long nonessential relative clause between the subject and the main verbs, so students have to strip out the modifier before they can see that two independent clauses meet at the blank. A and B are tempting because they look like natural pauses in the sentence, but both are comma splices.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A bookbinder discovers her apprentice has been secretly selling unfinished leather-bound volumes to a competitor at discounted rates

g.passage: Marguerite found the ledger tucked beneath the paring stone, its columns filled in her apprentice's careful, slanted hand. Each entry recorded a volume carried across the canal to Halloran's shop, every one of them still lacking its gilt titling and final coat of wax ______ the prices beside them were barely half of what she charged for finished work.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , worse,
worse,
, worse;
; worse,
g.design: 긴 절대구(every one of them...wax)가 첫 독립절 끝을 가려 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했고, 모든 선택지가 같은 부사 worse를 포함해 문장부호 위치만으로 비교하게 했다.
g.explanation: "Each entry recorded..."는 긴 수식구로 끝나는 독립절이고, "the prices...work"도 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에 세미콜론 같은 강한 경계가 필요하며, 연결 부사 worse 뒤에는 쉼표를 둔다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 절 사이에 아무 문장부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C는 세미콜론이 worse 뒤에 와서 worse가 앞 절에 붙어 버리고, 두 절이 여전히 쉼표로만 나뉜다.
g.explanation_en: "Each entry recorded..." is an independent clause, even though it ends with a long modifier, and "the prices...work" is also an independent clause. That means you need a strong boundary like a semicolon between them, and the transition word "worse" should be followed by a comma. So D is correct. A joins two independent clauses with just a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it's a run-on sentence. C puts the semicolon after "worse," which attaches "worse" to the first clause and still leaves only a comma between the two clauses.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A meteorologist presents weather data to city planners who visibly ignore her flood-risk projections while approving construction in mapped danger zones

g.passage: Dr. Imani Osei clicked to her final slide: a map of the riverside district, shaded in deepening blues where the projected floodplain had crept inland since the last survey ______ the council members, already squaring their papers for the vote on the new apartment blocks, did not look up. Only the stenographer, pen hovering, seemed to study the blue.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: survey;
survey,
survey
survey and
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "a map ... since the last survey"는 콜론 뒤 내용이고, 빈칸 뒤 "the council members ... did not look up"은 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로, 두 독립절 사이에는 세미콜론이 필요하다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓰지만 쉼표가 없어 "survey and the council members"가 하나의 명사구처럼 잘못 읽히며, 긴 두 독립절을 잇는 관습에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank, the sentence describes the slide and ends with "since the last survey." After the blank, "the council members ... did not look up" is a complete independent clause with its own subject and verb, so you need a semicolon between the two independent clauses. That makes A the answer. B joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. D adds "and" but leaves out the comma, so "the last survey and the council members" can be misread as one compound noun phrase, and it doesn't follow the convention for joining two long independent clauses.
g.design: The long participial phrase and the clause-final noun "survey" hide where the first clause ends, and the interrupting phrase after "council members" pushes the main verb far from its subject, so you have to locate both clauses before choosing the boundary.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A dental hygienist overhears her employer scheduling patients for unnecessary procedures while she prepares cleaning instruments in the next room

g.passage: For six years, Marisol had told herself that Dr. Hale's crowded appointment book was simply a sign of his reputation: patients trusted him, so they kept coming back. Now, laying out scalers on a tray in the next room, she heard him on the phone booking three crowns for Mr. Okafor, whose X-rays she had studied that very morning and found free of decay. ______ the comforting explanation she had leaned on for so long no longer seemed to hold, and her hands went still above the tray.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
Consequently,
For example,
Likewise,
g.explanation: 마리솔은 충치가 없는 엑스레이를 직접 확인했는데 의사가 크라운 세 개를 예약하는 것을 듣는다. 빈칸 뒤의 '오랫동안 믿어 온 설명이 더는 성립하지 않는다'는 이 발견에서 나온 결과이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용과 대조되는 듯하지만 빈칸 뒤 문장은 바로 앞의 발견을 뒤집는 게 아니라 그 발견에서 나온 것이다. C는 빈칸 뒤 문장을 앞 내용의 예시로 보는데, 그 문장은 사례가 아니라 결론이다. D는 비슷한 사건을 하나 더 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말이지만 그런 내용이 이어지지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Marisol hears Dr. Hale book three crowns for a patient whose X-rays she checked herself and found free of decay. The sentence after the blank says her long-held explanation no longer holds, and that follows directly from what she just heard, so B is correct. A may seem to fit because there is a contrast in the passage, but the second sentence doesn't push back against her discovery. It comes out of it. C would make the second sentence an example, but it's actually a conclusion. D signals that a similar point is being added, and the second sentence doesn't add anything parallel.
g.design: There's no word in the passage that signals the relationship. The reader has to see that losing faith in her old belief is the result of the X-ray discovery. The contrast-like setup makes A tempting, and the specific detail makes C tempting.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A museum archivist finds that donated correspondence letters have been selectively removed from a collection before her cataloging process began

g.passage: The donor's family had assured Lena that the four boxes held every letter their great-aunt Miriam had ever received, and the inventory sheet taped inside each lid listed the folders in tidy, unbroken sequence. ______ when Lena lifted the contents of the third box onto her worktable, the folder numbers jumped from 41 to 58, and pale rectangles of unfaded cardboard showed where the missing folders had pressed against the lining for decades.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Indeed,
Accordingly,
Still,
For example,
g.design: 첫 문장은 컬렉션이 완전하다는 가족의 주장과 목록을 제시하고, 둘째 문장은 어휘 단서 없이 그 주장을 뒤집는 물리적 증거를 보여 준다. 'For example'(구체적 세부)과 'Indeed'(강조)는 둘째 문장의 세부 묘사나 목록 이야기에 끌려 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉽게 만들었다.
g.explanation: 첫 문장은 상자에 모든 편지가 있고 목록도 끊김 없이 이어진다는 주장을 담고 있지만, 둘째 문장은 번호가 41에서 58로 건너뛰고 폴더가 사라진 자국까지 있다는 사실을 보여 준다. 즉 둘째 문장이 첫 문장의 기대를 뒤집으므로 대조를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용을 강조하거나 덧붙이는 말이어서 컬렉션이 완전하다는 주장과 어긋나는 증거 앞에 올 수 없다. B는 결과를 나타내지만, 폴더가 빠진 것은 가족의 장담 때문에 생긴 결과가 아니다. D는 둘째 문장이 구체적인 세부를 담고 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 그 세부는 '끊김 없는 순서'의 예가 아니라 반대 증거이다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence tells you the family claimed the boxes were complete and that the inventory listed the folders in an unbroken sequence. The second sentence then shows the opposite: the numbers jump from 41 to 58, and there are marks where folders used to be. Because the second sentence goes against what the first sentence led you to expect, the contrast word in C is correct. A adds emphasis to the earlier point, but this evidence argues against the claim that the boxes were complete. B signals a result, yet the family's assurance did not cause the folders to go missing. D may look tempting because the second sentence gives concrete details, but those details contradict the "unbroken sequence" instead of serving as an example of it.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A swimming pool maintenance worker observes a facility manager falsifying chemical safety test results on official documentation sheets

g.passage: Marisol held the test strip up to the light above the pump room door. The pad had barely changed color, which meant there was almost no chlorine in the pool, even though forty children were due for swim lessons at nine. Mr. Dunne took the strip from her, looked at it briefly, and dropped it in the trash. On the county inspection sheet, he wrote 3.0 ppm in the column marked "Free Chlorine," a perfectly normal reading. ______ he put a check in the box for pH balance without opening the testing kit at all, and then he signed the bottom of the page.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Instead,
Consequently,
Nevertheless,
Furthermore,
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 Mr. Dunne이 염소 수치를 허위로 적은 행동이고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그가 pH 검사를 아예 하지 않고 체크한 또 다른 조작 행동이다. 두 번째 행동은 첫 번째 행동에 더해지는 부정행위이므로 추가를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 그가 검사를 '하지 않았다'는 점 때문에 그럴듯해 보이지만, 'Instead'는 앞의 행동을 대신한다는 뜻인데 그는 염소 수치 기록을 그대로 한 뒤 pH 체크도 했으므로 대체 관계가 아니다. B는 한 조작이 다른 조작으로 이어진 것처럼 보이게 하지만, 염소 수치를 허위로 적은 것이 pH 칸 체크의 원인은 아니다. C는 대조를 나타내는데, 두 문장 모두 같은 방향의 행동을 묘사하므로 반전이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank shows Mr. Dunne writing a false chlorine reading, and the sentence after shows him checking the pH box without running the test at all. That second act is another falsification added to the first, so D, which signals addition, is correct. A might seem tempting because he skipped the test, but "instead" means one action replaces another, and he didn't take back the chlorine entry; he did both things. B makes the second act sound like a result of the first, but faking the chlorine number doesn't cause him to check the pH box. C signals a contrast, but both sentences describe the same kind of behavior, so nothing gets reversed.
g.design: There's no wording clue in the passage that points to the answer: the reader has to see that both sentences describe separate acts of falsification in order to pick the "addition" relationship. A is tempting because it picks up on the skipped test, and B is tempting because it suggests one dishonest act led to the next, so you have to compare them carefully to rule them out.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A rural schoolteacher watches administrators systematically discourage low-income students from advanced placement course enrollment during registration week

g.passage: During registration week, Ms. Okafor stood at the back of the gymnasium and watched families line up at the counseling table. A banner above the table read "Advanced Placement: Every Student Belongs," and the principal had repeated the slogan at the morning assembly, promising that no one would be turned away from the new AP biology course. ______ when the Delgado twins, whose father had come straight from his shift at the feed mill, asked for the AP forms, the counselor smiled, suggested they "start with something more manageable," and slid two general science sheets across the table.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: In practice,
For instance,
As a result,
Likewise,
g.design: 대조를 나타내는 어휘 단서(but, however) 없이, 앞에 나온 공식적 약속과 뒤에 나온 실제 행동 사이의 모순으로 관계를 판단해야 한다. 오답들은 피상적으로는 그럴듯하다. 쌍둥이 장면이 '사례'처럼 보이고(B), 상담 교사의 또 다른 행동처럼 보이며(D), 사건이 순서대로 이어지는 것처럼 보인다(C).
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 학교가 모든 학생에게 AP 과정을 열어 두겠다고 공식적으로 약속했다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 상담 교사가 저소득층 쌍둥이를 실제로는 일반 과목으로 유도하는 장면이다. 따라서 공식적인 말과 실제 행동의 차이를 드러내는 A가 정답이다. B는 쌍둥이 장면이 구체적 장면이라 그럴듯해 보이지만, 이 장면은 약속을 보여 주는 사례가 아니라 약속과 모순되는 장면이다. C는 약속 때문에 학생을 돌려보내는 결과가 생겼다는 인과 관계가 되어 논리가 맞지 않는다. D는 앞의 내용과 비슷한 내용이 이어진다는 뜻인데, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 반대 방향의 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence gives the school's official promise that every student is welcome in AP courses, and the next sentence shows the counselor quietly steering low-income twins away from AP. A is correct because it signals the gap between what was officially said and what actually happens. B might look tempting because the twins' scene is specific, but that scene contradicts the promise rather than illustrating it. C would mean the promise caused students to be turned away, which isn't a logical cause-and-effect relationship. g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: In contrast,
Consequently,
For example,
Nevertheless,
g.design: 어휘 단서 없이 '분 단위 과금 + 필름이 짧음'이라는 두 정보를 연결해야 결과 관계가 도출되도록 했다. 대조(A)와 예시(C)는 앞 문장들의 표면적 대비·구체성 때문에 부분적으로 그럴듯하다.

When you put those two facts together, it follows that the cinema paid for scenes it never got, so B is correct. A is tempting because the invoices and the actual reels don't match, but the last sentence isn't contrasting with what came before; it's the conclusion drawn from it. C is tempting because the last sentence sounds specific, but it isn't an example of an earlier claim; it sums up the evidence. D would signal a surprising outcome "despite" the facts, but the overbilling is exactly what those facts lead you to expect.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A geological surveyor's environmental impact assessment is quietly shelved after developers lobby the regional planning authority directly

g.passage: Maren Holt spent eleven weeks mapping the limestone beneath the proposed housing site, and her report warned that the fractured bedrock could channel runoff directly into the town's aquifer. The regional planning authority answered her within days with a courteous letter that praised the report's thoroughness and assured her that every finding would be weighed carefully before any vote. ______ the developers' representatives had already met privately with the planning director twice that month, and when the project was approved in October, Maren's report did not appear in a single set of meeting minutes.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Indeed,
In reality,
Likewise,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 당국이 보고서를 신중히 검토하겠다고 공식적으로 약속했다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 개발업자들이 이미 비공개로 로비했으며 보고서가 회의록에 한 번도 오르지 않았다는 실제 상황을 보여 준다. 즉 겉으로 내세운 약속과 실제가 대조되므로, 겉모습과 실상을 대비시키는 C가 정답이다. A는 정중한 편지가 비공개 회의를 일으킨 원인처럼 만드는데, 회의는 '이미' 열린 것이라 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. B는 앞 내용을 강조하거나 보강할 때 쓰므로 약속을 뒤집는 내용과 맞지 않는다. D는 비슷한 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 앞의 약속과 비슷한 내용이 아니라 정반대 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence describes the authority's official promise to weigh Maren's findings carefully. The next sentence shows what was actually going on: developers had already lobbied the director in private, and the report was never mentioned in any meeting minutes. Because the text sets an outward promise against the hidden truth, C is correct, since it signals that contrast between appearance and reality. A presents the polite letter as the cause of the private meetings, but those meetings had "already" taken place, so the cause and effect run the wrong way. B is used to emphasize or support the previous point, but this sentence undercuts the promise. D adds a similar example, but the sentence that follows is the opposite of the promise, not something similar to it.
g.design: There's no contrast word in the passage. The opposition comes only from setting the authority's courteous promise against the private lobbying. Skimmers may pick A (the sentence does describe an outcome) or B (it adds detail), so they have to check carefully which way the logic runs.

g.passage: Mara had worked in the museum's conservation studio for eleven years and thought she knew all its habits. So when she saw Tomas brushing a synthetic resin onto the back of the Flemish hunting tapestry, a resin the profession's ethics guidelines banned because it could never be removed, she told herself he must have a reason: the gallery reopened on Monday, and the director had been pacing the corridor all week. ______ that excuse fell apart the next morning, when she found the same yellowed residue on three other tapestries, some of them repaired months before any reopening had been announced.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Therefore,
For example,
Likewise,
Still,
g.explanation: 앞 문장에서 Mara는 마감 압박 때문이라는 변명을 받아들이려 하지만, 빈칸 뒤 문장에서는 그 변명이 무너진다. 즉 양보 후 반전의 관계이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 변명을 받아들인 것이 변명이 무너지는 원인이 된 것처럼 만들어 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. B는 다른 태피스트리의 잔여물이 규정 위반의 한 사례처럼 보이지만, 이 문장은 앞 문장의 예시가 아니라 앞 문장의 해석을 뒤집는다. C는 '같은 잔여물'이라는 표현 때문에 유사성처럼 보이지만, 두 문장의 논리는 비슷한 것이 아니라 서로 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: In the first sentence, Mara tries to accept an excuse for Tomas: the deadline pressure. The next sentence says that excuse fell apart. This is a concession followed by a reversal, so D is correct. A suggests that accepting the excuse caused it to fall apart, which gets the cause-and-effect direction wrong. B can look right because the other tapestries seem like more cases of breaking the rules, but the sentence doesn't illustrate the first sentence. It overturns Mara's explanation. C is tempting because of the phrase "the same yellowed residue," but the two sentences contrast with each other rather than show similar ideas.
g.design: Medium difficulty. No word in the passage signals the contrast. Students have to see that the excuse Mara accepts is later disproved. Distractors B and C draw on surface details (more cases, "same" residue), and A sounds like it follows naturally.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A court stenographer records testimony she knows contradicts her employer's prior written summary submitted to the judge that same morning

g.passage: Marguerite's fingers moved across the stenotype keys as steadily as they had for nineteen years. On the stand, the witness described a red sedan pulling out of the parking lot just after nine, not the blue pickup named in the summary her employer, attorney Daniel Hale, had submitted to the judge that very morning. Marguerite understood at once what the difference might cost him, and she knew Hale would read her transcript before anyone else did. ______ she recorded the testimony exactly as it was spoken, the word "red" included.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Even so,
Therefore,
Similarly,
For example,
g.design: Two-step judgment: the reader must notice that the preceding sentence gives reasons for Marguerite to hesitate or alter the record, and then see that her faithful recording goes against that pressure. "Therefore" is tempting to skimmers, because recording testimony accurately seems like a natural result of her long experience.
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 증언이 고용주 Hale에게 불리할 수 있고 Hale이 속기록을 먼저 읽는다는 점, 즉 기록을 망설이거나 바꿀 압박 요인을 제시한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 그녀가 "red"까지 그대로 기록했다는 내용이므로, 압박을 인정한 뒤 뒤집는 양보 전환어 A가 정답이다. B는 정확한 기록이 직업상 당연해 보여 그럴듯하지만, 앞 문장의 내용(Hale에게 미칠 손해와 그의 검토)은 정확히 기록할 이유가 아니라 오히려 망설일 이유이므로 인과 관계가 성립하지 않는다. C는 두 행동이 서로 비슷하다는 뜻인데, 상황을 이해한 것과 기록한 것은 같은 종류의 행동이 아니다. D는 앞 문장의 일반적 진술을 구체화하는 예시가 아니므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence lists pressures on Marguerite: the testimony could hurt her employer, Hale, and he will read her transcript first. These are reasons she might hesitate or change the record. The next sentence says she recorded everything exactly anyway, so the text needs a transition that admits that pressure and then reverses it, which makes A correct. B is tempting because recording testimony accurately sounds like what a stenographer should do, but the pressures in the previous sentence don't cause her accuracy; if anything, they push against it. C would mean the two actions are alike, but understanding the risk and recording the testimony aren't parallel actions. D doesn't work because her recording isn't an example of the sentence before it.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A marine salvage worker discovers the wreck inventory list omits valuable items that mysteriously appear on the company's private ledgers

g.passage: By the third week of the salvage, Mara had hauled up more from the wreck of the Corvina than anyone at Brannock Marine seemed to remember. The official inventory listed hull plating, two anchors, and a dozen crates of ruined tinned goods, yet it said nothing of the brass chronometer or the silver-banded chest she had lifted from the captain's cabin herself. She told herself that the clerk, buried in paperwork, had simply missed a page. ______ the private ledger she glimpsed on Mr. Halvorsen's desk that evening recorded both objects in neat ink, each with a sale price written beside it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
As it turned out,
Likewise,
In other words,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Mara가 누락을 서기의 단순 실수로 여기려 했다는 추측이고, 뒷 문장은 그 물건들이 판매가와 함께 사적 장부에 기록되어 있었다는, 추측을 뒤집는 사실이다. 따라서 예상과 다른 실제 상황을 드러내는 B가 정답이다. A는 서기의 실수가 장부 기록의 원인이 된다는 인과를 만들지만, 실수로 인해 의도적인 판매 기록이 생길 수는 없다. C는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이라는 뜻이지만 뒷 문장은 앞의 추측과 상반된다. D는 앞 문장을 다시 말한다는 뜻인데, 뒷 문장은 새롭고 모순되는 정보를 준다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives Mara's comforting guess that the clerk just missed a page. The sentence after it reveals a fact that overturns that guess: the items were carefully recorded, with sale prices, in a private ledger. You need a transition that shows reality turning out different from what she assumed, so B is correct. A sets up cause and effect, but a careless clerk can't cause a deliberate record of sales. C signals that the two ideas are similar, when they actually contradict each other. D signals a restatement, but the second sentence adds new information that conflicts with the first.
g.design: There's no "but" or "however" in the text to signal the contrast. The student has to notice that the second sentence undoes Mara's assumption. A and D sound plausible because the two sentences are closely connected, and C seems to fit because both sentences talk about records of the items, so the student has to compare the choices to rule them out.

The generic version contained the same active ingredient at the same dose and cost less than a third as much. She told herself there had to be a reason she couldn't see—an allergy noted somewhere in the chart, perhaps, or a problem with the supplier. ______ when a retired schoolteacher counted out crumpled bills at the front desk for her arthritic terrier, Mira pulled the dog's file after closing and read every page. There was no allergy, and no note of any kind.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
For instance,
Even so,
Likewise,
g.explanation: 앞 문장에서 미라는 처방에 자신이 모르는 정당한 이유가 있을 거라고 스스로를 납득시킨다. 그런데 뒤 문장에서는 그 설명을 믿지 않는 듯 직접 서류를 뒤져 확인하므로, 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 서류를 확인한 일이 앞의 자기 설득에서 비롯된 결과라는 뜻이 되지만, 실제로 확인 행동은 그 설득을 의심한 데서 나온 것이다. B는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장에 대한 예시로 만들지만, 서류를 읽은 일은 '이유가 있겠지'라는 생각의 사례가 아니다. D는 두 행동이 비슷하다는 뜻이 되는데, 믿는 것과 확인하는 것은 서로 대조된다.

The next sentence shows her acting against that comforting belief by checking the file herself, so a concession-then-reversal transition fits, and that makes C correct. A suggests that checking the file was a result of convincing herself, but she checks because she doubts that explanation. B turns the second sentence into an example of the first, yet reading the file is not an instance of assuming there's a reason. D signals that the two actions are similar, but trusting and investigating are opposites here.
g.design: There is no word clue pointing to the answer. Students have to see that Mira's self-reassurance is followed by an action that undercuts it. The distractors each offer a plausible relation (cause, example, similarity) that falls apart on a careful reading.

- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A community library branch manager receives orders to quietly reduce acquisitions for sections serving immigrant patrons while expanding English-language collections

g.passage: Marisol read the memo from the district office twice. Funds for the Spanish, Tagalog, and Vietnamese shelves would be "redirected" to the English-language collection, and the change was to take effect without any public announcement. She knew the families who came every Saturday for those books. She knew which grandmother waited each month for the newest Vietnamese novels. ______ she signed the acknowledgment form, filed it in the drawer marked "Policy," and went out to open the doors at nine o'clock as usual.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
For example,
In other words,
Even so,
g.design: 빈칸 앞에는 마리솔이 이용자들을 잘 알고 아낀다는 내용만 있고, 뒤에는 그녀가 지시를 따르는 행동이 나온다. 이 양보 후 반전 관계를 알아채야 하며, 'Consequently'(서명한 것만 보면 결과처럼 읽힘)와 'For example'(앞 문장의 구체적 예처럼 보이는 함정)은 겉핥기로 읽으면 맞는 것처럼 보이도록 만들었다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장들은 마리솔이 이민자 이용자들과 그들이 이 책들에 의지한다는 사실을 잘 안다는 내용이므로, 그녀가 이 지시에 반대할 것이라는 기대가 생긴다. 그런데 뒤 문장에서 그녀는 서류에 서명하고 평소처럼 일한다. 기대와 반대되는 행동이므로 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 이용자를 안다는 사실이 순응하는 이유가 되는 것처럼 만들어 인과 방향이 틀린다. B는 뒤 문장이 할머니 사례처럼 앞 내용의 예시가 아니므로 틀리고, C는 뒤 문장이 앞 내용을 다른 말로 바꾼 것이 아니므로 틀린다.
g.explanation_en: The sentences before the blank show that Marisol knows the immigrant patrons well and knows how much they depend on these books. That leads you to expect she will push back against the memo. Instead, the next sentence shows her signing the form and going about her day as usual. Because her action goes against that expectation, the contrast transition in D is correct. A treats her knowledge of the patrons as the reason she goes along with the order, which reverses the logic. B doesn't work because signing the form is not another example like the grandmother, and C doesn't work because the final sentence doesn't restate what came before.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A painting restorer is instructed to apply techniques that will increase perceived age and authenticity of a canvas to defraud potential buyers

g.passage: Over three evenings in the cramped studio above the frame shop, Ilse had listened to every step of Mr. Varga's plan: the crackle varnish that would split into fine webs as it dried, the coal dust to be worked into the stretcher bars, the auction label from 1911 he had already had printed. She had nodded at each point and even suggested a more convincing yellow for the varnish. ______ when he set the jar on her worktable on the fourth morning and stepped back to watch, her hand stayed flat against the apron, and the brush lay untouched beside the canvas.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Still,
Accordingly,
Moreover,
In other words,
g.explanation: 앞 문장들은 Ilse가 위조 계획을 끝까지 듣고 고개를 끄덕였으며 더 그럴듯한 색까지 제안했다는 내용으로, 그녀가 협조할 것이라는 예상을 만든다. 그러나 뒤 문장에서 그녀는 붓에 손도 대지 않으므로, 앞선 동의와 대조되는 결과를 이끄는 A(Still)가 가장 논리적이다. B(Accordingly)는 동의가 실행으로 이어질 것 같은 인과 흐름을 기대하게 하지만, 실제로는 실행하지 않았으므로 방향이 반대다. C(Moreover)는 협조의 근거를 하나 더 덧붙이는 표현이지만 뒤 문장은 협조를 거부하는 내용이다. D(In other words)는 앞 내용을 다르게 말하는 표현인데, 붓을 들지 않은 것은 동의를 다시 말한 것이 아니라 그와 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The earlier sentences show Ilse listening to the whole forgery plan, nodding along, and even suggesting a better varnish color, so you expect her to go along with it. In the final sentence, though, she won't touch the brush. That contrasts with her earlier agreement, so A (Still) is the most logical choice. B (Accordingly) would fit only if her agreement led her to do the work, but she does the opposite. C (Moreover) would add another sign that she's cooperating, yet the last sentence shows her refusing. D (In other words) would introduce a restatement, but leaving the brush untouched is the opposite of her earlier agreement, not another way of saying it.
g.design: 문장 사이의 관계는 '동의하는 행동이 쌓임 → 예상과 달리 실행을 거부'라는 서사 흐름으로만 드러나고, 'but'처럼 대조를 직접 알리는 단어는 없다. 오답 B와 C는 앞의 동의 행동을 근거로 그럴듯해 보이지만, 마지막 문장까지 읽어야 배제된다.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A prison education coordinator witnesses curriculum materials being systematically withheld from incarcerated students before scheduled classes begin

g.passage: Every Tuesday, Marisol Ortega arrived at Halbrook Correctional forty minutes early to confirm that the boxes of algebra workbooks had cleared the mailroom. The intake log always listed them as "received and approved," stamped and initialed by the same officer. ______ when she reached the classroom, the shelves were bare, and her students sat waiting with nothing but pencils, asking whether this would be another week of copying problems from the whiteboard.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Even so,
In other words,
Similarly,
g.design: 빈칸 앞(기록상 승인·수령)과 뒤(교실에 자료 없음)의 대조를 어휘 단서 없이 읽어 내야 한다. 결과(A)나 재진술(C)도 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보이게 구성했다.
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 교재가 공식 기록상 '수령 및 승인'되었다고 하는데, 뒤 문장은 교실 선반이 비어 있다고 말하므로 기대와 실제가 어긋나는 대조 관계이다. 따라서 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 승인 기록의 결과로 교재가 없다는 인과를 만들지만, 승인되었다면 교재가 있어야 하므로 논리가 거꾸로이다. C는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 재진술로 만드는데, 두 문장은 서로 반대 내용이다. D는 비슷한 사례를 덧붙인다는 뜻이지만 빈 선반은 승인 기록과 비슷한 것이 아니라 반대되는 상황이다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence says the official log listed the workbooks as "received and approved," but the next sentence says the shelves were bare, so what you expect and what actually happens don't match. That's a contrast, so B, which concedes a point and then reverses it, is correct. A sets up cause and effect, but approval should lead to the books being there, not missing, so the logic runs backward. C would make the second sentence a restatement of the first, but the two sentences say opposite things. D signals a similar example, yet the empty shelves are the opposite of the approved log, not something like it.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — An engineering inspector conducts final safety checks on a building while knowing the contractor substituted cheaper materials for expensive specifications

g.passage: Mara Okonkwo walked the third floor of the Halvorsen building with her clipboard, tapping each steel column as though it might answer her. Every weld she examined was clean, every bolt was tightened to the figure printed on the drawings, and the fire-rated drywall sat flush against the studs. ______ she knew from the invoices she had found in the contractor's trailer that the beams overhead were a lighter grade than the plans required, and no amount of tidy finishing would change what they could carry.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Likewise,
Even so,
Indeed,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Mara가 본 모든 것이 흠잡을 데 없다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 보이지 않는 보가 규격 미달이라는 사실을 그녀가 안다고 말하므로 양보 후 반전 관계이며 C가 정답이다. A는 깔끔한 마감이 규격 미달 정보를 '초래했다'는 인과를 만들어 논리 방향이 맞지 않는다. B는 두 문장이 같은 종류의 정보라고 보지만, 앞은 긍정적 점검 결과이고 뒤는 숨겨진 결함이라 대조된다. D는 앞 내용을 강조하거나 덧붙이는 표현인데, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장을 강화하는 것이 아니라 뒤집는다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence says that everything Mara can see passes inspection, but the next sentence tells us she knows the hidden beams are a lighter grade than the plans require. That's a concession followed by a reversal, so C is correct. A sets up a cause-and-effect link, as if the clean finishing work caused the problem with the beams, and that logic doesn't hold. B treats the two sentences as similar points, but one describes good inspection results and the other describes a hidden flaw, so they contrast. D would emphasize or build on the first sentence, but the second sentence actually undercuts it.
g.design: There's no "but" or "however" in the passage to signal the relationship, so students have to see that a list of positive observations is followed by hidden knowledge that contradicts them. The wrong answers, "Indeed" and "Consequently," look tempting if you skim, because the second sentence seems to continue the inspection description.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 긴 수식어구/도치 뒤의 주어-동사 일치, 병렬 구조, 수식어 위치(dangling modifier), 정동사 vs 분사/부정사 선택처럼 구조 파악이 필요한 문제.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A hotel housekeeping supervisor discovers management policies that intentionally assign fewer staff to rooms occupied by guests of particular ethnic backgrounds

g.passage: Marisol had supervised the fourth-floor crew at the Halvorsen Hotel for nine years, and she could read the morning assignment board the way other people read a clock. That was why the new spreadsheet stopped her cold. The column labeled "priority tier," which the regional managers had inserted without a word of explanation and which matched, row by row, the surnames printed on the guest registry, ______ how many housekeepers each room would receive. She scrolled down twice, hoping she had misread it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: determining
determine
were determining
determined
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The column"이고, 두 개의 which절은 그 주어를 꾸미는 삽입 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하면서 과거 시제 서술(had supervised, stopped)과도 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다. B와 C는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "managers"나 "surnames"에 맞춘 복수형이라 단수 주어 "column"과 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The column." The two "which" clauses are just interrupting modifiers that describe it. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject and also fits the past-tense narration ("had supervised," "stopped"). That makes D correct. A is a participle, so the sentence would be left without a main verb. B and C are finite verbs, but they are plural forms that match the nearby nouns "managers" or "surnames," not the singular subject "column."
g.design: 긴 이중 which 삽입절 뒤에 복수 명사(managers, surnames)를 배치해 주어-동사 일치를 흐리게 하고, 정동사 필요성과 과거 시제 문맥 확인의 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A pharmaceutical sales representative learns her company concealed moderate side effects in clinical trial data when marketing the new medication

g.passage: Dana had memorized the pitch by heart: fewer hospital visits, faster recovery, a cleaner safety profile than any competitor. But sitting in her car outside the clinic, she finally read the appendix she had always skipped. The binder of trial summaries that her regional manager had handed her at the spring conference, along with a sticky note urging her to "lead with the efficacy numbers," ______ no mention of the persistent dizziness reported by nearly a fifth of the study's participants.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: made
were making
making
have made
g.design: 긴 관계절과 'along with' 삽입구가 단수 주어 'binder'와 동사를 갈라놓아, 복수 명사(summaries, numbers)에 끌린 오답과 정동사가 없는 분사형 오답을 비교하게 했다. 서술 시제(과거)도 함께 확인해야 한다.
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The binder'이고, 'of trial summaries', 관계절 'that her regional manager...', 'along with...' 삽입구는 모두 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 주어에 맞고 지문의 과거 서술 시제와도 일치하는 정동사 A가 정답이다. B는 과거 서술과는 어울리지만, 가까이 있는 복수 명사 'summaries'에 끌린 복수 동사이다. D 역시 복수 동사이고, 현재완료 시제라 과거 서술과도 맞지 않는다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The binder." The phrase "of trial summaries," the clause "that her regional manager...," and the "along with..." phrase are all just modifiers. So you need a singular finite verb that also matches the passage's past-tense narration, and that's A. B fits the past-tense storytelling, but it's a plural verb that agrees with the nearby noun "summaries" instead of the real subject. D is also plural, and its present perfect tense doesn't match the past narration. C is a participle, so the sentence would have no main verb and wouldn't be complete.

g.passage: The memo arrived on a Tuesday, unsigned but unmistakable in its phrasing. Mara read it twice at the circulation desk, then a third time in the stacks, where no one could watch her face. The request from the chairs of the chemistry and biology departments, each of whom had spent the past year defending their laboratory's grant renewals, ______ that the library "reconsider the visibility" of three articles whose data quietly undercut those renewals.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: urge
urged

g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "She asked ... arrived"와 뒤 "he only shrugged ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사로 이어야 하므로 "arrived, but"인 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어서 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. C는 "and" 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 절의 흐름을 끊는다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("She asked ... arrived") and the words after it ("he only shrugged ...") are both independent clauses. To join two independent clauses, you need a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so D, "arrived, but," is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. C adds an unnecessary comma after "and," which breaks up the clause for no reason.
g.design: 독립절 두 개 사이에 쉼표+접속사가 필요한지 묻는 단일 규칙 문제로, 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스·무종지문·불필요한 쉼표라는 흔한 오개념이다.

c.instruction: 문장이 분사구문(-ing/-ed로 시작)이나 비교구문(Unlike/Like/As)으로 시작하고, 그 뒤에 콤마와 함께 주절이 이어지는 문법 문제를 만들어라. 정답은 수식어구가 의미적으로 가리키는 대상과 정확히 일치하는 주절 주어를 가져야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어와 무관한 엉뚱한 명사를 주어로 둔 경우, (2) 수식 대상과 비슷하지만 다른 범주의 명사(예: 사람 대신 그 사람의 저작물)를 주어로 둔 경우, (3) 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상을 주어로 둔 경우로 구성하라. 정답과 오답 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이 되도록 만들어 순수하게 의미적 연결 판단만으로 정답을 가려내게 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Taxi dispatcher receives instructions systematically assigning longer routes to passengers paying with government assistance vouchers versus credit cards

g.passage: Marisol had worked the night console at Bellweather Cab for eleven years, and she knew the city's streets the way some people know old hymns. When the new routing memo arrived, she read it twice: rides paid with county assistance vouchers were to be sent the long way, over the Calder Bridge and back, while riders paying by credit card got the direct line. Scrolling through the memo a third time as her coffee went cold, ______ the voucher rides on tonight's board had already been flagged in red.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the night shift grew quieter as she saw that every one of
Marisol realized that every one of
Marisol's console displayed that every one of
the memo itself showed her that every one of
g.explanation:
분사구문 'Scrolling through the memo a third time as her coffee went cold'에서 메모를 스크롤하고 커피가 식어 가던 사람은 Marisol이다. 따라서 콤마 뒤 주절의 주어는 Marisol이어야 한다. 정답은 B이다.
A: 주어 'the night shift'는 수식어와 상관없는 명사다. 야간 근무 시간이 메모를 스크롤할 수는 없다. 뒤에 she가 나오지만 주절 주어가 아니므로 수식 관계가 성립하지 않는다.
C: 'Marisol's console'은 Marisol의 이름이 들어가 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 사람이 아니라 사람에게 딸린 기기를 주어로 삼은 경우다. 스크롤하는 것은 콘솔이 아니라 사람이다.
D: 'the memo'는 단수 동사 showed와 수일치가 맞고 문장도 완전하지만, 메모가 스스로를 스크롤할 수는 없다. 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상이다.
g.explanation_en:
The introductory phrase "Scrolling through the memo a third time as her coffee went cold" describes Marisol, since she is the one scrolling through the memo while her coffee cools. That means the subject of the main clause right after the comma has to be Marisol. The answer is B.
A: The subject, "the night shift," has nothing to do with the modifier, because a work shift can't scroll through a memo. "She" does show up later in the sentence, but it isn't the subject of the main clause, so the modifier still doesn't attach to Marisol.
C: "Marisol's console" looks tempting because it contains her name. But the subject is the console, a device that belongs to her, not Marisol herself. A person scrolls, not a console.
D: "The memo" agrees with "showed," and the sentence is complete. However, the memo can't scroll through itself, so the modifier can't logically describe it.
g.design: I used an opening participial phrase whose logical subject is Marisol. Each wrong option gives the main clause a grammatical subject that doesn't match: an unrelated noun (the night shift), a possession that sounds similar (Marisol's console), and a singular noun that agrees with its verb but can't logically do the action (the memo). Only the meaning tells them apart.

c.instruction: 완전한 독립절 두 개가 이어지는 문장을 만들되, 두 절 사이의 논리적 관계(대조, 인과, 부연설명 중 하나)를 분명히 드러내라. 정답은 그 관계에 어울리는 구두점 전략(등위접속사+쉼표, 세미콜론, 또는 마침표) 하나이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 구두점 종류는 맞지만 절 관계와 안 맞는 접속사를 쓴 경우, (2) 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (3) 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 세미콜론을 넣어 절을 어색하게 쪼갠 경우로 만들어라. 정답 선택 시 단순히 구두점 유무가 아니라 절 간 의미 관계까지 고려해야 정답을 고를 수 있도록 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Wedding photographer discovers studio contracts contain hidden clauses allowing owner to sublicense images to stock photo agencies without bride consent

g.passage: The studio was quiet after the Hendricks reception, and Mara spread the paperwork across the light table to find the album delivery date. Instead, on page nine, she found a paragraph granting the owner "perpetual rights to sublicense all captured images to third-party agencies." She thought of the bride laughing under the arbor that afternoon, her face now potentially for sale in some stock catalog. Mara had photographed forty weddings for the studio______ she had never once read past the first page of the contract she handed each couple to sign.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , so
, but
but;
g.explanation:
정답 C. 빈칸 앞(Mara had photographed forty weddings for the studio)과 뒤(she had never once read ... contract)는 둘 다 완전한 독립절이다. 두 절의 관계는 대조로, 계약서를 수십 번 다뤘는데도 정작 읽지는 않았다는 뜻이다. 따라서 대조를 나타내는 등위접속사 but에 쉼표를 붙인 ", but"이 문법적으로도 의미상으로도 맞다.
A(", so"): 쉼표+등위접속사 구조라서 문법적으로는 맞지만, so는 인과 관계를 나타낸다. 결혼식을 40번 찍었기 때문에 계약서를 안 읽었다는 말은 논리적으로 성립하지 않는다.
B(","): 쉼표만으로 독립절 두 개를 이은 콤마 스플라이스다.
D("but;"): 세미콜론이 접속사 뒤에 붙어서 절 경계가 아닌 곳에서 문장을 끊는다. but이 앞 절 끝에 매달리게 되어 앞 절이 불완전해진다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is C. The text before the blank ("Mara had photographed forty weddings for the studio") and the text after it ("she had never once read past the first page...") are both independent clauses. The two ideas contrast: she handled the contract dozens of times, yet she never actually read it. A comma plus "but" joins the clauses correctly and signals that contrast.
A (", so") has a valid structure, a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, but "so" signals cause and effect. Photographing forty weddings doesn't logically cause someone to skip reading a contract, so the relationship is wrong.
B (",") is a comma splice, because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma.
D ("but;") puts the semicolon after the conjunction, so the sentence breaks at the wrong spot. The first part ends with a dangling "but" and isn't a complete clause.
g.design: Two independent clauses are joined by contrast. Each wrong answer matches one assigned error type: a wrong-logic conjunction in the right punctuation pattern (", so"), a comma splice, and a semicolon placed off the clause boundary. Because ", so" is grammatically valid, students can only rule it out by thinking about how the two clauses relate in meaning.

c.instruction: 짧은 부사적 삽입어구(however, for example, in fact 등)가 문장 중간에 등장하되, 이것이 두 독립절 사이에 낀 것인지 아니면 한 절 내부의 단순 삽입인지 헷갈리게 설계하라. 정답은 실제 절 구조(삽입어 앞뒤가 독립절인지 아닌지)에 맞는 구두점이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각해 불필요하게 세미콜론/마침표를 쓴 경우, (2) 실제 절 경계인데 쉼표만 찍어 콤마 스플라이스를 만든 경우, (3) 삽입어 앞뒤 쉼표를 하나만 찍어 비대칭으로 만든 경우로 구성하라. 문장을 읽고 삽입어 앞뒤가 각각 완전한 절인지 아닌지를 판별해야만 정답을 고를 수 있게 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Municipal building inspector witnesses elected officials approving variance requests violating zoning codes in exchange for campaign contributions from developers

g.passage: Ruth Okafor had measured the Halvorsen lot twice, and both times the developer's planned tower rose nine stories above what the zoning code allowed. She said nothing at the hearing, only watched the five council members raise their hands to grant the variance. Later, scanning the campaign finance filings in her cramped office, she confirmed what she had suspected: the members who had voted to waive the height limit ______ accepted generous contributions from Halvorsen Partners only a week before the vote.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: had; in fact,
had. In fact,
had, in fact
had, in fact,
g.explanation: 정답 D. 빈칸 앞의 'the members who had voted to waive the height limit had'는 주어와 조동사만 있고 본동사가 없어서 완전한 절이 아니다. 본동사 'accepted'는 빈칸 뒤에 나온다. 따라서 'in fact'는 두 독립절 사이의 경계가 아니라 한 절 안(조동사와 본동사 사이)에 들어간 삽입어구이므로 앞뒤에 쉼표를 하나씩 짝지어 찍어야 한다. A: 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각해 세미콜론을 썼다. 세미콜론 앞이 'had'로 끝나는 불완전한 절이라 쓸 수 없다. B: 같은 착각으로 마침표를 찍어 'the members ... had.'라는 문장 조각(fragment)을 만든다. 마침표 뒤를 독립 문장처럼 읽고 싶게 만드는 함정이다. C: 삽입어 앞에만 쉼표가 있고 뒤에는 없어서 쉼표가 비대칭이다. 삽입어구는 양쪽 쉼표로 감싸야 한다.
g.explanation_en: The answer is D. Look at what comes before the blank: "the members who had voted to waive the height limit had." This has a subject and a helping verb, but its main verb, "accepted," only appears after the blank. So this is not a complete clause. That means "in fact" doesn't sit between two independent clauses. It's an interrupter inside one clause, placed between "had" and "accepted," and it needs a pair of commas around it. A is wrong because it treats the interrupter as a boundary between clauses and uses a semicolon. A semicolon needs a complete clause on each side, and "...had" isn't one. B makes the same mistake with a period, which leaves a fragment ending in "had." C is wrong because it puts a comma before "in fact" but not after it. An interrupter has to be set off with commas on both sides.
g.design: 'in fact'가 조동사 had와 본동사 accepted 사이에 들어가도록 했다. 앞부분이 길고 그 자체로 완결된 듯 보여서 절 경계로 착각하기 쉽다. 오답은 세미콜론(경계 착각), 마침표(문장 조각), 한쪽에만 찍은 쉼표(비대칭)로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 문장이 분사구문(-ing/-ed로 시작)이나 비교구문(Unlike/Like/As)으로 시작하고, 그 뒤에 콤마와 함께 주절이 이어지는 문법 문제를 만들어라. 정답은 수식어구가 의미적으로 가리키는 대상과 정확히 일치하는 주절 주어를 가져야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어와 무관한 엉뚱한 명사를 주어로 둔 경우, (2) 수식 대상과 비슷하지만 다른 범주의 명사(예: 사람 대신 그 사람의 저작물)를 주어로 둔 경우, (3) 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상을 주어로 둔 경우로 구성하라. 정답과 오답 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이 되도록 만들어 순수하게 의미적 연결 판단만으로 정답을 가려내게 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A translator working alone in rented room discovers client deliberately mistranslated contract terms in previous drafts she must now correct

g.passage: The radiator in the rented room ticked through the night, and the single lamp threw Ilse's shadow across a stack of earlier versions she had inherited from another translator. Her assignment had seemed simple: polish the final English text of a shipping contract. Setting each Portuguese clause beside its English counterpart and reading both aloud under her breath, ______ that every penalty for late delivery had been quietly reduced, always in favor of the same client.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Ilse realized
Ilse's pencil annotations revealed
the radiator's steady ticking made clear
the inherited versions showed
g.explanation:
정답 A. 문장 앞의 분사구 "Setting each Portuguese clause beside its English counterpart and reading both aloud under her breath"는 조항을 나란히 놓고 소리 내어 읽는 행동을 묘사한다. 그러니 주절의 주어는 그 행동을 실제로 하는 사람, 곧 Ilse여야 한다. 주어를 Ilse로 두면 수식어가 올바르게 연결된다.
B: Ilse의 연필 메모(그녀가 만든 산출물)는 Ilse와 관련은 있지만 사람이 아니라 사물이다. 메모가 조항을 나란히 놓거나 소리 내어 읽을 수는 없으므로 현수 수식어(dangling modifier)가 된다.
C: 라디에이터 소리는 지문에 나오기는 하지만 수식어가 묘사하는 행동과 아무 관계가 없는 명사다.
D: "versions showed"는 주어와 동사의 수가 맞고 문장 형태도 완전하다. 하지만 이 버전들은 비교되는 대상일 뿐, 스스로 비교하고 읽는 주체가 될 수 없다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is A. The opening phrase, "Setting each Portuguese clause beside its English counterpart and reading both aloud under her breath," describes things a person does: lining up the clauses and reading them aloud. The subject of the main clause has to be the one doing those things, which is Ilse. "Ilse realized" makes the phrase attach correctly.
B is wrong because Ilse's pencil annotations are something she produced, not Ilse herself. Notes can't set clauses side by side or read aloud, so the modifier dangles.
C is wrong because the radiator's ticking is mentioned in the passage, but it has nothing to do with the action the phrase describes.
D is tempting because "versions showed" agrees in number and forms a complete sentence. But the versions are the things being compared. They can't do the comparing or the reading.
g.design: I opened the sentence with a participial phrase whose doer is a person (the translator). All four options make grammatically complete sentences, so you can only find the answer by asking who could logically perform the action. The wrong answers are: an unrelated noun from the scene (the radiator), something the translator made rather than the translator herself (her notes), and a noun that agrees with its verb but is the object of the comparison (the versions).

c.instruction: 완전한 독립절 두 개가 이어지는 문장을 만들되, 두 절 사이의 논리적 관계(대조, 인과, 부연설명 중 하나)를 분명히 드러내라. 정답은 그 관계에 어울리는 구두점 전략(등위접속사+쉼표, 세미콜론, 또는 마침표) 하나이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 구두점 종류는 맞지만 절 관계와 안 맞는 접속사를 쓴 경우, (2) 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (3) 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 세미콜론을 넣어 절을 어색하게 쪼갠 경우로 만들어라. 정답 선택 시 단순히 구두점 유무가 아니라 절 간 의미 관계까지 고려해야 정답을 고를 수 있도록 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Lighthouse keeper observes shipping company vessel repeatedly entering restricted waters despite posted warnings, documenting each violation in logbook

g.passage: Each dawn, Maren climbed to the lamp room and recorded the freighter's passage in the logbook in her careful, slanting hand. The warning buoys had been repainted twice that spring, and the notice at the harbor mouth declared the shoals closed to all commercial traffic in letters a meter tall. The captain of the Calloway could surely read that notice ______ steered his vessel past it every Tuesday, close enough that Maren could count the rust stains along the hull.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , so he
, but he
, he
but; he
g.design: 독립절 두 개를 대조 관계로 이었다(선장은 경고문을 읽을 수 있다 ↔ 그런데도 매주 그 앞을 지나간다). 오답은 각각 구두점은 맞지만 접속사가 인과를 나타내는 경우, 콤마 스플라이스, 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 세미콜론을 넣은 경우로 만들었다.
g.explanation:
정답 B: 'The captain … could surely read that notice'와 'he steered his vessel past it …'는 둘 다 독립절이다. 경고문을 읽을 수 있다는 내용과 그런데도 그 앞을 지나간다는 내용은 대조 관계이므로, 쉼표와 등위접속사 but으로 잇는 것이 맞다.
A: 쉼표와 등위접속사를 쓴 형식은 맞다. 하지만 so는 인과를 나타낸다. 경고문을 읽을 수 있다는 사실이 금지 수역에 들어가는 이유가 될 수는 없으므로 논리가 맞지 않는다.
C: 쉼표 하나만으로 독립절 두 개를 이은 콤마 스플라이스다.
D: 세미콜론이 but과 he 사이에 들어가서 'but'이 앞 절 끝에 붙어 버린다. 그 결과 앞 절은 접속사로 끝나는 어색한 구조가 되고, 절이 경계가 아닌 곳에서 잘린다.
g.explanation_en:
B is correct. "The captain of the Calloway could surely read that notice" and "he steered his vessel past it every Tuesday" are both independent clauses. The second clause contrasts with the first: he can read the warning, yet he ignores it anyway. When you join two independent clauses that contrast, a comma plus "but" is the right choice.
A uses the correct pattern (comma plus coordinating conjunction), but "so" signals cause and effect. Being able to read a warning is not a reason to sail past it, so the logic breaks down.
C is a comma splice: it joins two independent clauses with only a comma.
D puts the semicolon after "but." That leaves the first part ending with a dangling conjunction, so the sentence is split at a point that is not a real clause boundary.

c.instruction: 노트에 제시된 서로 다른 두 개의 사실(예: 각각 다른 대상/사건/수치에 대한 독립된 정보)을 하나의 문장으로 자연스럽게 결합하여 주어진 목표(예: 두 대상을 비교하거나 관계를 설명)를 달성하는 문제를 만들어라. 오답은 각각 (1) 한쪽 사실만 담아 목표를 절반만 달성, (2) 두 사실을 결합했지만 목표와 무관한 조합, (3) 노트에 없는 내용을 추가해 사실을 왜곡한 문장으로 구성하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Retired postal worker attends community meeting where officials propose closing rural mail sorting facility she worked in for thirty-two years

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Last Sort" is a short story by Delphine Arceneaux.
- Its protagonist, Ruth Hadley, is a retired postal worker who sorted mail at the Caddo Junction facility for thirty-two years.
- In one scene, Ruth attends a community meeting where a regional official proposes closing the facility.
- During his slide presentation, the official refers to the facility only as "redundant capacity."
- Throughout the meeting, Ruth remembers the facility through the names on the envelopes she handled there, such as the families who received letters from soldiers overseas.
- At the story's climax, Ruth stands up and recites the facility's delivery routes from memory.
g.question: The student wants to highlight the difference between how the person behind the plan and the main character each view the building. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas the official proposes closing the Caddo Junction facility at a community meeting, he presents his plan in a slideshow that calls it "redundant capacity."
Whereas Ruth Hadley sorted mail at the Caddo Junction facility for thirty-two years, at the story's climax she stands and recites its delivery routes from memory.
Whereas the official reduces the Caddo Junction facility to "redundant capacity," Ruth Hadley recalls it through the names of the families whose letters passed through her hands there.
Whereas the official calls the Caddo Junction facility "redundant capacity," Ruth Hadley warns the meeting that closing it would put hundreds of her former coworkers out of work.
g.explanation:
정답 C: 목표는 폐쇄를 제안하는 사람(관리)과 주인공(Ruth)이 시설을 어떻게 보는지 대비하는 것이다. C는 두 개의 서로 다른 사실, 즉 관리가 시설을 "redundant capacity"라고만 부른다는 점과 Ruth가 봉투에 적힌 이름들을 통해 시설을 기억한다는 점을 결합해 비인격적 관점과 개인적 관점을 대비시킨다.
A(한쪽 사실만 담음): 관리 쪽 정보만 있어 Ruth의 관점이 빠져 있다. 'Whereas' 구문을 썼지만 실제로는 대비가 이루어지지 않으므로 목표를 절반만 달성한다.
B(목표와 무관한 결합): 두 사실을 결합했지만 둘 다 Ruth에 관한 것이다(32년 근무, 배달 경로 암송). 관리의 관점이 없어 요구된 대비가 성립하지 않는다.
D(노트에 없는 내용 추가): 대비 구조는 갖췄지만, Ruth가 수백 명의 실직을 경고한다는 내용은 노트에 없다. 노트에서 Ruth는 이름과 기억을 통해 시설을 떠올릴 뿐이므로 사실을 왜곡한 문장이다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, C: Your goal is to contrast how the man proposing the closure (the official) and the protagonist (Ruth) each see the facility. C combines two separate facts from the notes. The official refers to the facility only as "redundant capacity," while Ruth remembers it through the names of the families whose letters she sorted. Putting these together sets an impersonal view against a personal one.
A gives only one side. Every detail is about the official. Even though the sentence uses "Whereas," it never contrasts him with Ruth, so it meets only half the goal.
B combines two facts, but both are about Ruth: her thirty-two years at the facility and her reciting the routes. Without the official's view, the required contrast doesn't happen.
D uses the right contrast structure but adds something the notes never say. Ruth doesn't warn that hundreds of coworkers will lose their jobs. The notes only say she remembers the facility through names, so D misrepresents the story.
g.design: I combined two separate facts, the official's label for the facility and Ruth's memories, into one contrast sentence. All four choices use the same "Whereas X, Y" frame. The wrong answers are built on three different errors: one gives only one side of the contrast, one combines two facts about the same character, and one adds information not in the notes. The question uses none of the correct answer's key words ("redundant," "names").

g.question: The student wants to describe what happens in the scene and present Hale's unverified claim about its origins, giving each the degree of confidence the notes support. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

g.explanation:
정답 A: 장면의 사건(상담교사들이 저소득 학생들에게 반이 '찼다'고 말하고 다른 학생은 등록시킴)은 소설 속에서 실제로 일어나는 일이므로 단정적으로 서술해야 한다. 반면 Hale의 자전적 근거 주장은 Vance가 확인하지 않았으므로 'suggests ... may have'처럼 잠정적으로 표현해야 한다. A는 두 가지를 모두 충족한다.
B: 'has shown'은 확인되지 않은 Hale의 추측을 입증된 사실처럼 과장한다.
C: 소설에 분명히 나오는 사건을 'appear possibly to discourage some'으로 불필요하게 약하게 줄여 말해, 확정적 사실을 잠정적인 것으로 축소한다.
D: 확실성 수준은 맞지만, 자전적 근거 주장을 독자 리뷰 분석(60%, 이는 Ruth에 대한 평가에 관한 것)과 혼동해 잘못된 출처를 내세운다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. The events of the scene really happen in the novel: counselors tell low-income students the course is "full" and then enroll other students. So these events should be stated directly. Hale's claim that the scene comes from Vance's own life has not been confirmed by Vance, so it should be framed tentatively ("suggests... may have"). A does both of these things.
Choice B is incorrect because "has shown" turns Hale's unconfirmed guess into a proven fact. That overstates it.
Choice C is incorrect because it weakens events that clearly occur in the novel ("appear possibly to discourage some"). This makes a definite plot fact sound uncertain when it isn't.
Choice D is incorrect because its level of certainty is fine, but it gets the source wrong. It credits the autobiographical claim to the reader-review analysis. That 60% figure is about how reviewers judged Ruth, not about where the scene came from.
g.design: Notes mix definite plot facts with a tentative scholarly claim and a statistic about something else. The three wrong answers are an overstatement (B), an unnecessary hedge on a plot fact (C), and a mix-up of the claim's source with the reader survey (D). All four choices use the same sentence frame.

A: 증언과 축자 인증 의무는 담았지만 Lass의 요약서가 빠져 있어서 무엇과 모순되는지가 드러나지 않는다. 목표를 절반만 달성한 문장이다.

g.explanation_en:

In the afternoon, the witness testifies that he left shortly after nine. Putting these side by side shows the contradiction, which explains why Dorota faces a dilemma: she must record testimony that goes against her employer's summary.
A: This choice includes the testimony and the word-for-word rule but leaves out Lass's summary. Without it, the reader can't tell what the testimony contradicts, so the choice meets only half the goal.
C: This choice combines two facts from the notes, but they are the wrong ones: Dorota's job and her hesitation to sign. It never mentions either account of the witness's whereabouts.
D: The notes never say Lass lied on purpose or that Dorota changed her transcript. They only say she hasn't signed yet. This choice adds details that aren't in the notes and changes the facts.

g.explanation:

A(지나치게 세부적): 다이빙 일지의 회수 기록만 담았습니다. 공식 목록 누락과 사적 장부 기재라는 대비가 없으므로 어떤 발견인지 드러나지 않습니다.

g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, C: The discovery that starts the conflict is a contrast. The crates are missing from the official inventory but recorded in a private ledger. C includes both facts, the absence from the official inventory and the listing in the supervisor's ledger, so it puts the discovery itself in focus.
A is too detailed. It only says what Ilse's dive log shows. It leaves out the missing inventory entry and the private ledger, so the discovery never appears.
