g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Mara has worked for three years as a photographer at Delgado Studio, which books weddings and pays her a flat fee per event.

Mara had never read past the first page of her contract; Mr. Delgado had always said the rest was "standard boilerplate." But after a former bride emailed her a link to a stock-photo website, where the bride's own first dance was being sold as "Romantic Couple, Ballroom," Mara spread all eleven pages across her kitchen table. Clause 14(c) granted the studio "perpetual rights to sublicense all captured images to third parties." Clause 9 stated that clients' "approval of usage" was required only for "promotional displays within the studio." Since a stock agency was neither a promotional display nor located inside the studio, Mara realized that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the bride's photograph had probably been posted on the stock site without the studio's knowledge, since Clause 14(c) applied only to images Mara herself had approved.
the bride could have stopped the sale of her photograph simply by refusing approval, since Clause 9 protected couples from any use of their images outside their wedding albums.
the contracts let Mr. Delgado sell couples' photographs to agencies like the one the bride found without ever asking the couples, since their approval was needed only for displays in the studio.
Mr. Delgado had violated his own contracts by selling the photograph, since Clause 14(c) allowed sublicensing only to promotional displays within the studio.
g.explanation: 14(c)항은 스튜디오가 모든 사진을 제3자에게 재라이선스할 수 있게 하고, 9항은 고객 승인을 스튜디오 내 홍보 전시에만 요구한다. 스톡 에이전시는 그 범위 밖이므로 이 판매에는 고객 승인이 필요 없다는 결론이 나오며, 이것이 C다. A는 14(c)항에 Mara의 승인 조건이 있다고 잘못 보고, 스튜디오가 몰랐다는 근거도 없다. B는 9항의 승인 범위를 전시 밖의 모든 사용으로 넓혀 잘못 해석했다. D는 9항의 '홍보 전시' 제한을 14(c)항에 섞어 붙였으므로 계약 위반이라는 결론이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Clause 14(c) lets the studio sublicense every image to third parties, and Clause 9 requires client approval only for promotional displays inside the studio. A stock agency falls outside that one approval rule, so the studio can sell to it without asking couples, which is choice C. Choice A invents a condition in Clause 14(c) about Mara's approval, and nothing in the text suggests the studio didn't know about the sale. Choice B stretches Clause 9's approval requirement to cover every use, but the clause limits it to in-studio displays. Choice D takes Clause 9's "promotional display" wording and wrongly applies it to Clause 14(c), so there's no basis for saying the contract was violated.
g.design: To get the answer, students have to connect two clauses: the broad sublicensing right and the narrow approval requirement. Each wrong choice misreads or blends one of the clauses, so students can't pick the answer by matching words; they need to read closely.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A municipal building inspector witnesses elected officials approving zoning variance requests in exchange for campaign contributions from real estate developers

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Teodora Vance, a building inspector for the city of Harlow, sits in the back row of a zoning board meeting.

For three years Teodora had flagged the same lot on Merrick Street: the soil was unstable, and her reports said no structure taller than four stories should stand there. Tonight the developer, Paul Graydon, wanted nine. Before the vote, she watched him lean across the aisle and press a folded campaign flyer into Councilman Ashby's hand, the same flyer whose donor list she had read that morning, Graydon's name printed near the top beside a sum larger than her yearly salary. When the variance passed five to two, no one on the board mentioned her reports; they had not been entered into the record at all. Teodora understood then that her careful measurements had never been part of the decision, and that the board's approval had been settled ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: by the two board members who voted against the variance, whose objections were overruled.
by her own reports, which the board had reviewed and judged too cautious for the site.
by new soil tests from Graydon's engineers, which showed the lot could safely hold nine stories.
by Graydon's donations long before anyone in the room raised a hand to vote.
g.design: 두 정보(후원자 명단의 거액 기부 + 보고서가 기록에서 아예 빠짐)를 연결해야 결론이 나오며, 오답 A·B는 지문의 표결·보고서 요소를 부분적으로 활용한다.
g.explanation: 테오도라는 그레이던의 이름이 거액과 함께 후원자 명단에 있었다는 것과 자신의 보고서가 기록에조차 들어가지 않았다는 것을 알게 되므로, 결정은 표결 전에 기부로 이미 정해졌다는 D가 정답이다. A는 반대표 2표를 언급하지만 승인을 정한 것은 반대자들이 아니다. B는 보고서가 검토되었다고 하나 지문에서는 기록에 들어가지도 않았다. C의 새 토양 검사는 지문에 근거가 없고, 측정이 결정과 무관했다는 깨달음과도 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: Teodora connects two facts: Graydon's name sits beside a huge sum on the donor list, and her reports were never even entered into the record. Together these show the outcome was fixed by money before the vote, so D is correct. A points to the two "no" votes, but the people who lost the vote didn't settle the approval. B says the board reviewed her reports, yet the text says they were never entered into the record at all. C brings in new soil tests that the text never mentions, and it clashes with her realization that measurements played no part in the decision.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A woman at railway station ticket counter realizes clerk systematically overcharges foreign passengers while keeping local fares unchanged

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Marta, who grew up in the river town, is waiting in line at its small railway station.

Ahead of Marta, a tourist with a canvas backpack asked in halting phrases for a one-way ticket to Velden. The clerk named a price, and the young man paid without a word. Marta had made the same trip every Friday for six years, and she knew the fare by heart; what the clerk had asked was nearly double that. A moment later a farmer in muddy boots bought the same ticket and was charged the usual amount. Then a couple speaking German stepped up, and again the price swelled. The fare chart was posted behind the glass, but it faced the clerk's chair, not the window. Marta realized that the difference had nothing to do with the destination or the time of day; it depended only on ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: whether the clerk could tell that a traveler was a stranger to the town and its customary prices.
whether a traveler was carrying luggage that suggested a longer or more expensive journey.
whether a traveler bought a one-way ticket instead of a round-trip ticket on a Friday.
whether the clerk could read the posted fare chart clearly from his position behind the glass.
g.explanation: A가 정답이다. 같은 Velden행 표를 산 승객 중 외지인(관광객, 독일어 쓰는 부부)만 비싸게 냈고 현지 농부는 정상 요금을 냈다. 게다가 요금표가 창구 밖을 향하지 않아 외지인은 정가를 확인할 수 없으므로, 차이는 승객이 이곳의 요금을 모르는 외지인인지에 달려 있다. B는 관광객의 배낭에는 맞지만 독일어 부부의 짐은 언급되지 않고 행선지도 모두 같다. C는 모두 같은 편도표를 샀으므로 차이를 설명하지 못하며, D는 요금표가 점원 쪽을 향하므로 오히려 지문과 반대이고 승객별 차이를 설명하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: Choice A is correct. Everyone bought the same ticket to Velden, but only the outsiders (the tourist and the German-speaking couple) paid more, while the local farmer paid the usual fare. Also, the fare chart faces the clerk and not the window, so strangers have no way to check the real price. That means the difference depends on whether a traveler is an outsider who doesn't know the local fares. Choice B fits the tourist's backpack, but the text never mentions the couple's luggage, and everyone was going to the same place. Choice C fails because all of them bought the same one-way ticket, and choice D contradicts the text: the chart faces the clerk, and it couldn't explain why different passengers paid different amounts anyway.
g.design: 외지인 공통점 파악과 요금표 방향 단서를 연결해야 한다. B·C는 지문 일부 사실(배낭, 편도·금요일)에 기대고, D는 요금표 단서를 거꾸로 읽게 만든 오답이다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Two former research collaborators encounter each other at provincial museum opening, maintaining surface cordiality while avoiding their abandoned joint project

g.passage: At the opening of the Harrowgate Regional Museum, Ilse found Tomas standing before the glass case of Bronze Age loom weights—the same weights the two of them had once spent three summers cataloguing for a book they never finished. He greeted her warmly, praised the lighting, asked after her sister, and remarked twice on the excellent wine. When a curator approached to say how much she had admired their early article on the weights and to ask whether the longer study would ever appear, Tomas laughed, said that the canapés were vanishing fast, and steered the group toward the buffet. Ilse noticed that he did not glance back at the case, though he had been studying it intently a moment before. The ease of his conversation, she concluded, was ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: evidence that he had finally lost interest in the loom weights and no longer thought about the work they had shared.
a way of keeping the talk on safe, trivial ground so that the unfinished book would not have to be discussed.
a sign that he hoped the curator's question would persuade Ilse to resume the study with him.
proof that he resented the curator for praising an article that he considered minor.
g.explanation: 토마스는 공동 연구 이야기가 나오자 카나페 얘기로 화제를 돌리고, 직전까지 유심히 보던 진열장을 다시 보지 않는다. 이 두 단서를 연결하면 그의 가벼운 대화는 미완성 책 이야기를 피하기 위한 수단이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 화제를 피한다는 점은 맞지만, 그가 진열장을 열심히 보고 있었다는 사실과 어긋난다. C는 큐레이터의 질문과 연결되지만 그는 그 질문을 피했으므로 재개를 바란다는 근거가 없다. D는 그가 화제를 돌린 것을 설명하려 하지만 큐레이터에 대한 원망이나 논문을 하찮게 여긴다는 근거는 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: Tomas changes the subject to the canapés the moment the unfinished study comes up, and he stops looking at the case he had been studying closely just before. Put those two clues together and his easy chatter looks like a way to avoid talking about the book, so B is correct. A gets the avoidance right, but it doesn't fit the fact that he had been studying the case intently. C ties into the curator's question, but Tomas dodges that question, so nothing suggests he wants to restart the work. D tries to explain why he changes the subject, but the text gives no hint that he resents the curator or thinks the article is minor.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect two clues: Tomas changes the subject, and he had been studying the case closely. A, C, and D each match part of the passage, but a careful reading rules each of them out.

c.instruction: 문장 앞부분에 분사구문(예: ~ing, having p.p., ~ed로 시작하는 수식어구)을 배치하고, 그 수식어구가 실제로 가리키는 행위자가 문장 중간이나 뒤쪽 명사구에 숨어 있도록 지문을 구성하라. 정답은 그 행위자를 주어 자리에 정확히 배치한 문장이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어구와 표면상 가장 가까운 무생물 명사를 주어로 착각, (2) 문장 앞부분의 배경 명사를 주어로 착각, (3) 수식어구가 가리키는 행위자와 문법적으로만 비슷한 다른 인물/사물을 주어로 착각하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A retired postal worker attends community meeting proposing closure of the rural mail sorting facility where she worked thirty-two years

g.passage: Folding chairs had been set out in uneven rows across the grange hall, and a county official stood beside an easel displaying a map of the proposed consolidation, each doomed route traced in red. Marguerite Olsen took a seat near the back, her coat still buttoned. Having sorted the valley's mail by hand for thirty-two years, ______ she could have recited the households along each red line without once glancing at the map.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the facility's old sorting cases still held, in Marguerite's memory, nearly every name on the list of affected routes;
the grange hall was filled, Marguerite saw, with nearly every name on the list of affected routes;
Marguerite recognized nearly every name on the official's list of affected routes;
the county official recognized, Marguerite noticed, nearly every name on the list of affected routes;
g.explanation: 분사구문 'Having sorted the valley's mail by hand for thirty-two years'의 의미상 주어는 32년간 우편물을 분류한 사람, 즉 Marguerite이다. 따라서 주절 주어는 Marguerite여야 하며, C가 이를 정확히 주어 자리에 둔다. A: 분사구문 내용과 가장 가까워 보이는 무생물 명사 'sorting cases'를 주어로 삼아, 분류함이 우편을 분류했다는 뜻이 되는 현수 수식어다. B: 앞 문장의 배경 명사 'grange hall'을 주어로 삼아 강당이 우편을 분류한 것처럼 된다. D: 문법적으로 같은 사람 주어지만 'county official'은 우편을 분류한 인물이 아니어서 수식 관계가 틀어진다. Marguerite는 삽입구에만 숨어 있을 뿐이다.
g.explanation_en: The opening modifier, "Having sorted the valley's mail by hand for thirty-two years," has to describe whoever comes right after the comma as the subject. The person who sorted the mail is Marguerite, so she must be the subject. Choice C does exactly that. Choice A makes the "sorting cases" the subject, which says the cases sorted the mail. They're a lifeless object that only seems connected to sorting. Choice B makes the "grange hall," a setting noun from earlier in the passage, the subject, which is illogical. Choice D uses a person as the subject, but it's the wrong one: the county official didn't sort the valley's mail. In both A and D, Marguerite shows up only inside a side phrase, so she never becomes the subject.
g.design: Marguerite, the real agent, appears in the earlier sentences and inside the distractors' side phrases. Each wrong answer puts something else in the subject spot: a nearby object (sorting cases), a setting noun (grange hall), or a different person (official). All four choices share a similar frame built on "nearly every name on the list."

c.instruction: 두 개의 절을 제시하되 그 사이의 논리 관계(대조/인과/단순나열 중 하나)가 접속사나 구두점 없이도 문맥상 명확히 드러나도록 구성하고, 학생이 먼저 그 관계를 파악한 뒤 알맞은 구두점·접속사 조합을 고르게 하라. 정답은 논리관계에 맞는 올바른 결합(세미콜론+접속부사, 종속접속사 등)이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 콤마만으로 두 절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (2) 논리 관계가 반대인 접속사(대조인데 인과 접속사 사용 등) 사용, (3) 불필요한 접속사 중복(and+however 등 형태)을 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A prison librarian discovers administrators are removing certain history and sociology books from inmate collections before her weekly distribution rounds

g.passage: Every Tuesday, Marisol Okafor pushed her squeaking cart down the corridor of C Block, carrying the same forty titles she had logged by hand the night before. This week, something was wrong with the count. The history and sociology shelf she had stocked on Monday afternoon held only three volumes by morning______ that nothing had been taken from the library, and the memo on her desk thanked her for her "continued diligence."
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , the warden's office insisted
; therefore, the warden's office insisted
, and however, the warden's office insisted
; nevertheless, the warden's office insisted
g.design: 책이 사라졌다는 사실과 교도소장실이 아무것도 가져가지 않았다고 주장하는 내용이 대조 관계임을 먼저 파악해야 한다. 그 뒤에 세미콜론+대조 접속부사를 고르게 했다. 오답은 콤마 스플라이스, 인과 접속부사, and+however 중복으로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 D. 앞 절(선반에 책이 세 권만 남음)과 뒤 절(교도소장실은 아무것도 가져가지 않았다고 주장함)은 서로 맞지 않는 대조 관계다. 독립절 두 개를 세미콜론과 대조 접속부사 nevertheless로 이은 D가 문법과 논리 모두에 맞는다.
A: 독립절 두 개를 콤마 하나로만 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다.
B: 구두점 형식은 맞지만, therefore는 인과 관계를 나타낸다. 책이 사라진 것이 '아무것도 가져가지 않았다'는 주장의 원인이 될 수 없으므로 논리가 맞지 않는다.
C: 등위접속사 and와 접속부사 however를 함께 써서 연결어가 중복된다. 게다가 and는 단순 나열을 뜻하므로 대조 관계와도 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice D is correct. The first clause says the shelf was nearly empty. The second says the warden's office claimed nothing had been taken. Those two ideas contrast. D joins the two independent clauses with a semicolon and the contrast word "nevertheless," so it is correct in both grammar and logic.
A creates a comma splice: it joins two independent clauses with only a comma.
B has correct punctuation, but "therefore" signals cause and effect. The missing books don't cause the office's denial, so the logic is wrong.
C uses two connectors at once, "and" plus "however," which is redundant. Also, "and" signals simple addition, not contrast.

c.instruction: 인용문(따옴표 안 문장)과 이를 감싸는 주절, 혹은 병렬로 나열된 여러 절을 함께 제시하고 그 전체에 걸쳐 시제나 형태가 일관되어야 하는 문장을 만들어라. 정답은 인용문/병렬구조 전체 맥락과 시제가 일치하는 형태이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 인용문 시제와 어긋나는 시제 선택, (2) 병렬 구조 중 한 항목만 다른 시제/형태로 만든 것, (3) 문장 내 한 절과는 맞지만 전체 문맥과는 어긋나는 시제를 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A wildlife census technician realizes her employer falsified population count data to justify eliminating a protected species habitat protection zone

g.passage: Mireille scrolled through the survey spreadsheet a third time. Her field notes recorded forty-one breeding pairs of marbled godwits in the wetland, but the report her supervisor had filed with the county listed only nine, low enough to strip the marsh of its protected status. When she raised the discrepancy, he barely looked up from his desk. "The numbers are whatever the board needs them to be," he said. That night, alone in the field office, she reopened the archived data files, compared each entry against her GPS logs, and ______ every altered count in red.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: marked
is marking
marking
had marked
g.explanation: 정답 A: 빈칸은 주어 she의 세 번째 동사로, reopened, compared와 병렬을 이룬다. 서술 전체가 단순과거로 진행되고 "That night"의 같은 시점에 순서대로 일어난 동작이므로 단순과거 marked가 알맞다. B(is marking): 인용문 속 현재시제(are, needs)에 이끌린 선택이다. 인용문은 상사가 말한 직접화법일 뿐이고, 이를 감싸는 서술은 과거시제이다. C(marking): 병렬 항목 중 이것만 분사형이 되어 주어 she의 정형동사가 빠지고 구조가 무너진다. D(had marked): 앞의 "the report her supervisor had filed" 절의 과거완료와는 맞아 보이지만, 표시하는 동작은 파일을 다시 열고 비교한 뒤에 일어났으므로 그보다 앞선 시점을 나타내는 과거완료는 문맥과 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: A is correct. The blank is the third verb in a series with the subject "she": she "reopened," "compared," and ___. The narration is in simple past, and all three actions happen in order on "That night," so the simple past "marked" keeps the series parallel and the tense consistent. B ("is marking") follows the present tense inside the supervisor's quotation ("are," "needs"). But that is his direct speech, and the narration around it stays in the past. C ("marking") turns only one item in the series into a participle, so "she" has no finite verb for that action and the parallel structure breaks. D ("had marked") seems to match the past perfect in "the report her supervisor had filed." But the marking happened after she reopened and compared the files, not before them, so the past perfect gives the wrong time order.
g.design: I put present-tense direct speech, a past perfect clause, and a series of three past-tense verbs in one excerpt. Each wrong answer matches only part of the text: B matches the tense inside the quotation, C breaks the form of the series, and D matches only one clause's past perfect. To pick A, the student has to read across the whole text.

c.instruction: 문장 앞부분에 분사구문(예: ~ing, having p.p., ~ed로 시작하는 수식어구)을 배치하고, 그 수식어구가 실제로 가리키는 행위자가 문장 중간이나 뒤쪽 명사구에 숨어 있도록 지문을 구성하라. 정답은 그 행위자를 주어 자리에 정확히 배치한 문장이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어구와 표면상 가장 가까운 무생물 명사를 주어로 착각, (2) 문장 앞부분의 배경 명사를 주어로 착각, (3) 수식어구가 가리키는 행위자와 문법적으로만 비슷한 다른 인물/사물을 주어로 착각하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A freelance translator notices her agency systematically underpays translators from non-Western countries while charging clients full rates for identical work quality

g.passage: By nine o'clock the office was empty; her editor, Tomás, had left an hour earlier, wishing her luck with the Portuguese contract. Mira stayed behind with the agency's invoices open in one window and the translators' rate sheet in another. Scrolling past the figures for the Manila and Lagos teams for the third time, ______ identical client fees, identical quality scores, and translators abroad paid less than half of what she earned for the same work.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the rate sheet laid bare for Mira what she had long suspected:
Mira found laid bare what she had long suspected:
the agency's invoices laid bare for Mira what she had long suspected:
her editor, Tomás, found laid bare what Mira had long suspected:
g.explanation:
정답 B. 분사구문 'Scrolling past the figures ... for the third time'는 화면을 내리는 사람을 꾸민다. 지문에서 늦게까지 남아 창을 띄워 놓은 사람은 Mira이므로, 그녀가 주절의 주어가 되어야 수식이 맞는다.
A: 수식어구 바로 앞에 나온 무생물 명사 'rate sheet'를 주어로 삼았다. 하지만 요율표가 스스로 화면을 내릴 수는 없으므로 현수 수식어(dangling modifier)가 된다.
C: 앞 문장에 배경으로 나온 'invoices'를 주어로 삼았다. 이 역시 무생물이라 '스크롤하는' 행위자가 될 수 없다.
D: Tomás는 사람이라 문법적으로는 행위자처럼 보인다. 그러나 그는 한 시간 전에 퇴근했으므로 화면을 내린 사람이 아니고, 수식 관계가 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en:
The correct answer is B. The opening phrase "Scrolling past the figures ... for the third time" describes a person moving down a screen. The subject of the main clause has to be that person. In the passage, Mira is the one who stayed late with both windows open, so "Mira found laid bare..." correctly connects the modifier to the right person.
A is wrong because it makes "the rate sheet" the subject. That's the nearest noun to the phrase, but a rate sheet can't scroll, so the modifier dangles.
C is wrong because it makes "the agency's invoices" the subject. The invoices are only background from the previous sentence, and they can't do the scrolling either.
D is wrong because Tomás is a person, so he might look like a fitting subject. But he left an hour earlier, so he isn't the one scrolling, and the modifier points to the wrong person.
g.design: The passage opens the key sentence with a participial phrase whose actual doer, Mira, appears earlier only as background. Each wrong answer uses the same sentence structure but swaps in a different subject: the nearest inanimate noun (rate sheet), a background noun (invoices), or a different person who could grammatically do the action (Tomás).

c.instruction: 두 개의 절을 제시하되 그 사이의 논리 관계(대조/인과/단순나열 중 하나)가 접속사나 구두점 없이도 문맥상 명확히 드러나도록 구성하고, 학생이 먼저 그 관계를 파악한 뒤 알맞은 구두점·접속사 조합을 고르게 하라. 정답은 논리관계에 맞는 올바른 결합(세미콜론+접속부사, 종속접속사 등)이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 콤마만으로 두 절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (2) 논리 관계가 반대인 접속사(대조인데 인과 접속사 사용 등) 사용, (3) 불필요한 접속사 중복(and+however 등 형태)을 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A railway maintenance worker observes supervisors deliberately scheduling track inspections during shifts when safety violations would go unreported to federal regulators

g.passage: Every Thursday, Ruth Okafor walked the switching yard with her clipboard, noting the cracked ties and loosened spikes that the inspection crews were supposed to catch. The posted schedule claimed that inspections rotated evenly across all shifts. Ruth had kept her own log for eleven months, ______ every inspection had fallen on the overnight shift, when the federal liaison was never on site to receive a report.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: though, and in it,
so; in it, therefore,
however; in it,
however, in it,
g.explanation: 먼저 논리 관계를 봐야 한다. 공지된 일정은 점검이 모든 근무조에 고르게 돌아간다고 했지만, Ruth의 기록에서는 점검이 전부 야간조에 몰려 있었다. 따라서 두 절은 대조 관계다. 뒤 절도 독립절이므로 'however; in it,'처럼 대조 접속부사 뒤에 세미콜론을 찍고 새 절을 시작하는 C가 정답이다. 이렇게 하면 however가 앞 절 끝에 붙어 일정과 기록을 대비시킨다. A: 'though'와 'and'를 함께 써서 접속어가 불필요하게 겹치고, 연결도 어색하다. B: 'so'와 'therefore'는 인과를 나타내므로 대조라는 논리에 맞지 않고, 인과 연결어가 중복되기도 한다. D: 'however'는 접속부사라서 콤마만으로는 두 독립절을 이을 수 없다. 콤마 스플라이스다.
g.explanation_en: Start with the logic. The posted schedule says inspections rotate evenly across all shifts, but Ruth's log shows every inspection fell on the overnight shift. That is a contrast. Both parts are independent clauses, so you need "however; in it,": the contrast adverb ends the first clause, and the semicolon properly separates the two clauses. That makes C correct. A stacks two connectors, "though" and "and," which is redundant and awkward. B uses "so" and "therefore," which signal cause and effect, not contrast, and they also repeat each other. D joins two independent clauses with only commas around "however." That's a comma splice, because "however" is a conjunctive adverb and can't join clauses by itself.
g.design: 이 문항은 학생이 먼저 대조 관계(공지된 일정과 실제 기록의 차이)를 파악해야 풀린다. 정답은 세미콜론과 접속부사를 함께 쓴 형태다. 오답은 각각 콤마 스플라이스(D), 인과 연결어(B), 접속어 중복(A)으로 만들었다.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 주장과 이유를, 텍스트 2는 같은 주제의 다른 접근을 각각 짧게 제시하되 서로를 언급하지 않게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자라면 텍스트 1의 주장에 어떻게 반응할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 2의 전제에서만 도출되는 반응으로 만들고, 오답 3개는 텍스트 1의 내용을 반복하는 선택지, 텍스트 2의 결론만 되풀이하는 선택지, 텍스트 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온 선택지로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A small-town newspaper editor receives pressure from advertisers to suppress stories about workplace safety violations at the largest local factory employer

g.passage:
Text 1
In Marisol Venn's novel The Linden Ledger, editor Ruth Abernathy decides to hold her story about safety violations at the Corwin Mill. The mill's owners buy half the paper's ad space, and Ruth reasons that if the Ledger folds, the town loses its only paper. "A paper that survives can tell the truth next year," she tells her reporter. "A paper that dies tells nobody anything."

Text 2
In a short story by Theo Ashgrove, a weekly's publisher prints an account of injuries at the town cannery the same week the cannery cancels its advertising. Ashgrove's narrator observes that every week a paper stays quiet, readers learn what its silence costs and who can buy it. By the time such a paper is ready to speak, the narrator says, no one is listening.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Ashgrove's narrator in Text 2 most likely respond to Ruth's reasoning in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that she is right to keep the paper alive, since a newspaper that closes can no longer report on anything in the town
By insisting that she should print the story at once, since a publisher's duty is to report injuries whatever happens to the advertising
By arguing that her real mistake is letting the mill buy so much ad space, since a paper should never depend on a single advertiser
By pointing out that her plan undermines itself, since staying quiet now would destroy the very credibility the paper needs if it is to report the truth later
g.explanation: 정답 D: Text 2의 화자는 신문이 침묵할 때마다 독자가 그 침묵이 매수될 수 있다는 것을 알게 되고, 결국 말할 준비가 되었을 때는 아무도 듣지 않는다고 본다. 이 전제를 적용하면 '살아남은 신문이 내년에 진실을 말할 수 있다'는 Ruth의 논리는 스스로를 무너뜨린다. 지금의 침묵이 나중에 진실을 전할 때 필요한 신뢰를 없애기 때문이다. A: Ruth의 주장(Text 1)을 그대로 되풀이할 뿐 Text 2의 관점이 아니다. B: Text 2의 결론(기사를 실었다)만 반복한 것으로, Ruth의 '나중에 말하겠다'는 근거를 신뢰 상실의 논리로 반박하지 못한다. 게다가 Text 2는 이를 의무로 제시하지도 않는다. C: 광고주 한 곳에 대한 의존 문제는 Text 2가 다루지 않는 쟁점이다.
g.explanation_en: D is correct. Ashgrove's narrator believes that each week a paper stays silent, readers learn that its silence can be bought, so by the time it finally speaks, no one is listening. Apply that idea to Ruth's reasoning that a paper that survives "can tell the truth next year," and her plan defeats itself: keeping quiet now destroys the trust the paper would need for its later reporting to matter. A just repeats Ruth's own argument from Text 1, so it doesn't reflect Text 2's view. B only restates what happens in Text 2 (the publisher prints the story). It doesn't answer Ruth's "speak later" reasoning with the narrator's point about lost credibility, and Text 2 never presents printing the story as a duty. C brings in an issue Text 2 never discusses: depending too heavily on one advertiser.
g.design: The two texts never mention each other. To get the answer, students have to apply Text 2's idea that silence costs a paper its credibility to Ruth's plan to report later, which shows that her plan defeats itself. Each wrong answer is a different trap: one repeats Text 1, one repeats Text 2's outcome, and one brings in an issue Text 2 never raises.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 하나의 결론을 이끄는 주장을, 텍스트 2는 그 주장의 핵심 근거를 약하게 만들 수 있는 별개의 관찰이나 연구를 제시한다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자가 텍스트 1의 어느 부분에 가장 이의를 제기할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 1의 결론이 아니라 그 결론이 기대는 가정으로 하고, 오답 3개는 결론 자체, 텍스트 1의 부수적 세부, 텍스트 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분으로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A dental lab technician discovers her employer substitutes inferior crown materials while billing insurance companies and patients for premium specifications

g.passage:
Text 1
In Mara Okafor's novel The Bite Registration, dental lab technician Dolores Varga opens a tray of crowns labeled as solid zirconia, the costly material her employer bills insurers and patients for, and finds cheaper metal-based crowns instead. Okafor describes the grayish edge of each crown in close detail, and critic Hal Brennan notes that someone with Dolores's twenty years at the bench would know at a glance what she is holding. For Brennan, this is why the six weeks she then spends saying nothing make the novel a study in workplace cowardice: she sees the fraud plainly and chooses to look away.

Text 2
Critic Ines Albarrán points out that the chapter right before the tray scene has Dolores's employer announcing a "new supplier with a slightly different finish." The weeks that follow are not empty, either. Dolores starts a private notebook in which she records order numbers, weighs crowns on the lab scale, and compares them with invoices, crossing out guesses as she rules them out. Okafor, Albarrán argues, turns these weeks into a slow, uncertain investigation. Readers may still judge Dolores's final choices harshly, but the early silence belongs to someone who is not yet sure what she has found.
g.question: Based on the texts, which part of Brennan's reading in Text 1 would Albarrán in Text 2 most likely take issue with?
options: The idea that Dolores understands what the substituted crowns mean the moment she sees the tray
The idea that the novel as a whole should be read as a portrait of cowardice at work
The idea that the employer charges insurers and patients for zirconia crowns
The idea that Okafor pays close attention to the physical details of Dolores's work
g.explanation:
정답 A: Brennan의 '비겁함' 결론은 Dolores가 쟁반을 보는 순간 사기임을 알아차렸다는 가정("know at a glance", "sees the fraud plainly")에 기대고 있다. Albarrán은 '새 공급업체' 발표와 확인 작업을 기록한 노트를 근거로, 그 몇 주 동안 Dolores가 아직 확신하지 못했다고 보므로 바로 이 가정을 정면으로 겨냥한다.
B: 결론 자체를 고른 오답이다. Albarrán은 독자가 Dolores의 마지막 선택은 여전히 가혹하게 평가할 수 있다고 인정한다. 그녀가 무너뜨리는 것은 결론이 기대는 전제이지, 소설 전체에 대한 평가가 아니다.
C: 부수적인 세부를 고른 오답이다. 청구 방식은 두 비평가 모두 문제 삼지 않는 배경 설정이다.
D: Text 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분이다. Albarrán도 무게 측정, 송장 대조 같은 작업 묘사에 기대어 논지를 펼친다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. Brennan's claim that the novel is about cowardice depends on an assumption: that Dolores recognizes the fraud right away. He says she would "know at a glance" and that she "sees the fraud plainly." Albarrán challenges exactly this point. She cites the employer's "new supplier" announcement and Dolores's notebook of checks to show that Dolores is not yet sure what she has found.
Choice B is wrong because it names Brennan's conclusion, not the assumption under it. Albarrán even grants that readers may still judge Dolores's final choices harshly. Her target is the premise the conclusion rests on.
Choice C is wrong because the billing practice is background that neither critic disputes.
Choice D is wrong because Albarrán agrees with it. Her own argument relies on Okafor's detailed scenes of weighing crowns and comparing invoices.
g.design: Text 1은 '비겁함'이라는 결론을 '즉시 알아차렸다'는 숨은 가정 위에 세운다. Text 2는 결론에는 일부 여지를 남긴 채 그 가정만 무너뜨린다. 오답은 각각 결론, 부수적 세부, Text 2가 동의하는 부분으로 구성했고, 질문에는 정답의 핵심어(understands, moment)를 쓰지 않았다.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1의 저자가 좋은 설명이나 해결책의 기준(예: 재현 가능성, 단순성, 장기적 효과)을 분명히 드러내게 쓰고, 텍스트 2는 그 기준과 어긋날 수 있는 결론을 내리게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 1의 저자의 기준에서 텍스트 2의 결론을 어떻게 평가할 것인가'로 한다. 오답 3개는 텍스트 2 저자의 기준으로 평가한 결과, 두 저자의 기준을 섞은 평가, 일반 상식에 따른 평가로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A rural electric cooperative meter reader notices the utility company systematically misreads consumption for low-income households to inflate their bills

g.passage:
Text 1
Fiction about institutional wrongdoing often fails at the very moment it seems to succeed. When a novelist exposes a scheme and then hands the blame to a single scheming individual, readers close the book relieved, and that relief is the problem. The most honest stories of this kind show harm living inside ordinary procedures—forms, schedules, habits no one questions—so that removing one person changes nothing essential.

Text 2
In Lorna Achterberg's novel The Long Route, Della Voss reads electric meters for a rural cooperative and slowly realizes that the households on the poorest roads are billed for power they never used. The novel's finest stretch follows Della as she matches her handwritten logs against the printed bills until the trail leads to one office: that of billing supervisor Harlan Pruitt. His dismissal in the final chapter delivers a resolution as earned as it is satisfying, rewarding the reader's patience with justice.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the final chapter of The Long Route that is praised in Text 2?
options: As a strength, because Della's careful comparison of logs and bills makes the supervisor's eventual dismissal feel deserved rather than arbitrary
As a weakness, because tracing the overbilling to one man's office lets readers believe the cooperative's ordinary practices are sound once he is gone
As a weakness, because Della's slow investigation is convincing but the punishment given to Pruitt is too mild to count as real justice
As a weakness, because a meter reader would be unlikely to have access to the printed bills needed to uncover the scheme
g.explanation:
정답 B: Text 1 저자의 기준은 '부정이 일상적 절차 속에 있음을 보여 주어, 한 사람을 제거해도 본질이 바뀌지 않게 하는 것'이며, 한 개인에게 책임을 돌려 독자에게 안도감을 주는 결말을 실패로 본다. Text 2가 칭찬하는 Pruitt 해고 결말은 바로 그 유형이므로 Text 1 저자는 이를 약점으로 평가할 것이다.
A: Text 2 저자의 기준(차근차근 쌓아 얻은 만족스러운 정의)으로 평가한 것이다.
C: 조사 과정 칭찬과 '처벌이 약하다'는 불만을 섞은 것으로, Text 1은 처벌 수위가 아니라 한 개인에게 책임을 돌리는 것 자체를 문제 삼는다.
D: 현실성이라는 일반 상식적 기준으로, 두 지문 어디에도 근거가 없다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, B: The author of Text 1 judges this kind of fiction by one standard: it should show that the harm is built into ordinary procedures, so that removing one person changes nothing essential. Text 1 calls stories that pin the blame on a single individual a failure because they leave readers feeling relieved. The ending Text 2 praises, Pruitt's dismissal, does exactly that, so the author of Text 1 would see it as a weakness.
A judges the ending by Text 2's standard, a hard-earned and satisfying sense of justice. The author of Text 1 rejects that standard.
C combines praise for the investigation with a complaint that the punishment is too mild. Text 1 doesn't care how harsh the punishment is. Its objection is to blaming one person at all.
D judges the plot by whether it's realistic, which is a common-sense standard. Neither text supports it.
g.design: Text 1 states a criterion (expose systemic, procedural harm rather than a lone villain); Text 2 praises a lone-villain resolution. Distractors use Text 2's criterion (A), a blend that faults only the punishment (C), and a general plausibility criterion (D).

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A conservation biologist presents research showing a development project will destroy nesting habitat, only to have funders quietly cancel her grant before publication

g.passage:
Text 1
In a novel, conservation biologist Mara Elling shows a slide of plover nests mapped across the dunes where a marina will be built. Later, her funders cancel her grant before the study is published. The narrator says Mara's mistake was presenting too early: if she had kept her findings private until the paper appeared in print, the data would have been safe, and the cancellation could not have buried it.

Text 2
A critic writing about the same novel argues that the grant's cancellation shows how institutions shape knowledge long before anything is published. In the book, the funders control the boat access, the field permits, and the lab where Mara's samples are stored. The critic notes that a paper's arrival in print depends at every step on resources the funders could take away whenever they chose.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the narrator's claim in Text 1 about when Mara should have shared her findings?
options: By agreeing that sharing her findings early was what led the funders to cancel the grant before publication
By arguing that the cancellation proves institutions shape knowledge before anything is published
By objecting that holding back her findings would not have protected them, since the funders could still cut off what publication required
By claiming that Mara should have looked for other funders whose interests had nothing to do with the marina
g.explanation: 정답 C: Text 2에 따르면 출판까지 가는 모든 단계(배 접근, 허가, 시료 보관 연구실)가 후원자에게 달려 있다. 그러니 비공개로 버텼더라도 후원자는 출판에 필요한 자원을 끊을 수 있었고, 이 전제에서 Text 1의 '출판 때까지 숨겼으면 안전했다'는 주장은 성립하지 않는다는 반응이 나온다. A: Text 1의 인과 설명을 그대로 되풀이할 뿐, Text 2의 관점과는 반대다. B: Text 2의 결론을 다시 말할 뿐, 공개 시점에 관한 주장에는 답하지 않는다. D: 다른 후원자를 찾는 문제는 Text 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
g.explanation_en: Choice C is correct. Text 2 says that every step toward publication (boat access, permits, the lab storing the samples) depends on the funders, and they can take these away at any time. From that point, it follows that keeping the findings private would not have kept them safe, because the funders could still block publication. That undercuts the narrator's claim in Text 1. Choice A just repeats Text 1's explanation, which Text 2's view contradicts. Choice B restates Text 2's own conclusion but doesn't address the claim about when Mara should have shared her findings. Choice D brings in a different issue, finding other funders, which Text 2 never discusses.
g.design: Text 2 never brings up the narrator's timing claim. The rebuttal has to be worked out from its premise that funders control everything publication needs. The wrong answers each follow the assigned pattern: one repeats Text 1, one restates Text 2's conclusion, and one raises an outside issue.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 하나의 결론을 이끄는 주장을, 텍스트 2는 그 주장의 핵심 근거를 약하게 만들 수 있는 별개의 관찰이나 연구를 제시한다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자가 텍스트 1의 어느 부분에 가장 이의를 제기할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 1의 결론이 아니라 그 결론이 기대는 가정으로 하고, 오답 3개는 결론 자체, 텍스트 1의 부수적 세부, 텍스트 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분으로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A medical records clerk observes her supervisor altering patient medication dosages in official charts after treatment decisions have already been made

g.passage:
Text 1
In Marisol Achebe-Reyes's novel The Quiet Ward, records clerk Ines Okafor watches through the glass of a late-shift office as her supervisor, Mr. Halvorsen, rewrites medication dosages in charts for patients whose treatment has already been given. Ines files the charts without a word. Critic Dana Whitcomb argues that this silence is the novel's moral center: because Ines plainly grasps that the new figures are falsifications, her choice to stay silent makes her complicit. The book therefore indicts institutions that reward quiet compliance.

Text 2
Critic Rafael Moynihan points to a scene that readers often skip over. On Ines's first day, Halvorsen tells her that charts are routinely "reconciled" against pharmacy logs after the fact, and the narrator notes that Ines, hired from a shipping company, "could not have told a milligram from a microgram." When she later watches the charts being changed, Moynihan observes, the text gives no sign that she reads the changes as anything but the reconciliation she was told to expect. Her silence, he argues, is real, but it may not be a choice to look away.
g.question: Based on the texts, which part of Whitcomb's reading as described in Text 1 would Moynihan most likely dispute?
options: The claim that the novel ultimately indicts institutions that reward quiet compliance
The claim that the late-shift office setting separates Ines from the scene she watches
The claim that Ines files the altered charts without saying anything to anyone
The claim that Ines understands the revised figures to be falsifications
g.explanation:
정답 D: Whitcomb은 Ines가 수정된 수치를 조작으로 '분명히 알아차렸다'는 가정 위에서 침묵을 공모로 해석한다. Moynihan은 첫날 들은 '사후 대조' 설명과 Ines에게 약학 지식이 없다는 점을 근거로, Ines가 그 변경을 일상적인 대조 작업으로 보았을 수 있다고 지적한다. 그러므로 Moynihan이 직접 공격하는 것은 Ines가 상황을 이해했다는 이 전제다.
A: Whitcomb의 결론이다. Moynihan은 그 결론이 기대는 전제를 흔들 뿐, 소설이 제도를 비판하는지 여부는 다루지 않는다.
B: 장면 배경에 관한 부수적 세부다. Text 2는 이 점을 언급하지 않는다.
C: Moynihan도 "Her silence ... is real"이라며 동의하는 부분이다.
g.explanation_en:
D is correct. Whitcomb's reading rests on the assumption that Ines plainly understands the new figures to be falsifications. That is why she can call Ines's silence complicity. Moynihan cites the "reconciliation" explanation Ines heard on her first day and her lack of pharmacological knowledge. He argues that she may have taken the changes for routine corrections, which directly undermines this assumption.
A is wrong because it is Whitcomb's conclusion. Moynihan challenges what that conclusion depends on, not whether the novel criticizes institutions.
B is wrong because it is a minor detail about the setting, and Text 2 never mentions it.
C is wrong because Moynihan agrees with it: he says her silence "is real."
g.design: Text 2 adds evidence from an earlier scene that undercuts the assumption Text 1's conclusion depends on (that Ines recognizes the changes as fraud). The wrong answers are Text 1's conclusion, a minor setting detail, and a point Text 2 accepts. The question avoids the key words of the correct answer, and all four options use the same "The claim that…" structure.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Priya, a software tester, has found three serious security flaws in a banking app that is set to launch on Friday.

Priya's manager read her report and slid it back across the desk. "Hold this until after launch," he said. "Nobody outside this room needs to know yet." Priya returned to her cubicle. She opened the report again, checked every detail, and then saved a second copy, dated and signed, in a folder only she could access. Her decision to make that extra copy suggests that she ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: wants a record proving she found the flaws before the launch.
wants the flaws repaired before her manager reads the report.
wants her manager to see a neater version of the report.
wants the launch moved up so that the app reaches users sooner.
g.explanation: Priya의 상사는 출시 후까지 보고를 미루라고 지시했고, 그녀는 날짜와 서명을 넣은 사본을 자기만 접근할 수 있는 곳에 저장했다. 이는 자신이 결함을 일찍 발견했다는 증거를 남기려는 행동이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 틀렸다. 상사는 이미 보고서를 읽었다. C는 틀렸다. 사본은 상사에게 보여 주려는 것이 아니라 자신만 볼 수 있는 곳에 숨겨져 있다. D는 틀렸다. 출시를 앞당기고 싶어 한다는 단서는 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: Priya's manager tells her to hold the report until after launch, and she then saves a dated, signed copy in a folder only she can access. That is a way of keeping proof that she found the flaws early, so A is correct. B is wrong because the manager has already read the report. C is wrong because the copy is hidden where only Priya can see it, not prepared for her manager. D is wrong because nothing in the text suggests she wants the launch to happen sooner.
g.design: 이 문항은 한 단계 추론만 필요하다. 보고를 미루라는 지시를 받은 뒤 날짜와 서명을 넣은 비공개 사본을 저장한 행동에서 증거를 남기려는 의도를 읽어 내면 된다. 네 선택지는 모두 같은 'wants...' 문장 틀로 썼다.

g.passage: After the Sunday service, Marisol stayed behind to help count the coat-drive donations. While filing receipts, she noticed that every check written to the parish's community aid fund had been deposited not into the fund's account but into an account she didn't recognize, one listed under the treasurer's own name. The fund's balance sheet, which Mr. Hadley read aloud to the congregation each month, showed none of these deposits. Since the money given for families in need had been moved somewhere the congregation was never told about, Marisol concluded that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the treasurer had simply made an honest filing error that the bank would soon correct.
the treasurer had been keeping the aid money for himself while hiding it from the parish.
the congregation had stopped giving money to the community aid fund some months earlier.
the families in need had received more help than the balance sheet reported.
g.explanation: 지문은 기부금이 재무 담당자 본인 명의의 계좌로 입금되었고, 매달 신도들에게 읽어 주는 잔액표에는 그 입금이 빠져 있었다고 말한다. 따라서 그가 돈을 자기 몫으로 챙기면서 숨겼다는 B가 가장 논리적인 결론이다. A는 '단순한 실수'라고 하지만, 매번 그의 개인 계좌로 들어갔고 보고에서도 빠졌다는 사실과 맞지 않는다. C는 수표가 실제로 들어왔다는 내용과 모순된다. D는 돈이 가족들에게 가지 않고 다른 곳으로 옮겨졌다는 내용과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the donation checks went into an account in the treasurer's own name, and the balance sheet he read to the congregation left those deposits out. So the most logical conclusion is B: he was keeping the aid money for himself and hiding it. A calls it an honest error, but that doesn't fit with every check landing in his personal account and also being left off his reports. C contradicts the passage, since checks were still coming in. D is the opposite of what happened, because the money was moved away from the families instead of reaching them.
g.design: This is an easy, one-step inference. The clues (deposits going to his personal account and being left off his reports) point straight to the conclusion. Each wrong answer uses the same 'the X had...' sentence pattern and reflects a common misreading.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Marisol, a new aide at the Willow Bend care home, slowly notices a pattern in how the other staff members treat the residents.

A student claims that, in the story, Marisol comes to realize that the staff give careful attention mainly to residents who could later describe how they were treated, while residents with memory loss are quietly ignored.
g.question: Which quotation from the story, if true, would most directly support the student's claim?
options: "Mr. Alvarez, whose daughter visited every Sunday with flowers, had his sheets changed each morning; Mrs. Pike, whose family lived three states away, had hers changed only when someone remembered."
"Mrs. Chen, who laughed at every joke the aides told, was wheeled out to the garden after lunch; Mr. Ross, who complained about the food, was left by the window all afternoon."

"Mr. Okafor, who still wrote each aide's name in his notebook and read it back to the nurse, had his water refilled every hour; Mrs. Dunn, who no longer knew the day or the aides' faces, sat beside an empty cup until dinner."
"Mrs. Webb, whose room was next to the nurses' station, was checked on every few minutes; Mr. Hale, whose room was at the far end of the hall, was checked on only at the start of each shift."
g.explanation: 학생의 주장은 직원들이 자신이 받은 대우를 나중에 말할 수 있는 입주자만 잘 돌보고 기억을 잃은 입주자는 방치한다는 것이다. C는 직원 이름을 기록하고 간호사에게 읽어 주는 Mr. Okafor는 정성껏 돌보고, 날짜와 얼굴을 기억하지 못하는 Mrs. Dunn은 방치하는 모습을 보여 주므로 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 가족 방문 여부에 따른 차이라서 기억 능력과는 관계가 없다. B는 입주자의 성격이나 태도에 따른 차이이고, D는 방의 위치에 따른 차이이므로 둘 다 주장과 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The student claims that the staff carefully look after residents who could later report how they were treated, while they ignore residents with memory loss. C directly supports this: Mr. Okafor writes down the aides' names and reads them back to the nurse, and he gets constant care, while Mrs. Dunn can't remember the day or the aides' faces, and she is left with an empty cup. A shows a difference based on family visits, not on memory. B shows a difference based on a resident's personality, and D shows one based on where a room is, so neither one is about memory loss.
g.design: This is an easy item: the only thing you need to check is whether a quote contrasts residents by memory or ability to report. All four options use the same "resident X got care, resident Y was neglected" frame. The wrong answers point to other believable reasons for unequal care, so a student who doesn't hold each option up against the claim might pick one.

The following text is adapted from a short story. Marisol Ortega, a building inspector, is examining a new office building whose final certification review is scheduled for the next morning.

Marisol pointed her flashlight at the open panel. Three of the breakers were wired to cables far too thin for the load, a clear violation of the electrical code. Behind her, the contractor, Dale Whitcomb, cleared his throat. "The review board meets at nine," he said. "If your signature isn't on that form tonight, my crew loses a month of work." Marisol kept her eyes on the wires. Her pen stayed in her pocket. A student reading the story claims that Marisol is determined not to approve work she knows is unsafe, no matter how much Whitcomb pushes her.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's claim?
options: Later in the story, Marisol remembers that she had admired Whitcomb's buildings when she first started her career as an inspector.
Later in the story, Marisol notices that the building's lobby has been finished with expensive marble floors and tall glass windows.
Later in the story, Marisol tells Whitcomb that the review board has recently become stricter about deadlines for paperwork.
Later in the story, Marisol writes "FAILED: undersized wiring" on the form and hands it back to Whitcomb as he protests.
g.explanation: 학생의 주장은 마리솔이 압박에도 불구하고 안전하지 않은 작업을 승인하지 않으려 한다는 것이다. D는 휘트컴이 항의하는 중에도 불합격 판정을 적어 돌려주는 행동을 보여 주므로 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 휘트컴에 대한 과거의 존경일 뿐 승인 거부와 무관하다. B는 건물의 외관 묘사로 결정과 관련이 없다. C는 심사위원회의 마감 규정에 관한 것으로 안전하지 않은 작업을 거부한다는 점을 보여 주지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The student claims that Marisol refuses to approve unsafe work even under pressure. Choice D shows her marking the form as failed because of the wiring while Whitcomb protests, which directly supports that claim. Choice A only shows past admiration for Whitcomb, which says nothing about whether she will approve the work. Choice B describes the building's appearance, not her decision. Choice C concerns paperwork deadlines and does not show her refusing to approve unsafe work.
g.design: Easy: the one rule is to find the finding that shows the claimed behavior (refusing approval despite pressure); the distractors are details from the same story that have nothing to do with the claim.

g.passage:
Text 1
In this scene from a novel, freelance journalist Mara Quint reads her published profile of a local baker and finds a quote she never recorded: "Bread is my whole life." Her editor, Dev, shrugs it off. "It's what he would have said," Dev tells her. "Readers want a voice, and nobody gets hurt by a harmless line."

Text 2
Later in the same novel, Mara calls the baker to apologize. He is upset. "I never said that," he tells her. "My customers now think I care about nothing but the shop. My daughter asked why I said it. Words you put in a person's mouth do not stay small."
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the baker in Text 2 most likely respond to Dev's claim in Text 1 about the invented quote?
options: He would reject it, pointing out that the made-up line has changed how people close to him see him.
He would accept it, pointing out that the made-up line matches what he would probably have said anyway.
He would accept it, pointing out that the made-up line gave readers the lively voice they wanted.
He would reject it, pointing out that the made-up line was too dull to interest readers.
g.explanation: Text 1에서 Dev는 꾸며낸 인용문이 아무에게도 해가 없다고 주장한다. Text 2에서 제빵사는 손님들과 딸이 자신을 다르게 보게 되었다고 말하며 그 말이 "작게 남지 않는다"고 하므로, 해가 없다는 주장을 반박할 것이다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 제빵사가 "그런 말을 한 적 없다"며 화를 내므로 틀렸다. C는 Dev의 관점일 뿐 제빵사의 관점이 아니고, D는 제빵사가 문장이 지루하다고 불평한 적이 없으므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: In Text 1, Dev claims the invented quote is harmless. In Text 2, the baker says his customers and even his daughter now see him differently, and that such words "do not stay small," so he would reject the idea that no harm was done. That makes A correct. B is wrong because the baker is upset and insists he never said it. C reflects Dev's view, not the baker's, and D is wrong because the baker never complains that the line was dull.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도: 해가 없다는 주장과 실제 피해를 설명하는 진술을 직접 대비해 한 단계 추론으로 풀리게 했다. 오답 중 두 개는 Text 1의 관점을 반복하고, 하나는 근거 없는 이유를 대도록 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A school lunch coordinator learns her district deliberately reduced nutrition standards for schools serving predominantly low-income student populations

g.passage:
Text 1
In Marisol Reyes's short story "Second Helping," lunch coordinator Dana Pruitt finds a district memo showing that schools in low-income neighborhoods now receive cheaper meals with fewer vegetables. When she shows it to her principal, he shrugs and says the change probably makes no real difference to the children, since most of them would throw the vegetables away anyway.

Text 2
In a review of "Second Helping," critic Owen Hale writes that the story's quiet strength lies in its later scenes. Dana watches the same children grow tired and unfocused by early afternoon, and the nurse's office fills with students complaining of headaches. Hale argues that these details make clear the cut is hurting the students in visible ways.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Hale (Text 2) most likely respond to the principal's claim in Text 1?
options: He would agree with it, since the story shows that students rarely ate the vegetables they were served.
He would reject it, since the story shows the students suffering effects that can be seen after the change.
He would agree with it, since the story suggests that the nurse's visits were unrelated to the meals.
He would reject it, since the story shows that the memo was written by the principal himself.
g.explanation: 교장은 식단 변경이 아이들에게 실질적 차이가 없다고 주장한다. Text 2의 Hale은 아이들이 오후에 지치고 두통을 호소하는 장면이 식단 감축의 눈에 보이는 피해를 보여 준다고 말하므로 교장의 주장에 반대할 것이고, 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 학생들이 채소를 먹었는지는 다루지 않으며 Hale이 동의하지도 않으므로 틀리다. C는 Hale이 보건실 방문을 오히려 식단 감축과 연결하므로 틀리다. D는 메모를 교장이 썼다는 내용이 어느 글에도 없으므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The principal claims the meal change makes no real difference to the children. Hale points to scenes where students grow tired and visit the nurse with headaches, and he says these details show the cut is hurting them in visible ways, so he would reject the claim. That makes B correct. A is wrong because Text 2 doesn't discuss whether students ate the vegetables, and Hale doesn't agree with the principal. C is wrong because Hale actually links the nurse's visits to the cuts. D is wrong because neither text says the principal wrote the memo.
g.design: 이 문항은 '교장의 주장 vs Text 2의 눈에 보이는 피해'라는 하나의 명시적 대조만으로 풀리도록 만들었습니다. 오답은 같은 문장 틀(agree/reject + since)을 사용해 그럴듯해 보이도록 구성했습니다.

c.instruction: 지문에 두 변수 사이의 이론적 관계(예: A가 클수록 B도 커진다, 정직한 신호일수록 비용이 크다)를 제시하고, 이 이론을 새로운 구체적 집단이나 사례에 적용했을 때 나올 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 이론이 제시한 방향을 그대로 새 사례에 적용한 것이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 관계의 방향을 반대로 뒤집기, 원인과 결과를 바꾸기, 이론과 무관한 제3의 요인을 결론으로 제시하기의 실제 오개념을 사용해 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A restoration architect realizes her employer instructs workers to use cheap materials on historic buildings while invoicing clients for authentic period-appropriate restoration

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Mara, a restoration architect, is reviewing her firm's records.

Mara had learned one rule from her first mentor: a building always tells the truth eventually, and the more a repair departs from the original materials, the sooner the walls give it away. As she compared supply receipts with the invoices sent to clients, she saw what her employer had done. The Whitcombe Library, billed for hand-made lime mortar, had in fact been repointed with a mortar that was close to the original but slightly cheaper. The Aldous Chapel, billed for the same lime mortar and the same hand-carved oak, had received hard industrial cement and pressed particleboard. The two buildings were the same age, stood on the same street, and had been finished in the same month. If her mentor's rule held, Mara realized, ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the library would crack and stain before the chapel did, since its repairs had stayed closer to the original materials.
the chapel had been given the cheapest materials because it was the building most likely to fall apart first.
the chapel would show signs of the fraud well before the library did.
whichever building's owners had paid the larger invoice would be the first to see their walls fail.
g.explanation:
멘토의 원칙은 '수리가 원래 재료에서 멀어질수록 벽이 더 빨리 그 사실을 드러낸다'이다. 예배당은 원래 재료에서 크게 벗어났고(산업용 시멘트, 파티클보드), 도서관은 원래와 거의 비슷한 재료를 썼다. 두 건물은 나이, 위치, 완공 시기가 같아 다른 변수가 통제되어 있다. 따라서 예배당이 먼저 부정을 드러낸다(C).
A: 관계 방향을 뒤집었다. 원래 재료에 가까울수록 오히려 더 늦게 드러나야 한다.
B: 원인과 결과를 바꿨다. 원칙에서 재료가 원인이고 손상이 결과인데, B는 무너질 가능성이 높아서 싼 재료를 썼다고 거꾸로 말한다.
D: 청구 금액은 원칙과 무관한 제3의 요인이다. 게다가 두 건물은 같은 재료 기준으로 청구되었다.
g.explanation_en:
Here's the mentor's rule: the further a repair departs from the original materials, the sooner the walls reveal it. The chapel's repairs departed far from the original (industrial cement and particleboard), while the library's repairs stayed close to it. The two buildings are the same age, stand on the same street, and were finished in the same month, so nothing else explains a difference. That means the chapel should betray the fraud first, which is choice C.
A flips the direction of the rule. Staying closer to the original should delay damage, not speed it up.
B swaps cause and effect. In the rule, the choice of materials causes the decay. B claims instead that the chapel's expected decay caused the choice of materials.
D brings in a factor the rule never mentions, the invoice amount. Also, both buildings were billed for the same materials.
g.design: Mara applies her mentor's rule (bigger departure from original materials means faster visible decay) to two buildings where every other factor is held equal. The wrong answers reverse the direction, swap cause and effect, or bring in an unrelated factor (payment amount).

c.instruction: 짧은 표나 그래프 하나와 이를 설명하는 가설 문장 하나를 함께 제시하고, 두 정보를 결합해야만 답할 수 있는 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 시각 자료의 특정 수치와 가설 문장을 연결해야 나오고, 오답 3개는 각각 시각 자료만 보고 가설을 무시한 결론, 가설 문장만 보고 시각 자료를 무시한 결론, 시각 자료의 다른 항목을 잘못 짝지은 결론으로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A wildlife rehabilitation center director discovers donations designated for animal care are redirected toward executive salaries and administrative overhead costs

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Marisol directs a small wildlife rehabilitation center. Late one night, she opens the annual ledgers the board has never asked her to read.

Ledger summary (in thousands of dollars)
Year | Gifts designated for animal care | Spending on animal care | Executive salaries
2021 | 410 | 405 | 180
2022 | 520 | 390 | 240
2023 | 610 | 370 | 335

For months the board had told her that the empty medicine shelves and the owl enclosure left unrepaired were the price of a "lean period." Marisol turned that explanation over in her mind. A lean period, she reasoned, would cut the care budget only if the gifts meant for the animals had also shrunk; if those gifts grew while care spending fell, the missing money had not vanished but gone somewhere else. Running her finger across the page, she decided that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the figures for executive salaries, which nearly doubled over three years, proved on their own that the board's raises had been undeserved.
the figures for designated gifts must have been falling, since a lean period was the only thing that could explain the bare medicine shelves.
the figures for 2021, when designated gifts exceeded care spending, offered the clearest proof that money had been redirected.
the figures for 2023, when designated gifts climbed by 90 while care spending dropped by 20, exposed the "lean period" as a cover for diversion.
g.explanation:
정답 D: Marisol의 추론은 '지정 기부금이 늘었는데 돌봄 지출이 줄었다면 돈이 다른 곳으로 갔다'는 것이다. 2023년에 지정 기부금은 520→610으로 90 늘었고, 돌봄 지출은 390→370으로 20 줄었다. 바로 그녀의 기준에 들어맞으므로 '긴축기'라는 설명은 전용을 가리기 위한 핑계라는 결론이 나온다.
A(표만 보고 추론을 무시): 급여가 늘었다는 사실은 표에 있지만, Marisol의 판단 기준은 기부금과 돌봄 지출의 관계다. 또 '부당한 인상'은 그녀가 세운 논리에서 나오지 않는다.
B(추론만 보고 표를 무시): 이사회의 '긴축기' 설명을 받아들인 것이다. 하지만 표에서 지정 기부금은 해마다 늘었다.
C(다른 항목과 잘못 연결): 2021년에는 비교할 전년도 수치가 없어 '증가와 감소'를 확인할 수 없다. 기부금이 지출을 넘은 차이도 5에 불과하다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: Marisol's test is this: if gifts meant for the animals grew while care spending fell, the money must have gone somewhere else. In 2023, designated gifts went up by 90 (520 to 610), and care spending went down by 20 (390 to 370). That fits her test exactly, so the "lean period" story looks like a cover for diverting the money.
A takes the salary column by itself and ignores her reasoning. Her test compares gifts with care spending, and nothing in it supports calling the raises "undeserved."
B accepts the board's story and ignores the table, where designated gifts rose every year.
C points to the wrong row. 2021 has no earlier year to compare it with, so you can't see a rise in gifts alongside a drop in spending. The gap that year is also only 5.
g.design: 자료로 장부 표 하나를 주고, 주인공이 세운 조건부 추론을 함께 제시했다. 정답을 고르려면 2023년의 증가·감소 수치를 그 추론과 연결해야 한다. 오답은 각각 표만 본 결론(A), 추론만 본 결론(B), 다른 해를 잘못 짝지은 결론(C)으로 만들었다.

c.instruction: 하나의 결론이나 가설을 먼저 제시한 뒤, 그것을 뒷받침/약화/무관하게 만드는 추가 사실 하나를 골라야 하는 빈칸 문제를 만든다. 정답은 가설의 핵심 조건을 직접 충족하거나 위배하는 사실이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 표면적으로만 관련 있어 보이지만 실제로는 무관한 사실, 가설과 반대 방향으로 작용하는 사실을 지지 사실인 것처럼 제시한 것, 결론과 무관한 배경 정보를 결론 지지처럼 위장한 것으로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A shipping company warehouse manager observes supervisors systematically short-weighing shipments to cut shipping costs while charging customers full declared weight rates

g.passage: In the novel's third chapter, Ruth Okafor, night manager at the Harlow Freight warehouse, begins to suspect the floor supervisors. Customers are billed by the declared weight printed on each manifest, but the carrier Harlow pays to haul the crates charges by the weight logged on the warehouse's own scale. Ruth notices that on Tuesdays, when supervisor Dennis Prue runs the loading dock, the scale tickets for outgoing crates come in consistently lighter than the manifests, while customer invoices still list the full manifest figures. She reasons that if Prue is deliberately recording false weights to cut the company's hauling bill while customers keep paying full rates, then the gap should not be explainable by the scale itself. Her suspicion would therefore be strengthened most directly if she found that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the same crates, reweighed on the carrier's certified scale at the depot, matched their manifest weights rather than Prue's tickets.
the crates loaded on Tuesdays came mostly from customers who had used Harlow Freight for more than a decade.
the warehouse scale, when tested with standard weights, read about as low as Prue's tickets did on every shift.
the company's hauling bill had risen steadily over the past year as fuel surcharges increased.
g.explanation: Ruth의 가설의 핵심 조건은 '무게 차이가 저울 탓이 아니라 Prue가 일부러 낮게 기록한 결과'라는 것이다. A: 같은 화물을 독립적인 인증 저울로 다시 쟀더니 매니페스트 무게와 일치했다면, 실제 무게는 정상이고 Prue의 티켓만 낮다는 뜻이므로 조작 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다(정답). B: 화요일 고객이 오래된 고객이라는 사실은 표면적으로 관련 있어 보이지만 무게 기록이 정확한지와는 무관하다. C: 지지하는 사실처럼 보이지만, 저울이 모든 근무조에서 낮게 나온다면 차이가 저울 오류로 설명되므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. D: 운송비가 올랐다는 것은 비용 절감 동기의 배경처럼 보이지만, 화요일 티켓이 거짓인지는 전혀 보여주지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Ruth's hypothesis depends on one key condition: the gap comes from Prue deliberately recording false weights, not from the scale itself. A satisfies that condition directly. If an independent, certified scale shows that the same crates match their manifest weights, then the crates really weigh what the manifests say, and only Prue's tickets are low. That points to deliberate falsification, so A is correct. B sounds related because it involves Tuesday shipments, but how long customers have used the company says nothing about whether the weights were recorded accurately. C may look like support, but it actually pushes the other way. If the warehouse scale reads low on every shift, a faulty scale explains the gap, and that weakens the case against Prue. D is background that looks like a motive. A rising hauling bill does not show that Prue's tickets are false.
g.design: 가설(고의적 저울 기록 조작, 저울 결함 배제)을 먼저 제시하고, 핵심 조건을 직접 충족하는 독립 재계량 사실을 정답으로 했다. 오답은 각각 무관하지만 관련 있어 보이는 사실(B), 반대 방향인데 지지처럼 보이는 사실(C), 동기처럼 위장한 배경 정보(D)이며, 네 선택지 모두 같은 'the ... ' 명사절 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Ottoman janissary corps military recruitment and devshirme system of child conscription from Balkans

g.passage: Beginning in the late fourteenth century, Ottoman officials periodically conducted the devshirme, a levy in which boys, usually from Christian families in the Balkans, were taken from their villages, converted to Islam, and trained for state service. Most were sent to work on Anatolian farms to learn Turkish before entering the janissary corps, the sultan's elite infantry; a smaller group judged especially talented was educated in the palace and could rise to become provincial governors or even grand viziers. Historians have long described the system as a brutal uprooting, and many families did hide sons or arrange early marriages to avoid the levy. Yet records from some Bosnian communities show parents petitioning to have their boys included, apparently seeing the levy as a route to advancement otherwise closed to rural Christian subjects. Such evidence does not erase the coercion at the heart of the devshirme, but it suggests that responses to it varied more widely than the traditional account allows.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although the devshirme was intended to supply the janissary corps, most recruits were ultimately trained for high administrative posts in the palace.
Although the devshirme was a coercive levy, evidence suggests that Balkan families reacted to it in more varied ways than historians have usually assumed.
Although some families resisted the devshirme, records show that resistance largely disappeared once parents learned that recruits could become grand viziers.
Although historians have long condemned the devshirme, Bosnian records prove that the levy was in fact largely voluntary.
g.explanation: 지문은 데브쉬르메의 강제성을 인정하면서도, 일부 보스니아 공동체 기록을 근거로 가족들의 반응이 전통적 설명보다 다양했다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 궁정 교육이 '소수'에게만 해당했다는 서술과 반대된다. C는 저항이 사라졌다고 말하지만, 지문은 저항과 자원이 공존했음을 보여 줄 뿐이다. D는 기록이 강제성을 지우지 않는다는 마지막 문장과 모순되며 '대체로 자발적'이라는 주장은 과장이다.
g.explanation_en: The text acknowledges that the devshirme was coercive, but it uses records from some Bosnian communities to argue that families' responses varied more than the traditional account suggests. That makes B the answer. A is wrong because the text says only a smaller group was educated in the palace. C claims resistance disappeared, but the text shows that resistance and willing participation existed at the same time. D goes too far: the final sentence says the evidence does not erase the coercion, so the levy can't be called largely voluntary.
g.design: To find the main idea, students have to connect the concession about coercion with the new evidence about varied reactions. Each wrong choice uses a real detail from the text (palace careers, family resistance, Bosnian petitions) but distorts or exaggerates it. All four choices use the same "Although..." frame.

c.instruction:

c.seed: history and civics — Treaty of Tordesillas 1494 and Portuguese-Spanish division of colonial exploration territories

g.passage: In 1494, envoys of Spain and Portugal signed the Treaty of Tordesillas, which drew a north-south line roughly 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands and assigned newly encountered lands east of it to Portugal and those west of it to Spain. The agreement is often remembered as a bold carving-up of the globe, but its authors understood remarkably little of what they were dividing. No one in 1494 could reliably measure longitude at sea, so neither crown could say exactly where the line fell, and the treaty itself left the matter to a future joint expedition that never took place. Within a few years, Portuguese navigators reached the coast of what is now Brazil and argued it lay on their side; decades later, the two kingdoms quarreled over whether the Moluccas, the prized spice islands, fell within Portugal's or Spain's sphere once the line was extended around the far side of the world. Thus a treaty meant to settle rivalry instead supplied the vocabulary in which new rivalries were argued.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Treaty of Tordesillas succeeded in preventing conflict between Spain and Portugal because it relied on a precise north-south line that both crowns accepted.
The Treaty of Tordesillas mattered mainly because it gave Portugal a legal claim to Brazil, which became the most valuable of its overseas territories.
The Treaty of Tordesillas, though intended to resolve competing claims, was so imprecise in practice that it became a framework for further disputes between Spain and Portugal.
The Treaty of Tordesillas was abandoned soon after it was signed because Spain and Portugal refused to send the joint expedition needed to measure longitude.
g.explanation: 지문은 조약이 경쟁을 끝내려 했지만 경도 측정이 불가능해 경계선 위치가 불분명했고, 그 결과 브라질과 몰루카 제도를 둘러싼 새 분쟁의 틀이 되었다고 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '정확한 선'이라는 표현으로 지문의 핵심(부정확성)과 정반대이다. B는 브라질이라는 세부 사례 하나만 다루고, 브라질이 가장 가치 있는 영토였다는 내용도 지문에 없다. D는 공동 탐사가 실현되지 않았다는 세부 사실은 맞지만, 지문은 조약이 폐기됐다고 하지 않으며 오히려 수십 년 뒤에도 분쟁의 기준으로 쓰였다고 설명한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the treaty was meant to settle rivalry, but because no one could measure longitude, the line's location stayed uncertain, and it ended up framing new disputes over Brazil and the Moluccas. That makes C correct. A says the line was "precise," which contradicts the text's central point about how imprecise it was. B focuses on a single example, Brazil, and adds a claim about its value that the text never makes. D is built on a true detail (the joint expedition never happened), but the text doesn't say the treaty was abandoned; in fact, it was still being used to argue claims decades later.
g.design: This applies the medium standard because you have to connect the stated purpose of the treaty with its later outcomes. B and D each rest on a real detail from the passage, so they only fall apart when you compare them with the overall idea.

c.seed: history and civics — Salem witch trials 1692 and mass hysteria driven by ergot fungal contamination hypothesis

g.passage: In 1976, psychologist Linnda Caporael proposed that the accusations at Salem in 1692 might have stemmed from ergot, a fungus that infects rye and can cause convulsions and hallucinations when contaminated grain is eaten. The idea drew wide public attention, in part because it offered a tidy physical cause for a notoriously puzzling episode. Yet historians Nicholas Spanos and Jack Gottlieb soon raised objections. Ergot poisoning typically strikes whole households, including infants, who are especially vulnerable, but the afflicted in Salem were mostly adolescent girls and young women, while their family members who shared the same bread showed no symptoms. Moreover, the accusers' fits often began and ended on cue in the courtroom, appearing when a suspect entered and subsiding once that person was condemned. For these critics, such patterns pointed less to a contaminated food supply than to social pressures operating within the community.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although ergot can cause convulsions and hallucinations, it rarely contaminated rye grown in colonial New England.
Although the ergot hypothesis gained public attention, historians later showed that adolescent girls were especially vulnerable to ergot poisoning.
Although Caporael's proposal was popular, Spanos and Gottlieb argued that the Salem accusers deliberately invented their symptoms to settle family disputes.
Although the ergot explanation was appealing, features of the Salem afflictions fit poorly with how the poisoning usually affects people.
g.design: 정답은 지문의 두 반박 근거(가족 단위 발병 불일치, 법정에서의 발작 타이밍)를 종합해야 도출되며, 오답은 각각 지문 세부를 왜곡·과장한 같은 'Although' 틀로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 지문은 맥각균 가설이 관심을 끌었지만, Salem 피해자들의 증상 양상(주로 젊은 여성에게만 나타남, 법정에서 발작이 시작되고 멈춤)이 실제 중독 양상과 맞지 않는다는 비판을 소개하므로 정답은 D이다. A는 지문이 언급하지 않은 사실, 즉 뉴잉글랜드 호밀의 오염 빈도를 주장한다. B는 지문과 반대이다. 지문에서 특히 취약하다고 한 대상은 영아이며, 청소년 소녀가 주로 증상을 보였다는 점은 오히려 가설에 대한 반론이다. C는 비판자들이 언급한 '사회적 압력'을 '의도적 조작'과 '가족 분쟁'으로 과장하고 있어 지문의 근거를 넘어선다.
g.explanation_en: The text introduces the ergot hypothesis and then focuses on critics who point out that the Salem symptoms didn't match how ergot poisoning normally works: mostly young women were affected, not whole households, and the fits started and stopped in the courtroom. That makes D correct. A claims something the text never discusses, namely how often rye in New England was contaminated. B reverses the text: infants are the group described as especially vulnerable, and the fact that adolescent girls were the main victims counts against the hypothesis. C goes too far. The critics pointed to "social pressures," not to deliberate fakery or family disputes.

c.seed: history and civics — Haitian Revolution 1791-1804 and Toussaint Louverture's military strategy defeating French forces

g.passage: Historians once attributed the French defeat in Saint-Domingue largely to yellow fever, which killed thousands of soldiers sent by Napoleon in 1802. Recent scholarship, however, emphasizes that the disease's impact was shaped by revolutionary strategy. Toussaint Louverture and his officers understood that newly arrived European troops had no immunity to tropical illnesses, so during the spring campaign they avoided decisive battles, burned coastal towns, and withdrew into the mountainous interior. This approach forced French columns to remain in the lowlands during the rainy season, when mosquito-borne fever spread fastest, while the revolutionary forces preserved their own strength. By the time Jean-Jacques Dessalines led the final offensive in 1803, the French army had been so weakened that it could no longer hold the colony.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Revolutionary leaders deliberately prolonged the conflict in ways that made illness far more damaging to French forces than it otherwise might have been.
Yellow fever killed so many French soldiers in 1802 that the revolutionary forces had little need to fight major battles.
Revolutionary leaders burned coastal towns mainly to deny French troops the supplies needed to march into the mountains.
Dessalines's offensive in 1803, rather than earlier campaigns, was the decisive factor in ending French control of the colony.
g.explanation: 지문은 황열병만으로 프랑스 패배를 설명하던 기존 견해를 수정하며, 투생 루베르튀르 측이 결전을 피하고 내륙으로 후퇴해 프랑스군을 우기 저지대에 묶어 두는 전략으로 질병의 피해를 키웠다고 주장하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문이 반박하는 옛 견해, 즉 질병만이 원인이라는 관점을 반복한다. C는 지문에 나온 도시 방화를 언급하지만 보급 차단이라는 목적은 지문에 없고, 이는 전체 요지가 아닌 세부 사항이다. D는 1803년 공세를 언급하지만, 지문은 그 공세가 앞선 전략으로 이미 약해진 군대를 상대로 성공했다고 설명한다.
g.explanation_en: A is correct because the text revises the older view that yellow fever alone defeated the French: it argues that Louverture's strategy of avoiding battle and retreating inland kept French troops in the lowlands during the rainy season, which magnified the disease's toll. B restates the older view that the text pushes back against, treating disease as the only cause. C mentions the burning of towns, but the text never says the goal was to cut off supplies, and this detail isn't the main point anyway. D refers to the 1803 offensive, but the text says it succeeded because earlier strategy had already weakened the French army.
g.design: 오답들이 지문의 실제 세부(황열병 사망, 도시 방화, 1803년 공세)를 활용해, 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯하지만 '전략이 질병의 효과를 키웠다'는 연결을 파악해야 A를 고를 수 있게 했다.
