c.seed: history and civics — Meiji Restoration 1868 and Japan's rapid industrialization through government-directed modernization policy

g.passage: After the Meiji Restoration of 1868, Japan's new leaders sought to close the industrial gap with Western powers as quickly as possible. Because private investors at the time had little capital and less experience with modern machinery, the government itself built model factories, such as the Tomioka silk mill, and staffed them with hired foreign engineers. Many historians once treated these enterprises as proof that state ownership drove Japan's growth. Yet most of the model factories lost money, and in the 1880s the government sold many of them to private firms at low prices. Historian Thomas C. Smith argued that the factories' real contribution was not their output but the trained workers, technical knowledge, and proven methods they passed on to the private companies that later expanded Japanese industry.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Japan's early model factories succeeded mainly because the foreign engineers who staffed them produced goods more efficiently than private firms could.
Japan's early model factories mattered less for what they produced than for the skills and methods they handed on to later private industry.
Japan's early model factories were sold in the 1880s because private investors had finally gathered enough capital to run them profitably.
Japan's early model factories show that state ownership, rather than private enterprise, was the main force behind the country's industrial growth.
g.explanation: 지문은 정부 모범 공장이 대부분 손실을 냈지만, Smith에 따르면 진짜 기여는 생산량이 아니라 민간 기업에 전수된 숙련 노동자·기술·방법이었다는 점을 핵심으로 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 외국인 기술자 언급을 활용했지만, 공장이 효율적으로 성공했다는 주장은 손실을 냈다는 진술과 모순된다. C는 1880년대 매각이라는 세부를 쓰지만, 매각 이유를 민간 자본 축적으로 설명하는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 과거 역사가들의 견해일 뿐, 지문은 'Yet' 이후 이 견해에 반박한다.
g.explanation_en: The text's key point is that most of the government's model factories lost money. According to Smith, their real value was the trained workers, technical knowledge, and methods they passed on to private firms, not their output. That makes B correct. A uses the detail about foreign engineers, but saying the factories succeeded through efficiency contradicts the fact that most of them lost money. C uses the detail about the 1880s sales, but the text never says the factories were sold because private investors had gathered enough capital. D repeats the view historians "once" held, and the text pushes back on that view starting with "Yet."
g.design: Distractors reuse true details (foreign engineers, 1880s sale, earlier historians' view), so readers must follow the "Yet" contrast and the reasoning that follows it to identify Smith's claim.

c.seed: history and civics — Serfdom abolition in Russia 1861 and emancipation edict's economic consequences for peasant society

g.passage: When Tsar Alexander II issued the Emancipation Manifesto in 1861, roughly twenty-three million privately owned serfs gained personal freedom: they could marry, own property, and bring cases to court without a landlord's permission. The economic terms of the reform, however, were far less generous. Land was not handed to former serfs outright; instead, peasants received allotments that were often smaller than the plots they had farmed before, and they were required to pay for them through "redemption payments" stretched over forty-nine years. Because these payments were frequently set above the land's market value, many households fell into chronic debt. Moreover, the allotments were usually assigned to the village commune, or mir, rather than to individual families, so peasants could not easily sell their share or leave to seek work elsewhere. Historians therefore argue that although the edict ended the legal bondage of serfdom, it left much of the peasantry tied to the land by financial obligation and communal control for decades afterward.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The 1861 reform granted former serfs new legal rights, which allowed most peasant households to leave their villages and find better-paying work.
The 1861 reform transferred land to the village commune, which historians regard as the main reason peasants gained personal freedom.
The 1861 reform freed serfs in law, but its land and payment terms kept many peasants economically constrained long after.
The 1861 reform set redemption payments below market value, but peasants resented them because the payments lasted for forty-nine years.
g.explanation: 지문은 1861년 칙령이 법적 자유(결혼, 재산 소유, 소송)를 주었다고 인정한 뒤 '그러나' 토지 분배·상환금·공동체 소유 조건 때문에 농민이 수십 년간 경제적으로 묶여 있었다고 결론짓는다. C는 이 두 측면을 모두 담는다. A는 법적 권리 부여는 맞지만, 농민이 떠나기 어려웠다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. B는 토지가 공동체(mir)에 배정되었다는 세부는 맞지만, 그것이 개인 자유의 원인이라는 인과는 근거가 없고 오히려 제약 요인이었다. D는 49년이라는 기간은 맞지만, 상환금은 시장가치보다 '높게' 책정된 경우가 많았다고 지문은 말한다.
g.explanation_en: The text grants that the 1861 edict gave serfs legal freedoms (marriage, property, court access), then turns with "however" to show how the land allotments, redemption payments, and communal control kept peasants bound for decades. C captures both halves of that argument. A is right about the new legal rights, but the text says peasants could not easily leave their villages, so it contradicts the passage. B correctly notes that land went to the commune, but the text presents this as a restriction, not as the source of personal freedom. D gets the forty-nine-year term right, but the text says payments were often set above market value, not below it.
g.design: 정답은 양보(법적 자유)+반전(경제적 속박)을 종합해야 하며, 오답 A·B·D는 각각 지문의 실제 세부(권리, mir, 49년)를 포함하되 결론이나 수치 방향을 왜곡해 비교가 필요하게 했다.

c.seed: history and civics — Berlin Conference 1884-1885 and European partition of Africa establishing colonial territorial claims

g.passage: The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885 is often described as the meeting where European powers carved up Africa with rulers and maps. Historians such as Matthew Craven argue that this image overstates what the delegates actually did. The conference's General Act drew few borders; instead, it set out procedural rules, most notably the principle that a power claiming African coastline had to notify the other signatories and demonstrate "effective occupation" through some administrative presence. These rules did not divide the continent on their own, but they changed how claims were made: by rewarding visible control, they encouraged rival states to rush agents, treaties, and garrisons into the interior over the following two decades. In this view, the partition of Africa was less a single act performed in Berlin than a competitive process that the conference set in motion.
g.question: According to the text, what is Craven's view of the Berlin Conference's role in the partition of Africa?
options: The conference divided Africa among European powers directly, and the treaties signed afterward simply confirmed borders the delegates had already drawn.
The conference had little effect on the partition, since European states had already established firm control over most of the African interior before 1884.
The conference mainly addressed disputes over coastal territory, and its rules were largely ignored once European powers moved into the interior.
The conference shaped the partition chiefly by establishing rules for making claims, which in turn spurred a later scramble for control of territory.
g.explanation: 지문은 회의가 국경을 직접 긋기보다 '통보'와 '실효적 점유' 같은 절차 규칙을 정했고, 이 규칙이 이후 내륙 쟁탈 경쟁을 촉발했다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 지문이 반박하는 통념(지도로 대륙을 나눴다는 이미지)을 그대로 진술한다. B는 회의의 영향이 작았다고 하지만, 지문은 회의가 경쟁 과정을 '작동시켰다'고 하며 1884년 이전 내륙 장악도 언급하지 않는다. C는 해안선 관련 규칙이라는 부분적 근거를 쓰지만, 그 규칙이 무시되었다는 것은 지문과 반대이다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the conference drew few borders and instead set procedural rules (notification and "effective occupation"), and that these rules encouraged rivals to rush into the interior afterward, so D is correct. A restates the popular image that the text says Craven rejects. B claims the conference had little effect, but the text says it set the partition process in motion, and it never says Europeans already controlled the interior before 1884. C picks up the real detail about coastline claims, but the text says the rules drove the later scramble, which is the opposite of being ignored.
g.design: 두 단계로 판단해야 한다. 먼저 회의가 국경이 아니라 규칙을 정했다는 점을 확인하고, 이어서 그 규칙이 이후의 쟁탈전을 일으켰다는 점과 연결해야 한다. A는 지문이 반박하는 통념을 담았고, C는 해안선이라는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 쓴 오답이다. B는 그럴듯하지만 지문과 맞지 않는다.

c.seed: history and civics — Mexican Land Reform 1910-1940 and ejido communal farming system redistributing hacienda properties

g.passage: The Mexican Constitution of 1917 authorized the government to break up large haciendas and grant the land to rural communities as ejidos, holdings that villagers could farm but could not sell. For nearly two decades, however, redistribution proceeded slowly; presidents in the 1920s transferred land mainly to quiet unrest in particular regions, and many hacendados kept their best fields through legal delays. Under President Lázaro Cárdenas (1934–1940), the pace changed dramatically: his administration distributed roughly 18 million hectares, more than all of his predecessors combined, including productive commercial estates such as the cotton plantations of La Laguna. Historians note that this expansion did not by itself make ejidos prosperous. Many recipients received land without adequate credit, irrigation, or machinery, and the national ejido bank lacked the funds to supply them, so yields on numerous ejidos lagged behind those of remaining private farms.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although land redistribution through ejidos accelerated sharply under Cárdenas after years of slow progress, the transfer of land alone did not ensure that ejido farming would succeed.
Although the 1917 Constitution called for ejidos, hacienda owners succeeded in preventing any meaningful redistribution of productive land before 1940.
Although Cárdenas distributed more land than earlier presidents, he did so mainly to calm unrest in particular regions rather than to transform rural landholding.
Although ejidos often lacked credit and equipment, their yields soon surpassed those of private farms once the national ejido bank was established.
g.explanation: 지문은 1920년대의 느린 재분배와 카르데나스 시기의 급격한 확대를 대비한 뒤, 토지만 나눠준 것으로는 에히도가 번영하지 못했다고 결론짓는다. 이 두 흐름을 모두 담은 것은 A이다. B는 지주들의 지연 전술을 언급하지만, 카르데나스가 라 라구나 같은 생산적인 농장까지 분배했다는 내용과 모순된다. C는 지역 불안 진정이라는 동기를 1920년대 대통령들에서 카르데나스에게 잘못 옮겨 붙였다. D는 지문과 반대로 말한다. 에히도 은행은 자금이 부족했고, 많은 에히도의 수확량은 사유 농장보다 뒤처졌다.
g.explanation_en: The text sets slow redistribution in the 1920s against the dramatic expansion under Cárdenas, then concludes that handing out land alone didn't make ejidos prosper. Choice A is the only option that captures both parts. Choice B builds on the detail about legal delays, but it contradicts the passage, which says Cárdenas redistributed productive estates such as La Laguna. Choice C takes the motive of calming regional unrest, which the text gives for the 1920s presidents, and wrongly applies it to Cárdenas. Choice D reverses the text: the ejido bank didn't have enough funds, and yields on many ejidos lagged behind those of private farms.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 대비 구조(느린 진행 → 급격한 확대)와 단서 조항(토지만으로는 부족)을 연결해야 한다. 오답 B와 C는 지문의 실제 세부 내용을 다른 시기나 주체에 잘못 붙여 만들었고, D는 전체 논지를 뒤집었다. 네 선택지 모두 같은 'Although' 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.seed: history and civics — Taiping Rebellion 1850-1864 and Christian millenarianism destabilizing Qing Dynasty rural China

g.passage: Historians once described the Taiping Rebellion (1850–1864) chiefly as a peasant uprising sparked by famine and heavy taxation in southern China. Hong Xiuquan, the movement's leader, did draw followers from impoverished villages, but recent scholarship emphasizes that economic hardship alone cannot explain why the revolt grew so large or fought so relentlessly. Hong, after reading Christian missionary tracts, came to believe he was the younger brother of Jesus, sent to destroy the Qing "demons" and establish a Heavenly Kingdom on earth. This millenarian promise gave converts a reason to abandon their land, pool their property in common treasuries, and accept strict codes of conduct. Because followers saw the war as the prelude to a divinely ordained new age, compromise with Qing authorities seemed not merely unwise but sinful, and the conflict became one of the deadliest of the nineteenth century, devastating rural communities across the Yangzi valley.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Taiping Rebellion grew out of famine and heavy taxation, which drove impoverished villagers in southern China to join Hong Xiuquan's movement.
The Taiping Rebellion's scale and intensity owed much to Hong Xiuquan's religious vision, which led followers to treat the conflict as a sacred struggle rather than a negotiable dispute.
The Taiping Rebellion's practice of pooling property in common treasuries shows that the movement was primarily an effort to redistribute land in rural China.
The Taiping Rebellion's destruction of rural communities in the Yangzi valley led historians to reject earlier accounts of its origins.
g.explanation: 지문은 기존의 경제적 설명을 소개한 뒤, 그것만으로는 반란의 규모와 집요함을 설명할 수 없고 홍수전의 천년왕국적 기독교 신앙이 타협을 죄악으로 여기게 만들었다는 점을 강조하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 지문이 한계를 지적하는 옛 해석만 진술한다. C는 공동 재산이라는 세부를 토지 재분배라는 주된 목적으로 과장하는데, 지문은 이를 종교적 약속의 결과로 제시한다. D는 지문에 나온 파괴를 학설 변화의 원인으로 잘못 연결하며, 지문은 그런 인과관계를 말하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text first presents the older economic explanation and then argues that hardship alone cannot account for the revolt's size and relentlessness, pointing instead to Hong's millenarian Christian vision, which made compromise seem sinful. That makes B the answer. A restates only the older view that the text says is incomplete. C takes the detail about common treasuries and inflates it into a land-redistribution goal, but the text presents pooling property as a result of religious belief. D links the devastation to historians changing their view, a cause-and-effect connection the text never makes.
g.design: 오답 A·C는 지문에 실제로 있는 세부(경제적 고난, 공동 재산)를 근거로 삼아서 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯하게 보인다. 정답 B는 '경제만으로는 부족하다'는 대조와 '타협이 죄악'이라는 결론을 함께 연결해야 고를 수 있다.

c.seed: history and civics — Indian partition 1947 and Radcliffe Line's arbitrary borders creating communal violence aftermath

g.passage: In the summer of 1947, British lawyer Cyril Radcliffe was given roughly five weeks to draw the borders dividing British India into India and Pakistan. He had never visited the subcontinent before, worked largely from outdated maps and census figures, and consulted few people with local knowledge. Historians have often focused on these constraints to explain why his lines cut through villages, farmland, and irrigation canals. Yet a number of recent scholars argue that the haste of the drawing explains less about the violence that followed than the decision of how to announce it. Although Radcliffe finished his work before independence on August 15, the final boundaries were withheld until two days afterward. During that gap, millions of people in Punjab and Bengal did not know which country they would live in, and rumors filled the silence. These scholars contend that this uncertainty, more than any particular flaw in where the line ran, allowed local militias to organize and helped turn fear into mass killing and flight.
g.question: According to the text, what do some recent scholars regard as the more important factor behind the violence that accompanied partition?
options: Radcliffe's reliance on outdated maps and census data, which led him to place the border through villages and canals
The short period Radcliffe was given to complete his work, which prevented him from consulting people with local knowledge
The delay in making the boundaries public, which left residents of divided regions unsure of their future nationality
The activity of local militias in Punjab and Bengal, which began organizing well before Radcliffe started drawing the line
g.explanation: 지문은 최근 학자들이 선을 서둘러 그린 것보다 경계 발표를 독립 이틀 뒤로 미룬 결정, 그리고 그로 인한 불확실성을 더 중요한 요인으로 본다고 설명하므로 정답은 C이다. A와 B는 지문에 나오는 사실이지만, 기존 역사가들이 강조해 온 제약일 뿐이며 최근 학자들은 이것이 덜 중요하다고 본다. D의 민병대는 불확실성의 결과로 조직된 것으로 제시되며, Radcliffe의 작업 이전부터 조직되었다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text says recent scholars think the decision to hold back the final boundaries until two days after independence mattered more than the haste of the drawing, because it left people uncertain about their country, so C is correct. A and B describe real details from the passage, but they are the constraints earlier historians emphasized, and the recent scholars treat them as less important. D gets the sequence backward: the text presents militia organizing as a result of the uncertainty, and it never says militias formed before Radcliffe started drawing the line.
g.design: Two distractors restate true details from the text (the constraints historians emphasized), so a quick reader picks them. To get the answer, the student has to connect the scholars' contrast ("less... than") with the announcement gap. D misplaces cause and timing.

c.seed: history and civics — Cuban Missile Crisis October 1962 and Soviet nuclear deployment brinkmanship with United States

g.passage: Popular accounts of the Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 often portray it as a contest of nerves won by the side that refused to blink: the United States imposed a naval "quarantine" around Cuba, and the Soviet Union, facing the threat of escalation, withdrew its nuclear missiles from the island. Historians working with declassified records from both governments have complicated this picture. They note that the settlement included terms kept from the public at the time, most notably a private American assurance that Jupiter missiles stationed in Turkey would be removed within months. Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev and President John F. Kennedy, these documents show, also exchanged letters through intermediaries in which each sought a way for the other to retreat without appearing defeated. In this view, the crisis ended less because one leader outlasted the other than because both quietly accepted concessions that allowed each to claim success.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Declassified records show that the US naval quarantine around Cuba was the main factor that forced the Soviet Union to remove its missiles from the island.
Declassified records show that the removal of US missiles from Turkey was a more significant outcome of the crisis than the removal of Soviet missiles from Cuba.
Declassified records show that Khrushchev and Kennedy relied on intermediaries because neither leader trusted the other to keep the terms of an agreement.
Declassified records show that the crisis was resolved through hidden mutual compromise rather than through one side's simple capitulation.
g.explanation: 지문은 '한쪽이 버텨서 이겼다'는 통념을 소개한 뒤, 기밀 해제 문서를 근거로 비공개 양보(터키 미사일 철거)와 서로 체면을 살려 주는 서신 교환이 있었음을 들어 위기가 양측의 조용한 타협으로 끝났다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 지문이 비판하는 통념 그 자체이다. B는 터키 미사일이라는 세부를 다루지만 두 철수 중 어느 쪽이 더 중요했는지 비교하는 내용은 지문에 없다. C는 중재자라는 세부를 언급하지만, 지문은 그 목적을 불신이 아니라 서로 물러설 길을 찾아 주려는 것으로 설명한다.
g.explanation_en: The text first presents the popular idea that one side won by refusing to back down. It then uses declassified records about a secret concession (the Jupiter missiles in Turkey) and face-saving letters to conclude that both sides quietly compromised, so D is correct. A just repeats the popular view that the text goes on to challenge. B picks up the Turkey detail, but the text never says that withdrawal mattered more than the one from Cuba. C mentions the intermediaries, but the text says the letters were meant to let each leader retreat with dignity, not that the leaders distrusted each other.
g.design: Every option uses the same "Declassified records show that..." frame. B and C each build on a real detail from the text but distort it, and A restates the popular view that the text argues against, so a student has to read the whole argument to rule them out.

c.seed: history and civics — Triangular trade system and Atlantic slave trade routes connecting Africa Europe Americas

g.passage: The phrase "triangular trade" is often used to describe Atlantic commerce from the sixteenth to the nineteenth centuries: European manufactured goods shipped to West Africa, enslaved Africans carried across the Atlantic to the Americas, and sugar, tobacco, and cotton returned to Europe. The image is tidy, and it does capture how profits in one region depended on labor and markets in the others. Historians such as David Eltis, however, have argued that the triangle misrepresents how most voyages actually operated. Shipping records show that many vessels did not complete all three legs; ships that delivered captives to the Caribbean frequently sailed home with little cargo, while plantation goods crossed the ocean on separate, specialized ships. Moreover, a large share of the trade to Brazil ran directly between Brazilian and African ports, with tobacco and rum from Bahia exchanged for captives in Angola and the Bight of Benin, bypassing Europe entirely. For these historians, the system is better understood as a web of overlapping routes than as a single closed loop.
g.question: Based on the text, what do historians like David Eltis conclude about Atlantic commerce during this period?
options: The familiar three-legged model oversimplifies a network in which many voyages followed other paths, including direct exchanges between South America and Africa.
The familiar three-legged model is accurate because profits in each region depended on labor and markets in the other regions.
The familiar three-legged model applied mainly to Brazil, where ships regularly carried goods among Europe, Africa, and the Americas.
The familiar three-legged model fails because plantation goods such as sugar and tobacco were rarely shipped to European markets.
g.explanation: A가 정답이다. Eltis 등은 많은 선박이 세 구간을 모두 운항하지 않았고 브라질-아프리카 직거래가 유럽을 거치지 않았다는 근거로 무역을 '겹치는 경로의 망'으로 보아야 한다고 결론짓는다. B는 지문이 삼각 모델의 장점으로 인정한 부분이지만, 역사가들은 그것 때문에 모델이 정확하다고 하지 않는다. C는 브라질을 언급하지만, 지문에서 브라질 무역은 유럽을 우회한 예로서 삼각 모델의 반례이다. D는 플랜테이션 상품이 별도의 선박으로 유럽에 갔다는 내용을 '거의 운송되지 않았다'로 왜곡한다.
g.explanation_en: A is correct. Eltis and others point out that many ships didn't complete all three legs and that the Brazil–Africa trade skipped Europe entirely, so they conclude the system was a web of routes rather than a single loop. B repeats a strength the passage grants the triangle image, but the historians don't use it to call the model accurate. C mentions Brazil, but the passage uses Brazil as a counterexample, since that trade bypassed Europe. D distorts the passage: plantation goods did reach Europe, just on separate, specialized ships.
g.design: A가 정답이 되려면 반론의 두 근거를 결론과 연결해야 한다. B와 C는 지문 속 사실을 일부 가져와 오답의 미끼로 쓰고, D는 세부 내용을 그럴듯하게 왜곡했다.

c.seed: history and civics — Dreyfus Affair 1894-1906 and French military antisemitism challenging republican justice system

g.passage: In 1894, Captain Alfred Dreyfus, a Jewish artillery officer, was convicted of passing military secrets to Germany and sent to Devil's Island. The evidence against him was thin, and when an intelligence officer, Georges Picquart, later identified another officer, Ferdinand Esterhazy, as the likely culprit, army leaders moved Picquart to a distant post rather than reopen the case. Esterhazy was tried and quickly acquitted in 1898. Many historians have described these events mainly as evidence of antisemitism within the French officer corps, and that prejudice clearly shaped how readily Dreyfus was suspected. Historian Ruth Harris, however, argues that the affair's lasting importance lies elsewhere. In her account, the military's refusal to admit error became a test of whether institutions of the young Third Republic, such as its courts, its press, and its elected officials, could force a powerful body to answer to the law. When Dreyfus was finally cleared in 1906, Harris contends, the outcome mattered less as a personal vindication than as proof that republican justice could prevail over the army's claim to judge itself.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Harris argues that antisemitism in the French officer corps was the main reason Dreyfus was wrongly convicted, a cause that earlier historians had overlooked.
Harris argues that the affair mattered most because it tested whether the Republic's civilian institutions could hold the army accountable to the law.
Harris argues that the affair mattered most because Picquart's discovery of Esterhazy's guilt showed that the army was able to correct its own mistakes.
Harris argues that Dreyfus's clearing in 1906 mattered most as a personal vindication that ended years of suffering on Devil's Island.
g.design: 이 문항은 통념(반유대주의)과 Harris의 반론(공화국 제도가 군을 법 아래 둘 수 있는지 시험한 사건)을 대비시켰다. 그래서 글 전체의 초점이 반론 쪽으로 옮겨 간다는 것을 알아야 정답을 고를 수 있다. 오답은 세부 사실을 하나씩 비틀어 만들었다.
g.explanation: 지문은 많은 역사가가 이 사건을 반유대주의의 증거로 본다고 소개한 뒤, Harris가 그 의의를 다른 곳에서 찾는다고 말합니다. Harris에게 이 사건은 법원·언론·선출직 같은 공화국 제도가 군을 법 앞에 세울 수 있는지를 시험한 일이었습니다. 따라서 정답은 B입니다. A는 반유대주의를 Harris의 핵심 주장으로 잘못 돌렸고, 지문에서는 그것이 다른 역사가들의 견해입니다. C는 지문과 반대입니다. 군은 Picquart를 좌천시키고 Esterhazy를 무죄로 풀어 주며 스스로 바로잡기를 거부했습니다. D는 Harris가 개인적 명예 회복보다 더 중요한 것이 있다고 본 바로 그 해석입니다.
g.explanation_en: The passage first says that many historians treat the affair as evidence of antisemitism. It then says Harris finds the affair's lasting importance somewhere else. For her, the affair tested whether the Republic's courts, press, and elected officials could make the army answer to the law, so B is correct. A is wrong because it credits Harris with the antisemitism view, which the passage gives to other historians. C gets the story backward: the army reassigned Picquart and let Esterhazy be acquitted, so it refused to correct itself. D is wrong because Harris says the 1906 outcome mattered less as a personal vindication than as a victory for republican justice.

c.seed: history and civics — Boxer Rebellion 1899-1901 and Chinese xenophobic uprising against foreign missionary presence

g.passage: Accounts of the Boxer Rebellion (1899–1901) often present it as a simple outburst of hatred toward foreigners. Historian Joseph Esherick, however, traced the movement's origins to the drought-stricken villages of northwestern Shandong province. There, Christian converts sometimes relied on the legal protection of foreign missionaries to win local land and lawsuit disputes. Unemployed young men, idled by failed harvests, blamed both the drought and their worsening circumstances on these converts and their foreign patrons. Esherick argues that the Boxers' hostility toward outsiders, though real, grew out of specific local grievances rather than a long-standing, nationwide rejection of everything foreign.
g.question: According to the text, what does Esherick conclude about the Boxers' anti-foreign attitudes?
options: They were mostly invented by later writers, since the Boxers actually focused on drought relief rather than on foreigners.
They spread from Shandong to the rest of China because missionaries had won land disputes in villages across the country.
They came out of particular conflicts and hardships in Shandong villages rather than from a general hostility shared across China.
They began among Christian converts, who turned against their missionary protectors after the harvests failed.
g.explanation: 지문 마지막 문장에서 Esherick은 Boxer의 적대감이 실제로 있었지만 전국적이고 오래된 외국 거부가 아니라 구체적인 지역 불만에서 생겨났다고 주장하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 가뭄이라는 소재를 쓰지만, 지문은 적대감이 "real"이라고 했으므로 지어낸 것이라는 주장은 틀렸다. B는 Shandong과 토지 분쟁을 언급하지만, 전국으로 퍼졌다거나 전국 마을에서 분쟁이 있었다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 개종자와 흉작을 연결하지만, 적대감을 품은 쪽은 개종자가 아니라 실업 청년들이었다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct because the last sentence says Esherick believes the Boxers' hostility, though real, came from specific local grievances in Shandong rather than from a long-standing, nationwide rejection of foreigners. A uses the drought detail, but the text calls the hostility "real," so the idea that it was invented is wrong. B mentions Shandong and land disputes, but the text never says the attitudes spread nationwide or that such disputes happened all over the country. D links the converts to the failed harvests, but the hostile group was unemployed young men, not the converts themselves.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect the details about local grievances with the contrast in the last sentence. The wrong answers reuse real details from the text (drought, land disputes, converts) but distort how they relate.

c.seed: history and civics — Parliament Act 1911 and British constitutional crisis limiting House of Lords legislative veto power

g.passage: In 1909 the House of Lords, dominated by hereditary Conservative peers, rejected the "People's Budget," a Liberal finance bill that proposed new taxes on land and high incomes. By long-standing custom, the Lords did not block money bills passed by the elected House of Commons, so the rejection provoked a constitutional crisis. After two general elections in 1910 and a promise from King George V to create enough new Liberal peers to overcome resistance if necessary, the Lords reluctantly passed the Parliament Act 1911. The act did not abolish the upper chamber or change its membership. Instead, it removed the Lords' power to reject money bills altogether and replaced its absolute veto over other legislation with a power merely to delay such bills for up to two years. Historians often note that the act's significance lay less in what it immediately changed than in the principle it fixed in law: when the two chambers disagree, the will of the elected house ultimately prevails.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Parliament Act 1911 reshaped the House of Lords by ending hereditary membership and making the upper chamber answerable to voters.
The Parliament Act 1911 was passed mainly because King George V favored Liberal tax policies and pressured the Lords to accept the People's Budget.
The Parliament Act 1911 is considered important chiefly because it gave the Lords a formal two-year delaying power they had previously lacked.
The Parliament Act 1911, prompted by the Lords' defeat of a budget, legally established that the elected chamber's decisions would win out over the unelected chamber's objections.
g.explanation: 지문은 예산 거부로 촉발된 위기 끝에 1911년 의회법이 통과되었고, 그 핵심 의의는 양원이 충돌할 때 선출된 하원의 의지가 결국 우선한다는 원칙을 법으로 확립한 데 있다고 말한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 지문이 상원의 폐지나 구성 변경은 없었다고 명시하므로 틀리다. B는 국왕의 약속이라는 세부 사항을 언급하지만, 국왕이 자유당 조세 정책을 지지했다거나 그것이 주된 원인이었다는 내용은 지문에 없다. C는 2년 지연권을 언급하지만, 이는 기존의 절대적 거부권을 약화한 것이며 역사가들은 그 의의가 원칙 확립에 있다고 본다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that a crisis over the Lords' rejection of a budget led to the Parliament Act 1911. It then says the act mattered most because it fixed in law the principle that the elected house prevails when the two chambers disagree, so D is correct. A is wrong because the text says the act did not abolish the Lords or change its membership. B mentions the king's promise, but the text never says he favored Liberal tax policies or that this was the main reason the act passed. C is about the two-year delay, but that delay was a reduced version of the Lords' old absolute veto, not a new power, and historians locate the act's importance in the principle it set.
g.design: In B and C, the incorrect choices reuse real details (the king's promise and the two-year delay) but misread them, so test takers must compare each one with the passage's closing claim about why the act mattered. All choices follow the same "The Parliament Act 1911..." sentence frame.

c.seed: history and civics — Bolshevik Revolution October 1917 and Lenin's seizure of Russian imperial state apparatus

g.passage: Popular images of October 1917 often show crowds storming the Winter Palace, as if the Bolsheviks won power in one dramatic assault. Historians such as Alexander Rabinowitch have drawn attention to a quieter process that came before that night. Over the preceding weeks, the Military Revolutionary Committee of the Petrograd Soviet sent commissars to the city's garrison units, and those units came to accept that orders from the Provisional Government were invalid unless the committee had approved them. Telegraph offices, railway stations, and bridges then changed hands mostly without fighting, because the soldiers guarding them had already switched loyalties. By the time the palace was taken, the government inside had little machinery left to command. Lenin's seizure of the old imperial state, on this account, depended less on defeating it in battle than on emptying it out from within.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Bolshevik takeover succeeded mainly because the Provisional Government's means of command had already been drawn away from it before the famous assault took place.
The Bolshevik takeover succeeded mainly because the attack on the Winter Palace was planned so carefully that the government's defenders could not resist it.
The Bolshevik takeover succeeded mainly because Lenin personally persuaded the soldiers of the Petrograd garrison to ignore the Provisional Government.
The Bolshevik takeover succeeded mainly because seizing telegraph offices and railway stations allowed the Bolsheviks to win the fighting in the streets of Petrograd.
g.explanation: 지문은 겨울궁전 습격이라는 극적인 이미지와 달리, 그보다 앞서 군사혁명위원회가 수비대의 충성을 옮겨 놓아 정부의 지휘 기구가 안에서부터 비워졌다고 주장하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문이 깎아내리는 궁전 습격을 오히려 핵심 원인으로 삼는다. C는 수비대의 충성이 바뀌었다는 내용은 맞지만, 그 일을 한 것은 위원회의 커미사르들이지 레닌 개인의 설득이 아니다. D는 거점들이 장악되었다는 세부는 맞지만, 지문은 그 장악이 대부분 전투 없이 이루어졌다고 말하므로 시가전에서 이겼다는 설명과 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: Choice A is correct. The text sets the dramatic storming of the Winter Palace against an earlier, quieter process: the Military Revolutionary Committee shifted the garrison's loyalty, so the government's power was emptied out from within before the palace fell. Choice B treats the palace assault as the key cause, which is exactly the view the text pushes back on. Choice C gets the garrison's change of loyalty right, but the text credits the committee's commissars with this, not Lenin's personal persuasion. Choice D correctly mentions the takeover of key sites, but the text says these changed hands mostly without fighting, so the idea of winning street battles doesn't fit.
g.design: Two wrong answers reuse true details from the text (the garrison's shift in loyalty, the captured key sites) but attach them to the wrong cause. A third wrong answer repeats the popular view that the text argues against. To get the answer, students have to link the "quieter process" to the final "emptying it out" claim.

c.seed: history and civics — Hundred Days Offensive 1918 and final German military collapse ending World War One

g.passage: Popular accounts of the end of World War One often credit Germany's surrender in November 1918 to a collapse on the home front, where food shortages and naval mutinies were said to have undermined an army that remained unbeaten in the field. Military historians who have examined the final months of fighting describe a different sequence. Beginning near Amiens in August 1918, Allied forces launched a series of coordinated attacks, later called the Hundred Days Offensive, that combined tanks, aircraft, and carefully timed artillery with infantry advances. Over the following weeks, German units lost ground steadily, and hundreds of thousands of soldiers surrendered or deserted. By late September, General Erich Ludendorff himself was urging the government to seek an armistice, weeks before the unrest in German ports and cities reached its peak.
g.question: According to the text, what do military historians conclude about the reasons Germany ended the war?
options: Germany sought an armistice mainly because naval mutinies and food shortages at home had already weakened its army's ability to keep fighting.
Germany sought an armistice mainly because its army was being defeated on the battlefield before domestic unrest became most severe.
Germany sought an armistice mainly because Ludendorff hoped that pausing the fighting would let his forces recover from the losses near Amiens.
Germany sought an armistice mainly because Allied tanks and aircraft had made traditional infantry tactics obsolete for both sides.
g.explanation: 지문은 패배 원인을 국내 붕괴로 보는 대중적 설명을 소개한 뒤, 군사사학자들은 8월부터 이어진 전장 패배를 원인으로 보며 루덴도르프의 휴전 요청이 국내 소요가 절정에 이르기 몇 주 전이었다고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 지문이 반박하는 대중적 설명을 그대로 옮긴 것이다. C는 루덴도르프와 아미앵을 언급하지만, 휴전을 전력 회복을 위한 시간 벌기로 보았다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 지문에 나온 전술 요소를 쓰고 있으나, 보병 전술이 쓸모없어졌다는 주장은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct. The text first presents the popular view that Germany lost because of a home-front collapse. It then explains that military historians point to battlefield defeats starting in August, noting that Ludendorff asked for an armistice weeks before domestic unrest peaked. A simply restates the popular view that the text argues against. C mentions Ludendorff and Amiens, but the text never says he wanted an armistice to buy time for his forces to recover. D uses tactical details from the text, but the text never claims that infantry tactics became obsolete.
g.design: 오답들이 지문의 실제 단어(mutinies, Ludendorff, Amiens, tanks)를 재활용하고 정답과 같은 문장 틀을 쓰게 해서, 대중적 견해와 학자들의 견해를 구별하고 시간 순서까지 연결해야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다.

c.seed: history and civics — Armenian genocide 1915 and Ottoman deportation policy resulting in mass civilian deaths

g.passage: Historians reconstructing the Armenian genocide of 1915 have often relied on the testimony of survivors and foreign diplomats, sources that Ottoman officials at the time dismissed as exaggerated or hostile. In recent decades, however, researchers such as Taner Akçam have turned to the Ottoman state's own records, including coded telegrams exchanged between the Interior Ministry and provincial governors. These documents show officials tracking the number of Armenians deported from each district and ordering that the deportees' share of the population in their destination regions be kept below a fixed percentage. __Such instructions are difficult to reconcile with the government's wartime claim that the deportations were merely a temporary security measure to move civilians away from the front lines.__ Instead, the records suggest a deliberate demographic policy, one whose execution through forced marches into the Syrian desert led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of civilians.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces the official justification for the deportations that the testimony of survivors and diplomats was used to confirm.
It explains why the Ottoman Interior Ministry chose to communicate with provincial governors through coded telegrams.
It indicates how the evidence just described undermines an account that the Ottoman government had offered for its actions.
It concedes that the Ottoman records are too limited to support firm conclusions about the government's intentions.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞에서 소개한 오스만 정부 문서(인구 비율 제한 지시)가 '일시적 안보 조치'라는 정부의 공식 주장과 맞지 않음을 지적하여, 이어지는 '의도적 인구 정책' 결론으로 연결한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 공식 주장을 언급한다는 점은 맞지만, 생존자 증언이 그 주장을 확인했다는 내용은 지문과 반대다. B는 암호 전보가 언급되긴 하지만 밑줄 문장은 암호 사용 이유를 설명하지 않는다. D는 오히려 문서가 결론을 강하게 뒷받침하므로 한계를 인정한다는 설명은 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence points out that the Ottoman records just described, which ordered deportees to be kept below a fixed share of the population, clash with the government's official claim that the deportations were a temporary security measure. That sets up the conclusion that the policy was deliberate, so C is correct. A does mention the official justification, but the passage never says survivor testimony confirmed it. In fact, Ottoman officials dismissed that testimony. B picks up on the coded telegrams, but the sentence doesn't explain why the ministry used codes. D gets the role backwards: the records strengthen the conclusion about intent instead of limiting it.
g.design: To get this right, you have to link the documentary evidence to the official claim it contradicts. Wrong answers A and B reuse real details from the passage (the official justification, the coded telegrams) but describe the sentence's role incorrectly.

c.seed: history and civics — Khmer Rouge regime 1975-1979 and Cambodian political re-education through agrarian collectivization

g.passage: After seizing Phnom Penh in April 1975, the Khmer Rouge forced millions of city dwellers into rural cooperatives, where they were assigned to dig canals and plant rice under quotas set by distant party officials. Leaders presented this upheaval as a form of political education: by laboring in the fields alongside peasants, so-called "new people" from the cities would supposedly shed the habits of a corrupt urban society. __Yet surviving cooperative records show that officials routinely reported harvests far larger than those actually gathered, while the rice that did exist was often shipped away rather than given to the laborers who grew it.__ For historians such as Ben Kiernan, such evidence suggests that the regime's promise of renewal through farm work hid a system that left many of its supposed students starving.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Khmer Rouge leaders chose rice farming instead of other kinds of labor for the people they relocated from cities.
It describes the methods historians have used to estimate how many people the Khmer Rouge moved into rural cooperatives.
It gives an example of how former city residents gradually adopted the outlook of the peasants they worked beside.
It presents documentary evidence that undercuts the regime's portrayal of agricultural labor as a path to reform.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 앞 문장에서 정권이 농업 노동을 정치 교육으로 내세웠다는 내용과 대비된다. 이어서 협동조합 기록(문서 증거)을 통해 수확 허위 보고와 쌀 반출을 보여 주며, 마지막 문장은 이 증거가 '재생'이라는 약속 뒤에 굶주림을 낳는 체제가 있었음을 시사한다고 정리한다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 쌀농사가 지문에 나오기는 하지만, 그것을 선택한 이유는 설명되지 않는다. B는 역사가와 기록이 등장한다는 점은 맞지만, 이주자 수를 추정하는 방법은 다루지 않는다. C는 정권이 주장한 내용일 뿐이며, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 그 주장을 반박한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence opens with "Yet," which sets it against the previous sentence, where the regime presents farm labor as political education. The sentence then uses cooperative records, a form of documentary evidence, to show that harvests were inflated and rice was shipped away. The final sentence confirms that this evidence reveals starvation behind the promise of renewal, so D is correct. A is wrong because rice farming does appear in the text, but nothing explains why it was chosen. B is wrong because historians and records are mentioned, but the text never discusses how anyone counted the people who were relocated. C is wrong because it repeats the regime's own claim, and the underlined sentence actually undermines that claim.
g.design: B와 C는 지문 속 요소(기록·역사가, 농민과 함께하는 노동)를 활용해 일부 근거가 있지만, 'Yet'이 만드는 대조와 마지막 문장의 결론을 함께 확인해야 배제된다. 정답 D는 지문의 표현을 바꿔 쓴 것이고, 네 선택지는 모두 같은 'It + 동사' 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Fall of Berlin Wall November 1989 and peaceful dissolution of communist East German state

g.passage: Popular accounts of November 9, 1989, often credit a single blunder for the opening of the Berlin Wall: at a televised press conference, East German official Günter Schabowski mistakenly announced that new travel rules took effect "immediately," and crowds rushed to the border crossings that night. __Yet the guards at Bornholmer Strasse who finally lifted the barrier did so only after months of mass demonstrations in Leipzig and other cities had already eroded the regime's willingness to use force against its own citizens.__ Historians such as Mary Elise Sarotte therefore argue that Schabowski's error merely set the timing of an event whose underlying causes had been building for a long time, and that the peaceful collapse of the East German state reflected pressure from ordinary people more than any single official's slip.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces circumstances that complicate a widely held explanation, preparing for the historians' alternative interpretation.
It provides evidence that confirms the widely held explanation of why the border crossings opened that night.
It describes the immediate reaction of the crowds to the announcement, illustrating how quickly events unfolded.
It presents the historians' central conclusion about the relative importance of ordinary citizens and officials.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 샤보프스키의 실수만을 원인으로 보는 통념에 몇 달간의 시위라는 배경을 덧붙여 그 설명을 복잡하게 만들고, 다음 문장의 역사가들의 대안적 해석(therefore)으로 이어지므로 A가 정답이다. B는 문장이 통념을 확인하는 것이 아니라 제한하므로 틀리다. C는 국경 검문소 장면이 나오긴 하지만 문장의 핵심은 군중 반응이 아니라 장기적 원인이다. D는 결론이 실제로는 마지막 문장에 제시되며, 밑줄 문장은 그 근거를 준비하는 역할이므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and adds the background of months of protests, which complicates the popular view that Schabowski's mistake alone opened the Wall. It then sets up the historians' alternative reading, introduced by "therefore," so A is correct. B is wrong because the sentence limits the popular explanation instead of confirming it. C is wrong because, although the border crossing appears in the sentence, its focus is on long-term causes, not the crowds' reaction. D is wrong because the historians' conclusion actually appears in the final sentence; the underlined sentence lays the groundwork for it.
g.design: 'Yet' 대조와 다음 문장 'therefore'를 연결해야 기능을 파악할 수 있게 했다. D(결론 자체로 오인)와 C(장면 묘사로 오인)는 부분적으로 그럴듯해 보이게 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Nuremberg Trials 1945-1946 and prosecuting Nazi war crimes establishing international law precedent

g.passage: When the International Military Tribunal convened in Nuremberg in November 1945, defense lawyers for the accused Nazi leaders raised a pointed objection: many of the charges, especially "crimes against peace," had not been clearly defined as crimes under international law when the acts were committed. Punishing defendants for them, the lawyers argued, amounted to applying law retroactively. __The tribunal answered that treaties such as the 1928 Kellogg-Briand Pact, which Germany had signed, had already renounced aggressive war, so the defendants could not claim they had acted without notice that such conduct was unlawful.__ Historians still debate whether this reasoning fully settled the matter, but its influence is clear: the principles the tribunal applied were affirmed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1946 and later shaped the statutes of courts such as the International Criminal Court.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a criticism of the tribunal that historians later used to challenge its legitimacy.
It explains how the tribunal responded to a legal challenge described in the previous sentences.
It describes a treaty that the defense lawyers cited to show the charges were applied retroactively.
It identifies the main reason the United Nations later affirmed the tribunal's principles.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장들에서 변호인단이 제기한 소급 적용 반론에 대해 재판소가 켈로그-브리앙 조약을 근거로 내놓은 답변이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 이 문장을 재판소에 대한 비판으로 보지만, 실제로는 재판소 측의 논리이고 역사가들의 논쟁은 그다음 문장에 나온다. C는 조약이 언급된다는 점은 맞지만, 그 조약을 인용한 것은 변호인이 아니라 재판소이며 소급 적용 반론을 반박하는 데 쓰였다. D는 마지막 문장의 UN 승인과 연결 짓지만, 지문은 밑줄 문장의 논리를 UN이 승인한 이유로 제시하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence gives the tribunal's reply to the defense's objection about retroactive law, which appears in the sentences before it, so B is correct. A treats the sentence as a criticism of the tribunal, but it is actually the tribunal's own reasoning, and the historians' debate only comes up in the next sentence. C is right that a treaty is mentioned, but it was the tribunal, not the defense, that cited it, and it was used to counter the retroactivity claim. D ties the sentence to the UN's affirmation in the last sentence, but the text never says this reasoning is why the UN affirmed the principles.
g.design: 이 문항은 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 먼저 밑줄 문장이 누구의 입장인지(재판소) 파악하고, 이어서 앞 문장에 나온 반론과 연결해야 한다. 오답 C와 D는 지문에 실제로 나오는 요소(조약, UN)를 잘못된 주체나 잘못된 인과에 붙여 부분적으로만 맞게 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Stonewall uprising June 1969 and LGBT resistance to police raids launching modern queer activism

g.passage: Police raids on gay bars were routine in 1960s New York, and patrons usually complied, lining up to show identification and dispersing quietly to avoid arrest or public exposure. When officers raided the Stonewall Inn in Greenwich Village in the early hours of June 28, 1969, however, the crowd that gathered outside refused to scatter. __Instead, patrons and neighbors pushed back against the officers, and the confrontation grew into several nights of protest in the surrounding streets.__ Historians note that earlier acts of resistance, such as a 1966 "sip-in" at a nearby bar, had already challenged discriminatory practices. Yet Stonewall's scale and visibility gave activists a rallying point: within a year, new groups such as the Gay Liberation Front had formed, and the first anniversary was marked by marches that became the model for later Pride events.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why police in 1960s New York began raiding gay bars more frequently than they had in earlier years.
It presents the 1966 sip-in as the event that first broke the pattern of patrons quietly complying with raids.
It shows how the response to the Stonewall raid departed from the usual pattern described earlier, setting up the later discussion of its consequences.
It shows that historians disagree about whether the Stonewall confrontation lasted several nights or only a single evening.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞에서 말한 '순순히 따르고 흩어지는' 관행과 달리 Stonewall에서는 사람들이 맞서 며칠간 시위가 이어졌음을 보여 주며, 이것이 뒤에 나오는 단체 결성과 Pride 행진이라는 결과로 이어지므로 C가 정답이다. A는 단속이 일상적이었다는 배경을 다루지만, 밑줄 문장은 단속이 늘어난 이유를 설명하지 않는다. B는 밑줄 문장이 아니라 뒤 문장에 나오는 1966년 sip-in을 끌어온 것이고, 밑줄 문장은 Stonewall에 관한 내용이다. D는 '며칠 밤'이라는 세부를 쓰지만, 지문에는 그 기간을 두고 역사가들이 의견이 갈린다는 내용이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence contrasts the crowd's resistance at Stonewall with the usual practice of complying and dispersing described earlier. That resistance then leads into the later discussion of new groups and Pride marches, so C is correct. A draws on the background that raids were routine, but the sentence never explains why raids became more frequent. B takes the 1966 sip-in from the following sentence, while the underlined sentence is about Stonewall. D reuses the detail about several nights, but the text never says historians disagree about how long the protests lasted.
g.design: To answer, students must link the sentence to both the earlier pattern of compliance and the later consequences. The wrong answers reuse nearby details (routine raids, the sip-in, several nights) to pull in students who skim.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Prague Spring 1968 and Czechoslovak democratic reform crushed by Soviet military intervention

g.passage: In January 1968, Alexander Dubček became leader of Czechoslovakia's Communist Party and soon announced a program he called "socialism with a human face." Press censorship was relaxed, citizens openly debated the party's past abuses, and reformers drafted plans to allow greater economic independence for enterprises. Many historians have described these months, later known as the Prague Spring, as an attempt to abandon communism altogether. __Yet the party's own Action Program of April 1968 explicitly reaffirmed Czechoslovakia's membership in the Warsaw Pact and the Communist Party's leading role in society.__ Soviet leaders nonetheless viewed the reforms as a threat to their control of Eastern Europe, and in August 1968 Warsaw Pact troops invaded the country, ending the experiment within a single night.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that explains why Soviet leaders decided that a military invasion of Czechoslovakia was necessary.
It presents a detail illustrating how far the reforms of the Prague Spring extended beyond the relaxation of press censorship.
It presents a claim that historians have used to argue that the reformers intended to leave the Warsaw Pact.
It presents information that complicates a characterization of the reformers' goals described in the previous sentence.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 앞 문장에서 소개한 '프라하의 봄은 공산주의를 완전히 버리려는 시도였다'는 역사가들의 해석과 달리 개혁 강령이 바르샤바 조약과 공산당의 지도적 역할을 재확인했음을 보여 준다. 따라서 그 해석을 복잡하게 만드는 D가 정답이다. A는 소련의 침공을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 개혁이 체제에 충실했음을 보여 주며 침공 이유는 다음 문장에서 따로 제시된다. B는 개혁의 범위를 다루지만, 밑줄 문장은 개혁이 넓어졌음이 아니라 그 한계를 보여 준다. C는 바르샤바 조약을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장의 내용은 조약 탈퇴 의도와 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet," which signals a contrast with the previous sentence, where historians describe the Prague Spring as an attempt to abandon communism. By showing that the Action Program reaffirmed Warsaw Pact membership and the party's leading role, it complicates that characterization, so D is correct. A mentions the invasion, but the underlined sentence actually shows the reformers staying loyal to the system; the Soviet reasoning comes in the next sentence. B is about the reach of the reforms, but the sentence shows their limits, not how far they went. C mentions the Warsaw Pact, but the sentence suggests the opposite of an intent to leave it.
g.design: 'Yet'으로 시작하는 대조 구조를 파악하고 앞 문장의 해석과 연결해야 풀 수 있다. 오답들은 지문 속 실제 요소(침공, 개혁, 바르샤바 조약)를 이용해 부분적으로 그럴듯하게 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Magna Carta 1215 and English baronial constraints on royal authority through written charter

g.passage: In June 1215, rebellious English barons compelled King John to accept a written charter later known as Magna Carta. Many popular accounts celebrate the document as an early guarantee of liberty for all English people. Historian Ralph Turner and others, however, emphasize that most of its clauses addressed narrow baronial grievances, such as the fees the king could demand when an heir inherited land. __Yet even these self-interested provisions mattered beyond their immediate purpose, because by setting them down in writing, the barons established that the king's demands could be measured against a fixed text rather than left to his discretion.__ That principle, more than any single clause, is why later generations could invoke the charter against monarchs whom its authors never imagined.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It qualifies the historians' point by identifying a broader significance in the very clauses they characterize as narrow.
It rejects the historians' point by showing that the charter's clauses were written to protect all English people.
It supports the popular accounts by showing that the barons intended the charter to serve future generations.
It illustrates the historians' point by giving an example of a fee the king could demand from an heir.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 역사가들이 '좁은 귀족적 불만'이라 본 조항들을 인정하면서도, 그것을 문서로 고정했다는 점에서 더 넓은 의의가 있다고 덧붙이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 '역사가 주장을 부정'한다고 하지만 밑줄 문장은 조항이 자기이익적(self-interested)임을 인정하므로 틀리다. C는 넓은 의의를 언급한 점은 맞지만, 마지막 문장이 작성자들이 후대를 상상하지 못했다고 밝히므로 '의도'라는 부분이 틀리다. D는 상속 수수료 예시가 앞 문장에 이미 나왔고, 밑줄 문장은 예시가 아니라 의의를 제시한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet," accepting the historians' view that the clauses were self-interested while adding that writing them down gave them a wider significance, so A is correct. B is wrong because the sentence concedes the provisions were self-interested rather than denying the historians' point. C notices the broader significance but wrongly claims the barons intended it; the final sentence says the authors never imagined later uses. D is wrong because the inheritance-fee example appears in the previous sentence, and the underlined sentence offers an interpretation, not an example.
g.design: Two-step reading: recognize the "Yet" concession to the historians and then confirm with the final sentence that the significance was unintended. B and C each partially fit (contrast, broader significance) but fail on detail.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Gutenberg printing press invention circa 1440 and mass production of books democratizing knowledge

g.passage: Historians often credit Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type press, developed in Mainz around 1440, with placing books in the hands of ordinary Europeans for the first time. The claim has some basis: by 1500, presses across Europe had produced millions of volumes, and the cost of a book fell sharply compared with that of a hand-copied manuscript. __Yet surviving sales records show that most early printed books were Latin religious and legal texts, priced well beyond the means of the farmers and laborers who made up the majority of the population.__ For several generations, then, the press mainly enlarged the libraries of clergy, lawyers, and wealthy merchants. Only later, as cheap pamphlets and vernacular works multiplied, did printing begin to reach readers outside these groups.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It supplies evidence that the cost of printed books fell more slowly than historians have generally assumed.
It introduces evidence that qualifies a widely held view of the press's immediate effects.
It identifies the kinds of texts that later made printing accessible to farmers and laborers.
It offers evidence that the number of books produced by 1500 has been overstated.
g.explanation: 글은 구텐베르크 인쇄기가 곧바로 일반인에게 책을 보급했다는 통념을 제시하고 일부 근거를 인정한 뒤, 밑줄 문장(Yet)에서 초기 책이 라틴어 종교·법률서였고 가격도 높았다는 증거로 그 견해를 제한한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 가격 언급이 있어 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 가격 하락 자체를 인정하며 하락 속도를 문제 삼지 않는다. C는 나중에 접근성을 넓힌 것이 팸플릿과 자국어 저작이라 했으므로 밑줄 문장의 라틴어 문헌과 반대다. D는 생산량 수치를 반박하지 않으므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The text first presents the common view that Gutenberg's press immediately brought books to ordinary people and grants it some support. The underlined sentence, introduced by "Yet," then gives evidence that early books were Latin religious and legal texts priced too high for most people, which limits that view, so B is correct. A is tempting because price is mentioned, but the text accepts that prices fell sharply and never questions how fast they fell. C is wrong because the text says it was later pamphlets and vernacular works, not the Latin texts in the underlined sentence, that reached wider readers. D is wrong because the sentence never challenges the production figures.
g.design: 'Yet' 뒤 증거가 통념을 전면 부정이 아닌 제한한다는 점을 파악해야 하며, 오답 A·C는 지문 속 가격·텍스트 종류 단서와 부분적으로 겹쳐 비교가 필요하다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Congress of Vienna 1814-1815 and European balance of power restoration after Napoleonic wars

g.passage: Historians have long credited the Congress of Vienna (1814–1815) with restoring a durable balance of power in Europe after the Napoleonic Wars. Diplomats such as Austria's Klemens von Metternich redrew borders so that no single state could dominate the continent, and the arrangement is often said to have kept major powers from fighting a general war for nearly a century. __Yet the settlement's stability rested less on the new map than on the habit of consultation it created: the great powers agreed to meet periodically to resolve disputes before they escalated.__ Some scholars argue that when this practice of regular conferences faded in the 1820s, the balance itself grew fragile, even though the borders drawn at Vienna remained largely intact.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces evidence that the borders drawn at Vienna were rejected by most of the great powers within a few years.
It explains how Metternich personally persuaded the other diplomats to accept a balance of power among European states.
It shifts the explanation of the settlement's success from one factor to another, setting up the claim that follows.
It challenges the view that the Congress of Vienna contributed in any meaningful way to peace in Europe.
g.design: 밑줄 문장이 'Yet'으로 시작해 성과 자체를 부정하는 듯 보이지만 실제로는 성공 원인을 국경에서 협의 관행으로 옮기는 역할이라 훑어 읽으면 D를 고르기 쉽게 했다. A와 B는 지문의 국경·메테르니히 언급과 부분적으로 겹치게 만들었다.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 빈 회의의 안정이 새로 그은 국경보다 정기적인 협의 관행 덕분이었다고 말하며 성공의 원인을 옮겨 놓는다. 그리고 바로 다음 문장에서 협의 관행이 약해지자 국경은 그대로였는데도 세력 균형이 흔들렸다는 주장으로 이어지므로 정답은 C이다. A는 국경이 거부당했다고 하지만, 지문은 국경이 대체로 유지되었다고 말한다. B는 메테르니히의 개인적 설득을 다루는데, 밑줄 문장은 그런 내용을 전혀 언급하지 않는다. D는 'Yet'만 보고 회의의 기여 자체를 부정한다고 오해한 선택지로, 밑줄 문장은 안정이 있었다는 점을 인정하고 그 원인만 다시 설명한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence says the settlement's stability came less from the new borders and more from the habit of regular consultation, so it moves the explanation of success from one cause to another. The next sentence builds on this point: when consultation faded, the balance weakened even though the borders stayed the same. That makes C correct. A is wrong because the text says the borders remained largely intact, not that they were rejected. B is wrong because the underlined sentence says nothing about Metternich persuading anyone. D misreads the word "Yet." The sentence accepts that the settlement brought stability and only reexplains why, rather than denying that it helped keep the peace.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Glorious Revolution 1688-1689 and English constitutional settlement establishing parliamentary supremacy

g.passage: Popular accounts often describe the Glorious Revolution of 1688–1689 as the moment Parliament simply seized control from the English monarchy. When William of Orange and Mary accepted the throne, they also accepted the Bill of Rights, which barred the Crown from suspending laws or keeping a standing army in peacetime without Parliament's consent. __Yet the settlement's most lasting effect came less from these written prohibitions than from a practical arrangement: Parliament began granting the Crown revenue for only a limited period, which meant it had to meet every year.__ Historians such as Mark Kishlansky have argued that because monarchs now depended on regular parliamentary sessions to fund government, parliamentary supremacy grew out of financial routine rather than out of a single dramatic declaration.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It lists the specific restrictions on royal power that the Bill of Rights set out, which the rest of the text then explains in detail.
It offers evidence that William and Mary resisted the limits placed on them, which complicates the popular view of the Revolution.
It introduces a historian's claim that the Bill of Rights had little effect, which the text then rejects as overstated.
It shifts attention from the formal legal limits to a fiscal mechanism, which sets up the explanation of how Parliament's dominance actually developed.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 앞에서 말한 권리장전의 명문화된 금지 조항에서 의회가 기한부로 세입을 승인한 재정 관행으로 초점을 옮기고, 마지막 문장은 그 관행에서 의회 우위가 생겨났다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 금지 조항을 나열하는 것은 앞 문장이고, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 그 조항들의 비중을 낮춘다. B는 지문이 대중적 견해를 다루기는 하지만, 윌리엄과 메리가 제한에 저항했다는 내용은 없다. C는 역사가가 언급되기는 하지만 밑줄 문장 뒤에 나오며, 지문은 그 주장을 반박하지 않고 받아들인다.
g.explanation_en: D is correct. The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and moves the focus away from the Bill of Rights' written prohibitions to a financial practice: Parliament granted revenue for only a limited time. The final sentence then explains that Parliament's supremacy grew out of that practice. A is wrong because the sentence before the underlined one is the one that lists the restrictions, and the underlined sentence actually plays them down. B is wrong because the text does mention the popular view, but it never says William and Mary resisted their limits. C is wrong because the historian is mentioned only after the underlined sentence, and the text accepts his argument instead of rejecting it.
g.design: 오답 A와 C는 각각 권리장전과 역사가라는 실제 지문 요소를 끌어와 부분적으로 맞아 보이게 만들었다. 정답을 고르려면 'Yet'이 일으키는 초점 전환과 마지막 문장의 결론을 연결해야 한다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Philippine-American War 1899-1902 and United States colonial counterinsurgency amid nationalist resistance

g.passage: When the Philippine-American War began in 1899, many US commanders expected Filipino resistance to collapse once Emilio Aguinaldo's conventional army was defeated in open battle. By late 1899, Aguinaldo had indeed disbanded his regular units, and some American officials declared the war effectively over. __Yet Aguinaldo had ordered his forces not to surrender but to split into small guerrilla bands that could blend into villages and strike without warning.__ Over the following two years, these bands drew on local networks of support, prompting US forces to adopt harsher measures such as relocating rural populations into guarded zones. Historians therefore argue that the war's most consequential phase began, rather than ended, with the breakup of the Filipino regular army.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a development that undercuts an earlier assumption and sets up the account of the conflict that follows.
It introduces a development that explains why US officials concluded that the conflict had come to an end.
It introduces a development that shows how US forces successfully adapted their tactics to Filipino resistance.
It introduces a development that historians cite to argue that Aguinaldo's army was defeated in open battle.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 미군 지휘관들이 기대했던 '정규군이 패하면 저항이 무너질 것'이라는 가정을 뒤집는다. 또한 이어지는 게릴라전과 미군의 강경책에 대한 서술, 그리고 결정적 국면이 정규군 해체와 함께 시작됐다는 결론으로 이어지므로 A가 정답이다. B는 반대이다. 관리들이 전쟁이 끝났다고 선언한 것은 밑줄 문장보다 앞에 나오며, 밑줄 문장은 그 결론을 반박한다. C는 미군의 대응을 언급하긴 하지만, 그 대응은 밑줄 다음 문장에 나오고 '성공'으로 평가되지도 않는다. D는 정규군 해체라는 앞부분 사실을 밑줄 문장의 기능과 혼동한 것이다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet," and it overturns the commanders' assumption that resistance would collapse once the regular army was beaten. It also sets up the rest of the text: the guerrilla campaign, the harsher US measures, and the historians' conclusion that the key phase began when the regular army broke up. That makes A correct. B gets it backward: officials declared the war over before the underlined sentence, and that sentence challenges their conclusion. C points to the US response, but that response comes in the next sentence, and the text never calls it successful. D mixes up the earlier fact that the regular army was disbanded with what the underlined sentence actually does.
g.design: To get this right, you have to see the contrast signaled by "Yet" and then connect it to the paragraph that follows. Each wrong answer is built from a detail found elsewhere in the passage.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Russo-Japanese War 1904-1905 and Asian military victory over European imperial power

g.passage: Japan's victory over Russia in 1905 is often described as the first modern defeat of a European great power by an Asian nation, but historian Rotem Kowner cautions against treating the war's outcome as having ______ European imperial dominance. Russia lost a fleet and a war, yet it kept its vast territorial empire, and Britain, France, and other colonial powers held on to their Asian possessions for decades afterward. What the war did change, Kowner argues, was perception: nationalist writers from Cairo to Calcutta cited Japan's success as proof that European supremacy was not inevitable.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: challenged
dismantled
inspired
questioned
g.design: 오답 A와 D는 전쟁이 유럽의 우월성을 실제로 흔들었다는 지문 후반부 내용과 부분적으로 맞아떨어지지만, Kowner가 경계하는 주장은 '실제 붕괴'라는 더 강한 주장이다. 따라서 '경계한다'라는 표현과 이어지는 반례를 연결해서 읽어야 정답을 고를 수 있다.
g.explanation: Kowner는 전쟁 결과를 어떤 식으로 보는 것을 경계하고, 바로 뒤에 러시아가 제국을 유지했고 식민 열강도 수십 년간 영토를 지켰다는 근거를 든다. 따라서 그가 부정하는 주장은 유럽 지배가 '해체되었다'는 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 지문 마지막 문장에서 전쟁이 유럽 우월성이 필연적이라는 인식을 흔들었다고 하므로 실제로 일어난 일에 해당하고, Kowner가 경계할 대상이 아니다. C는 전쟁이 유럽 지배를 '고무했다'는 뜻이 되어 Japan의 승리라는 문맥과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Kowner warns against one particular reading of the war, and the text immediately backs him up: Russia kept its empire, and the colonial powers held their Asian territories for decades. So the claim he rejects is that the war dismantled European dominance, which makes B correct. A and D describe what the war actually did, since the last sentence says it shook the belief that European supremacy was inevitable, so Kowner would have no reason to caution against them. C would mean the war inspired European dominance, which makes no sense given that an Asian nation won.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Qing Dynasty suppression of Tibetan autonomy and Chinese religious assimilation policies twentieth century

g.passage: In the final years of the Qing Dynasty, the official Zhao Erfeng led campaigns in the Kham region of eastern Tibet that went far beyond earlier imperial practice. Previous Qing administrators had generally been content to oversee the region's hereditary chieftains and the powerful monasteries allied with them. Zhao, by contrast, aimed to ______ these local rulers altogether: under the policy known as gaitu guiliu, he abolished their positions and installed magistrates appointed by the imperial court in their place.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: discipline
restrain
supplant
counsel
g.explanation: 지문은 Zhao가 지방 수장들의 직위를 폐지하고 그 자리에 조정이 임명한 관리를 앉혔다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '대체하다, 밀어내고 그 자리를 차지하다'는 뜻의 C(supplant)가 가장 정확하다. 또 'altogether'와 'by contrast'는 단순히 감독하던 이전 방식과 다르다는 점을 강조하는데, C가 이 대비에 맞는다. A(discipline)와 B(restrain)는 억압적 통치라는 분위기에는 맞지만, 수장들을 그 자리에 둔 채 통제한다는 뜻이어서 직위를 없앴다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. D(counsel)는 조언한다는 뜻이라 강경한 정책 전환과 어울리지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says Zhao abolished the chieftains' positions and put court-appointed magistrates in their place, so the blank needs a word meaning "replace." That is C (supplant). The words "by contrast" and "altogether" also set Zhao apart from earlier officials who only oversaw the chieftains, and C fits that contrast. A (discipline) and B (restrain) match the harsh tone, but each one means controlling the chieftains while they keep their posts, and the text says those posts were eliminated. D (counsel) means giving advice, which doesn't fit this forceful break from past practice.
g.design: 오답 A·B는 '억압' 맥락과 부분적으로 맞아 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉽지만, 직위 폐지와 대체라는 두 번째 단서까지 연결해야 C만 남도록 설계했다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Abolitionist movement in nineteenth-century Britain and William Wilberforce's parliamentary campaigns ending transatlantic slave trade

g.passage: Beginning in 1791, William Wilberforce introduced bills in the British Parliament to abolish the transatlantic slave trade, and each time the bills were defeated. Supporters outside Parliament then gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures on petitions and organized a boycott of sugar grown by enslaved people, showing lawmakers how many ordinary Britons opposed the trade. In 1807, after years of this public pressure, Parliament finally passed the Slave Trade Act by a large majority. These events suggest that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Wilberforce's early bills failed mainly because he stopped presenting them after 1791.
the petitions and the boycott had little connection to the eventual vote in Parliament.
the 1807 law passed because most lawmakers had supported abolition from the very beginning.
the campaign outside Parliament helped change lawmakers' votes on the slave trade.
g.explanation: 지문은 법안이 반복적으로 부결된 뒤 청원과 불매운동으로 대중의 압력이 쌓였고, 그 결과 1807년 법안이 큰 표차로 통과되었다고 서술하므로 D가 가장 논리적인 결론이다. A는 법안을 '매번' 제출했다는 지문 내용과 어긋난다. B는 '수년간의 대중 압력 이후' 통과되었다는 연결을 부정한다. C는 초기 법안들이 부결되었다는 사실과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The text says Wilberforce's bills were defeated again and again, then public petitions and a boycott built pressure, and after that Parliament passed the act by a large majority, so D is the most logical conclusion. A contradicts the text, which says he introduced bills repeatedly and they were defeated each time. B ignores the text's link between years of public pressure and the final vote. C conflicts with the fact that the early bills failed, which shows most lawmakers did not support abolition at first.
g.design: 이 문항은 '반복된 부결 → 대중의 압력 → 통과'라는 지문 속 순서를 한 단계만 추론하면 풀린다. 오답은 모두 정답과 같은 'X가 Y했다' 형식의 결론문으로, 제출 횟수를 잘못 읽거나 인과 관계를 무시하는 등 흔한 오독을 반영했다.
