c.seed: history and civics — Storming of the Bastille July 1789 and French Revolutionary symbolic destruction of royal absolutist authority

g.passage: On July 14, 1789, crowds in Paris stormed the Bastille, a fortress-prison long associated with the king's power to jail people without trial. When the crowd broke in, they found only seven prisoners inside, and none of them was being held for political reasons. Even so, the people of Paris spent the following months taking the building apart stone by stone, and some of its stones were carved into small models of the fortress and sent to towns across France. Because freeing a large number of prisoners clearly was not what made the event important, historians conclude that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the event mattered mainly because it destroyed a symbol of the king's unchecked authority.
the event mattered mainly because it gave the crowd weapons it later used in battle.
the event mattered mainly because it emptied a prison that held many of the king's critics.
the event mattered mainly because it gave Paris valuable building stone for new projects.
g.explanation: 지문은 바스티유가 왕의 재판 없는 투옥 권력과 연결된 장소였고, 안에 죄수가 7명뿐이었는데도 사람들이 건물을 허물고 그 돌로 모형을 만들어 전국에 보냈다고 설명한다. 따라서 이 사건이 중요했던 이유는 왕의 무제한 권력을 나타내는 상징을 무너뜨렸다는 데 있으므로 A가 정답이다. C는 정치범이 한 명도 없었다는 지문 내용과 어긋난다. B는 무기에 관한 정보가 지문에 전혀 없어 근거가 없다. D는 돌을 실용적인 건축 자재로 썼다는 뜻이지만, 지문에서 돌은 상징적인 모형으로 만들어졌으므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the Bastille stood for the king's power to jail people without trial. Even though only seven prisoners were inside, Parisians tore the building down and sent carved models of it across France. That shows the event mattered because it destroyed a symbol of the king's unchecked authority, so A is correct. C doesn't fit, because the passage says none of the prisoners was being held for political reasons. B has no support, since the passage never mentions weapons. D is wrong because the stones were turned into symbolic models rather than used for practical building.
g.design: 이 문항은 단서 하나로 한 단계만 추론하면 풀리도록 만들었다. 단서는 죄수는 몇 명 없었는데도 사람들이 건물을 허물고 그 돌로 모형을 만들었다는 점이다. 오답에는 학생들이 흔히 가진 오해(많은 정치범 석방, 무기 확보, 실용적 자재 활용)를 담았고, 네 선택지 모두 같은 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Trail of Tears 1838-1839 and forced Indian removal policy displacing Cherokee Nation westward

g.passage: In 1838 and 1839, the United States government forced thousands of Cherokee people to leave their homelands in the Southeast and move west to Indian Territory, a journey later called the Trail of Tears. Some historians argue that the removal was not simply the result of federal policy but was strongly pushed by people in Georgia who wanted Cherokee land, especially after gold was discovered there in 1829. According to this view, pressure from Georgia settlers and officials was a major force behind the removal.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' view?
options: Records show that many Cherokee families brought livestock, tools, and household goods with them on the journey west.
Letters from the 1830s show Georgia lawmakers repeatedly urging Congress to remove the Cherokee so the state could distribute their land to settlers.
Accounts show that the winter of 1838–1839 was unusually cold along parts of the route, causing many illnesses and deaths.
Documents show that after arriving in Indian Territory, the Cherokee Nation rebuilt its government and adopted a new constitution.
g.explanation: 역사가들의 주장은 조지아 주민과 관리들의 땅에 대한 압력이 강제 이주의 주요 원인이었다는 것이다. B는 조지아 의원들이 땅을 얻으려고 의회에 이주를 반복해서 요구했다는 내용이라 그 압력을 직접 보여 주므로 정답이다. A와 C는 이주 과정에서 있었던 일(가져간 물건, 날씨)을 다룰 뿐 이주가 왜 일어났는지는 말하지 않는다. D는 이주 이후의 일이라 원인에 관한 주장과 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The historians claim that pressure from Georgia settlers and officials who wanted Cherokee land was a major cause of the removal. B directly shows that pressure: Georgia lawmakers repeatedly pushed Congress for removal so the state could hand out the land, so B is correct. A and C describe what happened during the journey (the goods people carried, the weather), but they don't explain why the removal happened. D is about events after the removal, so it has nothing to do with a claim about its cause.
g.design: 쉬운 단일 규칙(원인에 관한 주장을 뒷받침하려면 원인을 보여 줘야 한다)으로 풀리게 만들었다. 오답들은 같은 'Records/Accounts/Documents show' 문장 틀을 쓰고 Trail of Tears와 관련은 있지만 원인과는 무관한 내용이다.

c.seed: history and civics — Luddite rebellion 1811-1817 and English textile workers' mechanized machinery destruction resisting industrial displacement

g.passage: Between 1811 and 1817, groups of English textile workers known as Luddites broke into workshops at night and smashed stocking frames and other machines. The Luddites are often remembered as people who simply hated new technology. However, some historians argue that the Luddites were not against machines in general. Instead, these historians claim, the workers attacked machines mainly to protest employers who used the machines to cut wages and replace skilled workers with cheaper, less trained labor.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' claim?
options: Records show that the Luddites carried out most of their attacks at night, when workshops were empty and guards were few.
Records show that the Luddites destroyed machines in many different towns, spread across several English counties.
Records show that the Luddites often left alone machines owned by employers who paid standard wages, while breaking machines owned by employers who had lowered pay.
Records show that the Luddites destroyed many more machines in 1812 than in any other single year of the rebellion.
g.explanation: 역사가들의 주장은 러다이트가 기계 자체가 아니라 임금을 깎는 고용주에게 항의하려고 기계를 부쉈다는 것이다. C는 정상 임금을 주는 고용주의 기계는 그대로 두고 임금을 낮춘 고용주의 기계만 부쉈다고 하므로, 공격 대상이 기계가 아니라 고용주의 행태에 따라 정해졌음을 직접 보여 준다. A는 공격 시간과 방식만 말할 뿐 동기를 알려 주지 않는다. B는 반란이 넓은 지역에 퍼졌다는 것만 보여 주고, 왜 공격했는지는 드러나지 않는다. D는 공격이 가장 많았던 해를 말할 뿐 기계를 부순 이유와 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The historians claim the Luddites attacked machines to protest employers who cut wages, not because they hated machines in general. C supports this directly: the workers left alone machines owned by fair-paying employers and broke those owned by employers who lowered pay. That means their targets depended on how employers behaved, not on the machines themselves. A only describes when and how the attacks happened, not why. B shows that the rebellion was widespread but tells you nothing about its motive. D gives the busiest year of attacks, which also doesn't explain why the machines were destroyed.
g.design: Easy: the only step is to check which finding links the attacks to wage-cutting employers rather than to machines in general. The wrong answers are true-sounding facts about the rebellion (when, where, and how many attacks) that say nothing about motive, and all four use the same "Records show..." frame.

c.seed: life science — Tardigrade cryptobiosis mechanism and anhydrobiosis survival enabling extreme environmental stress resistance

g.passage: Tardigrades, microscopic animals often called water bears, can survive almost complete drying by entering a state called anhydrobiosis, in which their metabolism slows to nearly undetectable levels. For years, researchers assumed tardigrades relied on the sugar trehalose, which protects many other drought-tolerant organisms by replacing water around cell structures. However, many tardigrade species produce little or no trehalose. Biologist Thomas Boothby and colleagues found that these animals instead make unusual proteins, which the team named tardigrade-specific intrinsically disordered proteins (TDPs). As a tardigrade dries out, TDPs form a glass-like solid inside its cells that appears to hold delicate molecules in place until water returns. When the researchers blocked TDP production, the tardigrades survived drying far less often, and when they added the genes for TDPs to yeast, the yeast became more resistant to drying.
g.question: According to the text, what did Boothby and colleagues' research show about how tardigrades survive drying?
options: Tardigrades survive drying mainly by producing large amounts of trehalose, which replaces the water around their cell structures.
Tardigrades survive drying by keeping their metabolism at normal levels so that damaged molecules can be repaired as the animals dry.
Tardigrades survive drying by taking in protective proteins from yeast and other organisms in their surroundings.
Tardigrades survive drying largely by relying on a distinctive set of proteins that solidify inside their cells as water is lost.
g.explanation: 지문은 많은 완보동물이 트레할로스를 거의 만들지 않고, 대신 TDP라는 특이한 단백질을 만들어 이것이 건조 시 세포 안에서 유리 같은 고체를 형성한다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. TDP를 차단하면 생존율이 떨어졌다는 결과도 이를 뒷받침한다. A는 연구자들이 오랫동안 가정했던 내용일 뿐이며, 지문은 이를 반박한다. B는 대사가 거의 감지되지 않을 정도로 느려진다는 서술과 모순된다. C는 효모와 단백질의 관계를 뒤집은 것으로, 실제로는 TDP 유전자를 효모에 넣은 것이다.
g.explanation_en: D is correct: the text says many tardigrades make little trehalose and instead make unusual proteins (TDPs), which turn into a glass-like solid inside their cells as they dry out. The finding that blocking TDPs made survival less likely supports this. A describes what researchers had long assumed, and the text goes on to challenge that assumption. B contradicts the statement that metabolism slows to nearly undetectable levels. C reverses the yeast experiment: the researchers put tardigrade TDP genes into yeast, not the other way around.
g.design: To get this right, you have to link the rejected trehalose assumption to the new TDP finding. A uses the earlier assumption, and C twists the details of the yeast experiment.

c.seed: life science — Naked mole rat cancer resistance and p16 tumor suppressor gene mutation conferring extraordinary longevity

g.passage: Naked mole rats can live for more than thirty years, roughly ten times longer than mice of similar size, and they almost never develop cancer. Biologist Vera Gorbunova and colleagues traced part of this resistance to a mechanism called early contact inhibition. Ordinary mouse cells stop dividing only once they become tightly crowded, but naked mole rat cells stop much earlier, at low density. The team found that this early halt depends on the tumor suppressor gene p16, which in naked mole rats responds to crowding before a second suppressor gene, p27, becomes active. When the researchers experimentally disabled p16, the cells lost early contact inhibition, though p27 still stopped them at higher densities. Because the animals carry two layers of growth control rather than one, Gorbunova argues, a single genetic error is less likely to let cells multiply unchecked, which may help explain how the species stays cancer-free over such a long life.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Research suggests that naked mole rats resist cancer partly because a gene halts cell division early, backing up a second gene that acts later.
Research suggests that naked mole rats resist cancer mainly because their cells divide far more slowly than mouse cells at every density.
Research suggests that naked mole rats resist cancer because the gene p27 alone halts cell division before cells become crowded.
Research suggests that naked mole rats resist cancer because disabling the gene p16 causes their cells to stop dividing entirely.
g.explanation: 지문은 p16이 낮은 밀도에서 먼저 세포 분열을 멈추고, p27이 더 높은 밀도에서 두 번째 제어층으로 작용하는 이중 구조가 암 저항성을 설명할 수 있다고 주장하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쥐와의 비교를 사용하지만 지문은 분열 속도가 아니라 분열이 멈추는 밀도의 차이를 말한다. C는 p27을 언급하지만, 이른 정지를 담당하는 것은 p16이고 p27은 나중에 작용한다. D는 실험을 왜곡했다. p16을 비활성화하자 이른 정지가 사라졌을 뿐, 분열이 완전히 멈춘 것이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: Choice A is correct: the text explains that p16 stops cell division early, at low density, while p27 acts later as a second layer, and it argues that this double system helps explain the animals' cancer resistance. Choice B uses the comparison with mice, but the text describes a difference in the density at which cells stop dividing, not in how fast they divide. Choice C mentions p27, but it is p16 that causes the early halt, and p27 only acts at higher densities. Choice D distorts the experiment: disabling p16 removed the early halt rather than stopping division entirely.
g.design: 두 정보(p16 조기 정지 + p27 후속 백업)를 연결해야 정답이 되도록 했고, 오답은 같은 문장 틀에 지문 속 세부(쥐 비교, p27, 비활성화 실험)를 잘못 연결해 넣었다.

c.seed: life science — Axolotl neoteny and thyroid hormone regulation maintaining larval characteristics throughout adult lifespan

g.passage: Most salamanders undergo metamorphosis: they hatch as aquatic larvae with feathery external gills and later transform into land-dwelling adults with lungs and thicker skin. The axolotl, a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City, typically never makes this transition. Instead, it reaches sexual maturity while keeping its gills, finned tail, and fully aquatic lifestyle, a condition known as neoteny. For decades, researchers assumed the axolotl simply lacked the biological machinery needed to transform. Experiments complicated that view. When biologists exposed axolotls to thyroid hormone, the animals developed lungs, lost their gills, and became terrestrial adults resembling their close relative, the tiger salamander. Later studies traced the axolotl's usual larval state to low activity in the gland system that triggers thyroid hormone release, not to tissues that are unable to respond to the hormone. In other words, the capacity for metamorphosis remains intact in the axolotl; what is ordinarily missing is the internal signal that would set it in motion.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although axolotls keep their gills into adulthood, studies show that their tissues have gradually lost the ability to respond to thyroid hormone.
Although axolotls usually remain larval-looking throughout life, research indicates this results from a weak hormonal trigger rather than an inability to transform.
Although axolotls resemble tiger salamanders after exposure to thyroid hormone, studies show the two species differ mainly in their native habitats.
Although axolotls reach sexual maturity while staying aquatic, research indicates that this trait developed because their lakes lack suitable land habitat.
g.explanation: 지문은 축삭이 보통 유생 형태를 유지하지만, 갑상선 호르몬을 주면 변태하며, 그 원인은 조직의 반응 불능이 아니라 호르몬 분비를 촉발하는 신호가 약하기 때문이라고 결론짓는다. 따라서 B가 중심 내용이다. A는 지문이 명시적으로 부정한 '조직의 반응 불능'을 원인으로 삼으므로 틀리다. C는 호르몬 처리 후 타이거 샐러맨더와 닮는다는 세부는 맞지만 서식지 차이가 핵심이라는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 성적 성숙과 수생 생활이라는 세부는 맞지만 육지 서식지 부족이라는 원인은 지문에 제시되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that axolotls normally stay larval-looking, but when given thyroid hormone they do metamorphose. It concludes that the cause is low activity in the system that triggers hormone release, not tissues that can't respond. That makes B the main idea. A is wrong because it blames the tissues' inability to respond, which is exactly the explanation the text rejects. C is built on a true detail (treated axolotls resemble tiger salamanders), but the text never says the two species differ mainly in habitat. D also starts with true details (sexual maturity, aquatic life), but the text never says a lack of land habitat explains the trait.
g.design: B를 포함한 모든 선택지가 같은 'Although…, research indicates…' 틀을 쓴다. 오답 A, C, D에는 지문의 정확한 세부를 넣고 거기에 틀린 결론을 붙였다. 그래서 한 단계에서 세부를 확인하고, 다음 단계에서 원인에 대한 결론을 대조해야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

c.seed: life science — Sea cucumber holothurian evisceration defense and visceral regeneration rapid organ restoration capability

g.passage: When threatened by a predator, many sea cucumbers do something that seems self-defeating: they contract their body walls and expel part of their internal organs, often including the gut and respiratory structures, through a rupture in the body. This behavior, called evisceration, was long viewed by naturalists as a desperate last resort that left the animal crippled. Studies of species such as Holothuria glaberrima, however, have shown that the loss is temporary. Within days, cells near the wound begin to lose their specialized features and migrate to form a new tube of tissue, and within a few weeks a functional digestive tract has been rebuilt. Because the discarded organs can distract or entangle an attacker while the animal crawls away, researchers now regard evisceration less as an act of desperation than as one half of a coordinated strategy whose success depends on the animal's capacity to restore what it gives up.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Sea cucumbers expel their internal organs mainly to entangle predators, a tactic that researchers have found works against most of the animals that hunt them.
Sea cucumbers that undergo evisceration are left temporarily unable to feed, which naturalists consider the chief cost of the behavior.
Sea cucumbers' ability to quickly rebuild lost organs has led scientists to reinterpret organ expulsion as part of an effective defense rather than a damaging final act.
Sea cucumbers regenerate their digestive tracts through cells that lose their specialized features, a process researchers first observed in Holothuria glaberrima.
g.explanation: 지문은 장기 배출이 한때 동물을 불구로 만드는 최후 수단으로 여겨졌지만, 빠른 재생 능력이 밝혀지면서 재생과 짝을 이루는 조직적 방어 전략으로 재해석되었다는 내용이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 장기로 포식자를 엉키게 한다는 세부는 맞지만, 대부분의 포식자에게 통한다는 주장은 지문에 없고 재생이라는 핵심도 빠져 있다. g.passage: Bdelloid rotifers, microscopic animals found in ponds and damp moss, have reproduced without males for tens of millions of years. Part of the answer may lie in their ability to survive complete drying. When its habitat dries, a bdelloid curls into a dormant state, and its DNA breaks into fragments. Researchers have found that during this repair, the rotifer's cells appear to stitch in foreign DNA, including genes taken up from bacteria and fungi. g.passage:
Most reptiles depend on their surroundings for body heat, so biologists were long puzzled that leatherback sea turtles regularly forage in waters off Nova Scotia that hover near 10°C. Measurements have shown that a leatherback's core can stay more than 15°C warmer than the surrounding sea. Part of the explanation is size: an adult leatherback can exceed 500 kilograms, and a large body loses heat slowly relative to the heat its muscles generate while swimming. Size alone, however, cannot account for the turtle's success, because its large front flippers are thin, broad, and constantly exposed to cold water, which should make them major sites of heat loss.

Researchers found that at the base of each flipper, arteries carrying warm blood outward run tightly alongside veins carrying cooled blood back toward the body. As the two flows pass each other, heat moves from the outgoing arterial blood into the returning venous blood, so much of the warmth is carried back to the core rather than reaching the flipper tip. This countercurrent arrangement, together with a thick layer of insulating fat, allows the leatherback to keep its core warm even as its flippers cool to nearly the temperature of the water.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although a leatherback's large body helps it retain heat, an arrangement of blood vessels in its flippers is also needed to explain how it stays warm in cold seas.
Although a leatherback's flippers lose a great deal of heat, the turtle's large body size by itself fully compensates for that loss in cold seas.
Although a leatherback's blood vessels exchange heat efficiently, the turtle must keep its flippers as warm as its core to swim in cold seas.
Although most reptiles rely on outside heat sources, the leatherback's insulating fat is the main reason biologists find it in cold seas.

g.passage: The Pacific lamprey, a jawless fish that spends part of its adult life at sea, feeds by fastening its round, tooth-lined oral disc to the side of a larger fish and rasping through the skin with its tongue. It explains why client fish visit cleaning stations despite the risks they face from the wrasse.
It describes a feeding preference that Bshary later found to disappear when wrasse are observed by other fish.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 청소놀래기가 기생충보다 점액을 선호해 고객 물고기에게 손해를 준다는 이해 충돌을 제시하고, 이후 문장들은 고객의 처벌이 그 관계를 유지시킨다고 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 통념을 복잡하게 만든다는 점은 맞지만, 해가 이익보다 크다고 주장하는 글은 아니다. 지문은 관계가 유지된다고 결론 내린다. C는 고객이 왜 찾아오는지를 설명하지 않으며, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 고객이 겪는 비용을 보여 준다. D는 관찰될 때 무는 횟수가 줄어든다는 내용에 기대고 있지만, 지문에서는 선호가 사라진다고 하지 않고 무는 빈도가 줄어든다고만 한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence shows a conflict of interest: the wrasse would rather eat the client's mucus, which hurts the client. The rest of the text then explains that the partnership stays stable because clients punish this cheating, so A is correct. B is wrong because the text complicates the usual "simple trade" view but never says the harm is greater than the benefit, and it concludes that the relationship holds together. C is wrong because the sentence describes a cost to clients, not a reason they visit stations. D is wrong because the text says wrasse bite less often when being watched, not that their preference goes away.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 밑줄 문장을 뒤에 나오는 처벌 메커니즘과 연결해야 한다. B와 D는 각각 '통념을 뒤집는 내용'과 '관찰될 때의 행동 변화'라는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 이용한다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: life science — American pika alpine mammal thermoregulation failure and climate warming range contraction vulnerability

g.passage: The American pika, a small relative of the rabbit, lives on rocky alpine slopes in western North America. Because it does not hibernate and carries a dense coat suited to cold, the pika can die after only a few hours of exposure to temperatures around 25°C. Researchers have therefore long predicted that warming summers would push pikas upslope and eliminate low-elevation populations. __Yet surveys in parts of the Columbia River Gorge have found pikas thriving at sites barely above sea level, where summer afternoons regularly exceed that threshold.__ Investigating these sites, ecologist Johanna Varner found that the animals shelter in deep talus and moss-covered rock, where temperatures stay cool, and shift their foraging to early mornings and evenings. Such findings suggest that the pika's vulnerability to warming depends less on air temperature alone than on whether its local terrain offers cool refuges.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It provides evidence confirming that pika populations have already shifted to higher elevations as summers have warmed.
It presents an observation that seems at odds with an expectation, prompting the investigation described afterward.
It identifies the specific temperature at which pikas begin to suffer harmful effects from overheating.
It presents a finding that leads researchers to conclude that pikas are not physiologically sensitive to heat.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 시작해 따뜻해지면 저지대 개체군이 사라질 것이라는 예측과 맞지 않는 관찰(해수면 근처에서 번성하는 피카)을 제시하고, 이어지는 Varner의 조사로 이어진다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 이 문장이 예측을 확인하는 것이 아니라 반박하는 내용이므로 틀렸다. C의 기준 온도(25°C)는 앞 문장에 나오고, 밑줄 문장은 이를 언급할 뿐 새로 밝히지 않는다. D는 지문이 피카의 열 민감성을 부정하지 않고, 서늘한 피난처가 그 민감성을 보완한다고 결론짓기 때문에 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and reports pikas thriving near sea level, which conflicts with the prediction that warming would wipe out low-elevation populations. That puzzle is exactly what Varner then investigates, so B is correct. A is wrong because the sentence goes against the upslope prediction rather than confirming it. C is wrong because the threshold temperature is given in the earlier sentence, and the underlined sentence only refers back to it. D is wrong because the text never says pikas aren't sensitive to heat; it concludes that cool refuges let them cope with that sensitivity.
g.design: 정답은 두 단계를 거쳐야 고를 수 있다. 'Yet'이 앞의 예측과 대비된다는 점을 읽고, 이어서 그 대비가 뒤의 조사로 연결된다는 점까지 확인해야 한다. 오답 C와 D는 지문의 수치나 결론을 부분적으로 가져와서 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보이도록 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: life science — Tree frog metamorphosis tadpole water toxin tolerance and terrestrial juvenile adaptation developmental transition

g.passage: Many tree frogs begin life as tadpoles in small ponds, where they breathe through gills and feed on algae. Researchers studying one species found that young tadpoles can survive fairly high levels of certain pollutants in the water. As the tadpoles approach metamorphosis, however, this tolerance drops sharply. During this stage, their bodies are rebuilding lungs, skin, and legs for life on land, and much of their energy goes into these changes rather than into defending against toxins. The researchers concluded that the weeks of transformation from water to land are the period when these frogs are most vulnerable to polluted water.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Tree frog tadpoles survive polluted water better than adult frogs because gills filter out toxins.
Tree frogs leave ponds early in life mainly to escape the pollutants found in the water.
Tree frogs are especially sensitive to water pollution while they are changing from tadpoles into land-dwelling frogs.
Tree frog tadpoles depend on algae for food, so pollution harms them chiefly by killing algae.
g.explanation: 지문은 어린 올챙이는 오염물질에 잘 견디지만 변태가 가까워지면 내성이 급격히 떨어지며, 물에서 육지로 바뀌는 시기가 가장 취약하다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 C가 중심 내용이다. A는 성체 개구리와 비교하거나 아가미가 독소를 거른다는 내용이 지문에 없다. B는 개구리가 오염을 피하려고 연못을 떠난다는 근거 없는 인과를 제시한다. D는 조류를 먹는다는 세부 사항을 근거 없이 오염 피해의 원인으로 확대했다.
g.explanation_en: The text says young tadpoles tolerate pollutants fairly well, but this tolerance drops sharply near metamorphosis, and it concludes that the change from water to land is the most vulnerable period. That makes C the main idea. A compares tadpoles with adult frogs and says gills filter toxins, but the text says neither of these things. B claims frogs leave ponds to escape pollution, which is a cause the text never gives. D takes a minor detail (eating algae) and turns it into an explanation for pollution harm that the text doesn't support.
g.design: This is an easy item: the main idea comes straight from the text's concluding sentence and needs only a one-step paraphrase. Each wrong answer reuses a real detail from the text (gills, ponds, algae) but adds a cause or comparison that the text doesn't support.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: life science — Songbird mate selection genetic compatibility preference and major histocompatibility complex immune gene recognition

g.passage: For many years, biologists assumed that female songbirds chose mates mainly by judging the quality of a male's song or the brightness of his feathers. Recent studies of species such as the great reed warbler and the house sparrow suggest that something less visible also matters. Females in these species often pair with males whose immune genes, known as major histocompatibility complex (MHC) genes, differ from their own. Researchers think females may detect these differences through scent. Chicks whose parents have different MHC genes tend to inherit a wider range of immune defenses, which can help them resist more kinds of disease.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Female songbirds rely mostly on song quality and feather brightness when they choose a mate.
Female songbirds pick mates whose immune genes match their own so that their chicks will stay healthy.
Female songbirds use scent mainly to locate food and safe nesting sites for their chicks.
Female songbirds may also pick mates based on hidden genetic differences that give their chicks stronger protection against illness.
g.explanation: 지문은 노래나 깃털 외에 눈에 보이지 않는 면역 유전자(MHC)의 차이도 짝 선택에 영향을 주며, 그 결과 새끼가 더 다양한 질병에 저항할 수 있다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 지문이 오래된 가정으로 소개한 내용을 핵심처럼 제시한다. B는 유전자가 '같은' 짝을 고른다고 하여 지문의 '다른' 유전자와 반대된다. C는 냄새의 용도를 지문에 없는 먹이·둥지 찾기로 바꾸었다.
g.explanation_en: The text says that besides song and feathers, females often choose males whose MHC immune genes differ from their own, and that this gives chicks wider disease protection, so D is correct. A restates the older assumption the text introduces only to move beyond it. B says females prefer matching genes, but the text says they prefer different ones. C changes the role of scent to finding food and nests, which the text never mentions.
g.design: Easy: one explicit contrast (old assumption vs. new finding) signals the main idea; distractors share the same "Female songbirds..." frame and reflect typical misreadings.

c.instruction: 두 개의 짧은 텍스트(또는 텍스트와 연구 결과 요약)를 제시하고, 두 번째 텍스트의 저자나 연구자가 첫 번째 텍스트의 주장에 대해 보일 반응을 추론하는 문제를 만든다. 오답은 (1) 한쪽 텍스트 내용만으로 답한 경우, (2) 두 입장을 반대로 뒤바꾼 경우, (3) 두 텍스트 어디에도 없는 제3의 입장을 만든 경우로 구성한다.
c.seed: life science — Daphnia predator defense morphological induction and kairomone chemical signal detection phenotypic plasticity

g.passage:
When the water flea Daphnia pulex detects kairomones, chemical cues released by predatory midge larvae, juveniles grow small spines called "neckteeth" on the back of the head. Many biologists have described this response as a cost-free switch: because neckteeth develop only when predators are present, they argue, Daphnia gets protection when it needs it and pays nothing for it the rest of the time.

Biologist Mira Kessler grew genetically identical Daphnia in water with and without midge kairomones. She then kept both groups in predator-free tanks. Daphnia that had developed neckteeth matured later and produced about 15 percent fewer offspring than those that had not. However, when midge larvae were added, the neckteeth group survived at nearly twice the rate of the other group.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Kessler most likely respond to the biologists' description of neckteeth in the first text?
options: She would argue that the biologists are right that neckteeth protect Daphnia from midges but wrong to think that growing them carries no reproductive penalty.
She would argue that the biologists are right that neckteeth protect Daphnia from midges and right to think that growing them carries no reproductive penalty.
She would argue that the biologists are wrong that neckteeth protect Daphnia from midges but right to think that growing them carries no reproductive penalty.
She would argue that the biologists are wrong that neckteeth develop in response to kairomones and wrong to think that growing them carries no reproductive penalty.
g.design: 첫 텍스트의 '보호 효과 + 무비용' 주장을 두 번째 연구가 보호는 지지, 무비용은 반박하도록 구성해 두 텍스트를 결합해야만 정답이 나오게 했다. 오답은 첫 텍스트만 반영(B), 입장 뒤바꿈(C), 어디에도 없는 제3의 입장(D)으로 같은 문장 틀을 사용했다.
g.explanation:
정답 A: Kessler의 연구에서 neckteeth를 가진 개체는 포식자가 있을 때 생존율이 거의 두 배였다(보호 효과 지지). 하지만 포식자가 없을 때 성숙이 늦고 자손이 약 15% 적었다(무비용 주장 반박). 
B: 첫 번째 텍스트의 입장만 그대로 따른 오답이다. 번식 감소라는 결과를 무시했다. 
C: 두 판단을 뒤바꾼 오답이다. 보호 효과는 확인되었고, 비용이 있다는 점이 드러났다. 
D: 두 텍스트 모두 kairomone이 neckteeth 형성을 유도한다고 전제하며, 실험에서도 kairomone 처리 집단에서만 neckteeth가 생겼다. 따라서 어디에도 없는 제3의 입장이다.
g.explanation_en:
A is correct. In Kessler's study, Daphnia with neckteeth survived at nearly twice the rate when midges were present, which supports the claim that neckteeth protect them. But in predator-free tanks, those same Daphnia matured later and had about 15 percent fewer offspring. That result contradicts the idea that the defense is "cost-free."
B only repeats the first text's position and ignores the reproductive cost Kessler found.
C flips the two judgments: Kessler confirmed that neckteeth protect Daphnia and showed that they do carry a cost.
D invents a position that neither text takes. Both texts treat kairomones as the trigger for neckteeth, and in Kessler's experiment neckteeth formed only in the group exposed to kairomones.

c.instruction: 인물의 행동이나 진술에 표면적으로 드러나지 않는 의도나 태도를 짧은 지문으로 제시하고, 겉으로 말한 것과 실제 상황(또는 결과) 사이의 어긋남으로부터 함의를 추론하게 한다. 오답은 (1) 지문에 명시된 문장을 그대로 가져온 오답, (2) 어긋남을 반대로 해석한 오답, (3) 지문과 무관한 일반적 상식을 답으로 만든 오답으로 구성한다.
c.seed: life science — Pacific chorus frog explosive breeding synchronization and vernal pool reproductive habitat seasonal dependence

g.passage: Each winter, a team of herpetologists surveying a cluster of vernal pools in northern California reported that Pacific chorus frogs (Pseudacris regilla) at the site were thriving: on the first rainy nights of the season, hundreds of males gathered and called in near-perfect synchrony, and females laid thousands of eggs within a span of about ten days. The team's annual summary described this explosive breeding as "a reliable sign of a healthy population." Yet the same summaries also noted, almost in passing, that in four of the past six years the pools had dried out in early spring, weeks before tadpoles could complete metamorphosis, and that in those years few or no juvenile frogs were found leaving the pools.
g.question: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the team's characterization of the frog population?
options: It is supported by the team's observation that hundreds of males called in near-perfect synchrony on the first rainy nights of the season.
It may be overly optimistic, because the breeding activity it relies on does not by itself indicate that new frogs are actually being added to the population.
It may be overly pessimistic, because the early drying of the pools shows that the frogs have adapted to complete development more quickly than expected.
It reflects the general principle that amphibian populations are healthiest in habitats with permanent, year-round sources of water.
g.explanation:
정답 B: 연구팀은 동시 번식을 '건강한 개체군의 신호'라 했지만, 6년 중 4년은 웅덩이가 변태 전에 말라 어린 개구리가 거의 나오지 않았다. 번식 행동(산란)과 실제 개체 보충 사이의 어긋남으로 보아 그 평가는 지나치게 낙관적일 수 있다.
A: 지문에 나온 관찰을 그대로 가져왔을 뿐, 그 관찰이 결론을 뒷받침하지 못한다는 핵심 어긋남을 놓쳤다.
C: 어긋남을 반대로 해석했다. 어린 개구리가 거의 없었다는 것은 빠른 적응이 아니라 번식 실패를 보여 준다.
D: 영구 수원에 관한 일반 상식일 뿐 지문에 근거가 없다. 오히려 이 종은 계절성 웅덩이에서 번식한다.
g.explanation_en:
B is correct. The team calls the explosive breeding "a reliable sign of a healthy population," but its own summaries report that in four of the past six years the pools dried out before tadpoles could finish metamorphosis, and few or no juveniles came out. A lot of egg-laying doesn't show that new frogs are actually joining the population, so the team's verdict may be too optimistic.
A is wrong because it just repeats an observation from the text. It ignores that this observation doesn't support the team's conclusion.
C is wrong because it reads the mismatch backward. Few or no juveniles points to failed breeding, not to faster development.
D is wrong because it's a general claim about amphibians that the text never makes. In fact, these frogs breed in seasonal pools.
g.design: I set the team's stated judgment (synchronized breeding means a healthy population) against its own almost-in-passing note about recruitment failure. That gap is what students have to infer. The wrong answers cover three traps: repeating a statement from the text, reversing the gap, and offering general knowledge. All four choices start with the same "It ..." frame.

c.instruction: 지문에 하나의 넓은 주장과 그를 뒷받침하는 좁은 세부사실을 함께 제시하고, 지문 전체의 핵심 요지로 가장 적절한 범위의 진술을 고르게 한다. 오답은 (1) 세부사실 하나만을 전체 요지인 것처럼 과잉축소한 것, (2) 지문이 다루지 않은 범위까지 과잉확장한 것, (3) 넓은 주장과 세부사실을 뒤섞어 범위가 어긋난 것으로 구성한다.
c.seed: life science — Coqui frog direct development terrestrial egg-laying and parental care absence neotropical reproductive strategy

g.passage: Most frogs lay their eggs in water, where they hatch into swimming tadpoles that later turn into adults. The coqui frog of Puerto Rico skips that stage entirely. Females lay clutches of about two dozen eggs on land, often in curled leaves or the bases of bromeliads. Each embryo develops fully inside its egg, breathing through a thin tail full of blood vessels, and after roughly three weeks a tiny froglet breaks out using a temporary egg tooth. Because coquis do not need ponds or streams to breed, they avoid the fish and insect larvae that eat tadpoles, and they can reproduce far from standing water. Land, however, has its own dangers. Eggs laid out of water can dry out quickly, so a male coqui stays with each clutch for most of its development, pressing his moist body against the eggs and fending off egg-eating invertebrates. In experiments where researchers removed the guarding males, many clutches dried out or were eaten.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Coqui embryos get oxygen through a thin tail full of blood vessels while they develop inside their eggs.
Developing on land instead of in water has let tropical frogs give up their need for water and outcompete species that breed in ponds.
By skipping the aquatic tadpole stage, coqui frogs escape one set of reproductive risks but face a different one that they must actively manage.
Male coquis guard their eggs because, without a tadpole stage, the young would otherwise be eaten by fish and insect larvae.
g.explanation:
정답 C: 지문은 육상 직접발생 덕분에 물속 포식자를 피하고 물이 없는 곳에서도 번식할 수 있다는 이점을 먼저 제시한 뒤, 'however' 이후에는 알이 마르기 쉬워 수컷이 알을 지켜야 한다는 새로운 위험을 설명한다. 이 두 흐름을 모두 포괄하는 것이 C이다.
A(과잉축소): 꼬리로 호흡한다는 것은 발생 과정을 보여 주는 세부사실 하나일 뿐 전체 요지가 아니다.
B(과잉확장): 지문은 코키 한 종만 다루며, 열대 개구리 전반이나 연못 번식 종과의 경쟁은 언급하지 않는다. 또 알이 마를 위험이 있어 물기에 여전히 의존하므로 '물이 필요 없어졌다'는 말도 지문과 어긋난다.
D(범위 혼합): 넓은 주장(물속 포식자 회피)과 세부사실(수컷의 알 보호)을 잘못 연결했다. 수컷이 지키는 이유는 알의 건조와 알을 먹는 무척추동물 때문이며, 물고기나 곤충 유충은 코키가 피하는 위험이다.
g.explanation_en:
C is correct. The text first explains what coquis gain by developing on land: they avoid the fish and insect larvae that eat tadpoles, and they can breed away from water. Then, starting with "however," it describes a new danger. Eggs on land can dry out, so males have to guard them. C is the only choice that covers both halves of the text.
A narrows the scope too much. Breathing through the tail is just one detail about how the embryo develops.
B stretches the scope too far. The text is about one species, not tropical frogs in general, and it never compares coquis with pond-breeding frogs. Also, coqui eggs can still dry out, so the frogs haven't fully escaped their need for water.
D mixes up the broad claim and the details. Males guard the eggs to keep them from drying out and to drive off egg-eating invertebrates. Fish and insect larvae are the dangers the coquis avoid by breeding on land, not the reason males stand guard.
g.design: The text pairs a broad claim (direct development swaps the dangers of water for the dangers of land) with narrow details (tail breathing, egg tooth, males guarding the eggs). Each wrong answer has a different scope problem: A is too narrow, B goes too far, and D mixes the claim with the details incorrectly.

- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).

c.seed: life science — Soil nematode Caenorhabditis elegans programmed cell death and apoptosis genetic pathway model organism

g.passage: During its development, the tiny soil worm Caenorhabditis elegans produces 1,090 cells, but exactly 131 of them die on schedule before the worm reaches adulthood. Biologist H. Robert Horvitz found that a gene called ced-3 is required for these deaths: in worms with a working copy of ced-3, the 131 cells die as expected. A researcher studying a new strain of worms observes that all 131 of these cells survive into adulthood. Based on Horvitz's finding, the researcher can reasonably conclude that the worms in the new strain most likely ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: produce far fewer than 1,090 cells during development.
have an extra working copy of the ced-3 gene.
lose additional cells beyond the usual 131 before adulthood.
lack a working copy of the ced-3 gene.
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 131개 세포가 죽으려면 ced-3 유전자가 필요하다. 새 계통에서는 131개 세포가 모두 살아남았으므로, 그 계통에는 제대로 작동하는 ced-3가 없을 가능성이 가장 높다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 세포 생존과 관련이 없는 전체 세포 수 이야기이고, B는 ced-3가 작동하면 세포가 죽어야 하므로 관찰과 반대다. C는 세포가 더 많이 죽는다는 뜻이라 관찰 결과와 정반대다.
g.explanation_en: The text says ced-3 is required for the 131 cells to die. In the new strain, all 131 cells survive, so the most likely explanation is that these worms lack a working ced-3 gene, which makes D correct. A is about the total number of cells produced, which doesn't explain why the scheduled deaths didn't happen. B can't be right because a working ced-3 would cause the cells to die. C says even more cells die, which is the opposite of what the researcher observed.
g.design: 'ced-3가 있어야 세포가 죽는다'는 명시적 규칙 하나를 관찰에 적용하는 한 단계 추론. 오답은 같은 문장 틀로 원인과 결과를 뒤집거나 관련 없는 내용을 담았다.

c.seed: life science — Honey bee waggle dance navigation and solar compass directional communication symbolic language evolution

g.passage: When a honey bee worker returns to the hive after finding food, she often performs a "waggle dance" on the vertical surface of the honeycomb. The angle of her waggle run relative to straight up on the comb matches the angle between the food source and the sun's position in the sky. For example, a run pointing straight up tells other bees to fly directly toward the sun. Because the sun moves across the sky during the day, a researcher reasoned that if a bee danced for the same flower patch in the morning and again in the late afternoon, the angle of her waggle run would ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: shift between the two dances, since the direction of the food compared with the sun would have changed.
stay exactly the same between the two dances, since the flower patch itself would not have moved.
shift between the two dances, since bees in the hive would have forgotten the earlier dance by afternoon.
stay exactly the same between the two dances, since the dance shows only how far away the food is.
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 춤의 각도는 먹이 방향과 태양 위치 사이의 각도와 같다. 태양은 하루 동안 움직이므로, 꽃밭이 그대로여도 태양 기준 각도가 달라져 춤의 각도도 바뀐다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 각도가 태양 기준이라는 규칙을 무시하고 꽃밭이 고정된 것만 본다. C는 각도가 바뀐다는 결론은 맞지만 지문에 없는 '기억 상실'을 이유로 든다. D는 춤이 거리만 나타낸다고 하지만 지문은 춤의 각도가 방향을 전달한다고 설명한다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the angle of the waggle run matches the angle between the food and the sun. The sun moves during the day, so even though the flower patch stays put, the food's angle relative to the sun changes, and the dance angle changes with it. That makes A the answer. B ignores the rule that the angle is measured from the sun and looks only at the fact that the patch hasn't moved. C correctly says the angle shifts, but it gives a reason that's not in the passage: bees forgetting the earlier dance. D says the dance shows only distance, but the passage explains that the dance angle tells other bees which direction to fly.
g.design: Easy: one explicit rule (dance angle = food angle relative to sun) plus a stated fact (the sun moves) leads to a one-step inference. The wrong answers use the same sentence frame and reflect common misconceptions.

c.seed: earth and space science — Atmospheric river storms and atmospheric moisture transport mechanism intensifying precipitation events in California

g.passage: Atmospheric rivers are long, narrow corridors of water vapor that carry moisture from the tropical Pacific toward the West Coast of North America. A strong one can move more water than the Mississippi River discharges at its mouth. For years, forecasters judged how dangerous an incoming atmospheric river would be mainly by how much vapor it held. Research by meteorologist F. Martin Ralph and colleagues, however, suggests that the amount of moisture alone is a poor guide to how much rain falls in California. What matters more is how long the storm stays over one place and how sharply the region's mountains force the moist air upward, cooling it until the vapor condenses. A storm carrying only moderate moisture that stalls against the Sierra Nevada for two days can drop far more rain than a wetter storm that sweeps quickly past the coast.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Atmospheric rivers that reach California carry more water than the Mississippi River, making them the region's most dangerous storms.
The rainfall an atmospheric river brings to California depends less on its vapor content than on how long it lingers and how strongly terrain lifts its air.
Forecasters have stopped measuring the water vapor in atmospheric rivers because the Sierra Nevada blocks most storms from reaching the coast.
Atmospheric rivers that move quickly past the coast tend to carry more moisture than those that stall against the mountains.
g.explanation: 지문은 예보관들이 수증기 양을 기준으로 위험도를 판단해 왔지만, 실제 강수량은 폭풍의 체류 시간과 산지에 의한 상승 정도에 더 좌우된다고 주장하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 미시시피강 비교라는 세부를 사용하지만, 지문은 수분량만으로 위험도를 판단할 수 없다고 말하므로 핵심과 반대된다. C는 산맥을 언급하지만 측정 중단이나 해안 차단은 지문에 없는 내용이다. D는 마지막 예시를 일반화한 것으로, 지문은 빠른 폭풍이 일반적으로 수분이 더 많다고 주장하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct because the text argues that forecasters long judged danger by vapor content, but California's rainfall depends more on how long a storm stays in place and how strongly the mountains lift its air. A takes the Mississippi comparison, which is just a detail, and draws a conclusion the text actually argues against, since moisture alone doesn't determine danger. C mentions the mountains, but the text never says forecasters stopped measuring vapor or that the mountains keep storms from reaching the coast. D turns the final example into a general rule, and the text never claims that fast-moving storms usually carry more moisture.
g.design: To answer, you have to connect the old view (judging storms by vapor) with the new finding (how long a storm stays and how much the terrain lifts it), and the correct answer paraphrases this instead of copying it. Wrong answers A and D each build on a real detail from the text (the Mississippi comparison and the final example) but distort it.

c.seed: earth and space science — Lunar laser ranging measurement and Earth's moon orbital recession rate quantifying tidal friction effects

g.passage: Since astronauts left retroreflectors on the lunar surface during the Apollo missions, observatories have fired laser pulses at them and timed the light's round trip. These measurements reveal that the Moon is drifting away from Earth by roughly 3.8 centimeters per year. Many people assume this drift is simply a leftover from the Moon's formation, but researchers trace it to an ongoing exchange between the two bodies. The Moon's gravity raises tidal bulges in Earth's oceans, and because Earth rotates faster than the Moon orbits, friction drags those bulges slightly ahead of the Moon. The bulges in turn pull the Moon forward, boosting its orbital energy while gradually slowing Earth's spin. The laser data thus do more than track distance: they let scientists calculate how much rotational energy tidal friction removes from Earth today, a figure that can be compared with growth bands in ancient corals and sediments recording how long days once were.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Laser timing has shown that the Moon is moving away from Earth at a rate that has stayed fixed since the Moon first formed.
Laser timing has shown that ocean tides on Earth are mainly controlled by the speed of Earth's rotation rather than by the Moon's gravity.
Laser timing of the Moon's slow retreat lets scientists measure the present-day effect of a tidal interaction that is also slowing Earth's rotation.
Laser timing of the Moon's retreat has replaced the need to study ancient corals and sediments as records of past day length.
g.explanation: 지문은 레이저 측정으로 달이 연 3.8cm씩 멀어진다는 사실을 밝히고, 이것이 조석 마찰로 인한 에너지 교환의 결과이며 이를 통해 현재 지구 자전에서 빠지는 에너지를 계산할 수 있다고 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 지문이 반박하는 '형성의 잔재' 가정과 같고, 속도가 일정했다는 내용도 없다. B는 조석 팽대부를 일으키는 것이 달의 중력이라는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D는 고대 산호·퇴적물이 비교 대상으로 쓰인다는 지문과 달리 '대체'했다고 왜곡한다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that laser measurements show the Moon receding about 3.8 cm per year, traces this to tidal friction that transfers energy from Earth's spin to the Moon's orbit, and notes that the data let scientists calculate today's energy loss. That makes C correct. A repeats the "leftover from formation" assumption the text rejects, and the text never says the rate has stayed fixed. B contradicts the text, which says the Moon's gravity raises the tidal bulges. D distorts the ending: the corals and sediments are used for comparison, not replaced.
g.design: 정답은 레이저 측정과 조석 마찰 기제 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 오답은 모두 'Laser timing...'이라는 같은 문장 틀을 쓰고, 지문에 나온 세부(형성, 조석, 산호)를 일부 담고 있지만 왜곡되어 있다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Permafrost methane release and positive feedback amplification accelerating Arctic climate warming cycle

g.passage:
For decades, climate models treated Arctic permafrost largely as a passive store of carbon, frozen soil that would thaw gradually and release its methane and carbon dioxide at a slow, predictable pace. Field research led by ecologist Merritt Turetsky has complicated that picture. Her team found that in ice-rich permafrost, thawing does not simply proceed downward a few centimeters each year; instead, melting ground ice can cause the land surface to collapse abruptly, forming slumps and ponds known as thermokarst. These waterlogged depressions create oxygen-poor conditions in which microbes produce methane, a greenhouse gas far more potent than carbon dioxide over short periods.

Because the warming caused by this methane can in turn thaw more permafrost, abrupt thaw strengthens a feedback loop that models built around gradual thaw tend to underestimate. Turetsky and her colleagues estimate that although abrupt thaw is likely to affect less than a fifth of the permafrost region, it could roughly double the climate impact projected from gradual thaw alone. Their conclusion is not that the Arctic has already passed a point of no return, but that projections ignoring sudden ground collapse may substantially understate how much permafrost will contribute to future warming.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because thermokarst ponds lack oxygen, microbes in permafrost regions now emit more methane than carbon dioxide, making methane the main driver of Arctic warming.
Because abrupt thaw affects less than a fifth of the permafrost region, its contribution to Arctic warming is likely to remain minor compared with that of gradual thaw.
Because permafrost has begun collapsing abruptly, the Arctic has likely passed a point beyond which further warming cannot be prevented.
Because sudden ground collapse can intensify a self-reinforcing cycle of thaw and warming, models assuming only slow thaw probably underestimate permafrost's climate effect.
g.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 얼음이 많은 영구동토층의 급격한 붕괴(thermokarst)가 메탄 방출을 늘려 되먹임 고리를 강화하므로, 점진적 해빙만 가정한 모델이 영구동토층의 기후 영향을 과소평가한다는 것이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 산소 부족 환경에서 메탄이 생성된다는 세부는 맞지만, 메탄이 이산화탄소보다 많이 배출된다거나 북극 온난화의 주된 원인이라는 주장은 지문에 없다. B는 '5분의 1 미만'이라는 수치를 인용하지만, 지문은 그럼에도 영향이 약 두 배가 될 수 있다고 하므로 결론이 반대이다. C는 지문이 명시적으로 부정한 '돌이킬 수 없는 지점'을 주장하므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The text's central point is that abrupt collapse of ice-rich permafrost (thermokarst) boosts methane release and strengthens a feedback loop, so models that assume only gradual thaw likely understate permafrost's contribution to warming. That makes D correct. A gets the detail about oxygen-poor ponds producing methane right, but the text never says methane emissions exceed carbon dioxide emissions or that methane is the main driver of Arctic warming. B cites the "less than a fifth" figure but reaches the opposite conclusion, since the text says abrupt thaw could roughly double the projected impact. C claims a point of no return has been passed, which the text explicitly says is not the researchers' conclusion.
g.design: Each wrong choice is built from a real detail (oxygen-poor ponds, the one-fifth figure, abrupt collapse) but draws a conclusion the text doesn't support. To get it right, you have to connect the feedback mechanism to the researchers' limited conclusion about model underestimation. All four choices use the same "Because..., ..." structure.
