c.seed: earth and space science — Plate tectonics subduction zone megathrust earthquakes and tsunami generation in Cascadia Subduction Zone

g.passage: For much of the twentieth century, geologists considered the Cascadia Subduction Zone, where the Juan de Fuca Plate slides beneath North America off the coast of the Pacific Northwest, to be relatively harmless. Unlike subduction zones in Japan or Chile, it had produced no large earthquakes in recorded history, and some researchers proposed that the plates were slipping past each other smoothly rather than locking and building strain. In the 1980s, however, geologist Brian Atwater found buried marsh soils along Washington's coast covered by layers of tsunami-deposited sand, along with "ghost forests" of cedars that had died when the land suddenly dropped. Tree-ring dating showed that these trees died between 1699 and 1700. Researchers later matched this timing to Japanese records of an "orphan tsunami" that struck in January 1700 with no local earthquake to explain it. Taken together, the evidence showed that Cascadia's quiet history reflected the long gaps between its ruptures, not an absence of danger: the fault had generated a magnitude 9 earthquake only about three centuries earlier.
g.question: According to the text, what did the combined geological and historical evidence reveal about the Cascadia Subduction Zone?
options: Its lack of recorded large earthquakes was misleading, because it had in fact produced a massive earthquake around 1700.
Its plates were slipping past each other smoothly, which explained why no large earthquakes had been recorded there.
Its earthquakes were less powerful than those in Japan, which is why its 1700 tsunami was noticed only overseas.
Its coastline had been dropping gradually for centuries, slowly burying marsh soils and killing coastal cedar forests.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 연대를 알려주는 나무 나이테 증거와 일본 기록을 연결하고, 마지막 문장에서 '조용한 역사'를 다시 해석한 부분까지 읽어야 한다. 오답 B, C, D는 각각 지문의 실제 세부(과거 가설, 일본, 고스트 포레스트)를 가져와 틀리게 비틀었다.
g.explanation: 지문은 매몰된 습지 토양, 고스트 포레스트의 나이테 연대(1699~1700년), 그리고 1700년 일본의 '고아 쓰나미' 기록을 함께 놓고 보면 캐스케이디아의 조용한 역사가 위험이 없다는 뜻이 아니었으며 약 300년 전에 규모 9 지진이 있었다고 결론 내리므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일부 연구자들이 내놓았다가 이 증거로 뒤집힌 옛 가설이다. C는 일본을 언급하지만 지진은 규모 9였고, 지문은 캐스케이디아 지진이 더 약했다고 말하지 않는다. D는 땅이 '갑자기' 내려앉았다는 지문 내용과 반대로 점진적 침하를 주장한다.
g.explanation_en: A is correct. The text combines the buried marsh soils, the tree-ring dates for the ghost forests (1699–1700), and Japan's record of an "orphan tsunami" in 1700 to conclude that Cascadia's quiet history didn't mean it was safe, since it had produced a magnitude 9 earthquake about three centuries earlier. B is the old hypothesis that some researchers proposed, and this evidence overturned it. C mentions Japan, but the earthquake was magnitude 9, and the text never says Cascadia's earthquakes are weaker. D contradicts the text, which says the land dropped suddenly rather than gradually.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Ocean acidification and pteropod shell dissolution affecting marine food webs in Southern Ocean

g.passage: Pteropods, tiny swimming snails sometimes called "sea butterflies," build delicate shells of aragonite, a form of calcium carbonate. As the ocean absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, seawater becomes more acidic and holds fewer of the carbonate ions that aragonite requires. Cold water absorbs carbon dioxide especially readily, so the Southern Ocean around Antarctica is among the first regions where surface waters are expected to become corrosive to aragonite. In 2012, researchers led by Nina Bednaršek collected pteropods from waters near South Georgia where carbonate levels had dropped, and under electron microscopes the animals' shells showed pitting and thinning. Researchers caution that the stakes extend beyond the snails themselves. In parts of the Southern Ocean, pteropods are a major food source for krill, small fish, and seabirds, and some of these predators are in turn eaten by penguins, seals, and whales. Because so many species depend directly or indirectly on pteropods, damage to their shells could ripple outward through the region's food web.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because cold water absorbs carbon dioxide readily, the Southern Ocean has already become more acidic than any other ocean region on Earth.
Rising acidity is beginning to weaken the shells of a small Southern Ocean animal, which raises concern for the many species that rely on it.
Rising acidity has forced Southern Ocean predators such as penguins and whales to replace pteropods with other prey.
Electron microscopes have allowed researchers to show that pteropods can repair shell damage caused by changes in seawater chemistry.
g.explanation: 지문은 산성화로 익족류 껍데기가 얇아지고 있다는 증거를 제시한 뒤, 익족류에 의존하는 먹이그물 전체로 영향이 퍼질 수 있다는 우려로 연결하므로 두 내용을 모두 담은 B가 정답이다. A는 차가운 물이 CO2를 잘 흡수한다는 세부 내용을 '이미 가장 산성'이라는 단정으로 과장했다. 지문은 이 지역이 '가장 먼저 그렇게 될 것으로 예상되는' 곳 중 하나라고만 말한다. C는 포식자들을 언급하지만 먹이 대체는 지문에 없으며, 영향은 '일어날 수 있다'고 했을 뿐이다. D는 전자현미경을 언급하지만 지문이 보여 준 것은 손상이지 회복이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The text first presents evidence that rising acidity is pitting and thinning pteropod shells, then explains that this could spread through the food web because so many species depend on pteropods. B is correct because it covers both parts. A takes a detail about cold water and turns it into an overstatement: the text only says the Southern Ocean is among the first places expected to become corrosive, not that it is already the most acidic. C mentions the predators, but the text never says they have switched to other prey; it only says the effects could spread. D mentions electron microscopes, but they revealed damage, not repair.
g.design: 정답은 산성화 증거와 먹이그물 영향을 연결해야 고를 수 있게 했다. 오답 A, C, D는 지문의 실제 세부 내용(차가운 물, 포식자, 현미경)을 하나씩 가져와 왜곡했고, 모두 정답과 같은 문장 틀을 따른다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Magnetic field reversal records in volcanic basalt columns documenting geomagnetic polarity timescale

g.passage: When lava cools into basalt, tiny grains of magnetite inside the rock lock in the direction of Earth's magnetic field at that moment. In the mid-twentieth century, geologists sampling stacked lava flows in places such as Iceland and Hawaii noticed that some layers recorded a field pointing roughly north, as it does today, while others recorded one pointing south. At first, some researchers suspected that certain minerals simply magnetized themselves backward as they cooled, a chemical quirk unrelated to the planet's field. That explanation weakened when scientists dated the flows using the slow decay of radioactive potassium into argon. Rocks of the same age from distant continents turned out to share the same polarity, and reversed layers did not consistently contain a different mix of minerals than normal ones. By matching polarity to age across many sites, researchers assembled a timeline of alternating normal and reversed intervals—the geomagnetic polarity timescale—which later helped confirm that the seafloor spreads outward from mid-ocean ridges.
g.question: According to the text, what led researchers to doubt that reversed magnetization in basalt was caused by a chemical quirk of certain minerals?
options: Basalt layers from Iceland and Hawaii showed that reversed layers formed only in lava that cooled especially slowly.
Basalt layers that recorded a southward field turned out to be much older than layers that recorded a northward field.
Basalt layers of matching age from widely separated locations shared a polarity, and reversed layers were not mineralogically distinct.
Basalt layers dated by potassium-argon decay showed that magnetite grains lose their recorded direction over time.
g.explanation: 지문은 연대 측정 결과 멀리 떨어진 대륙의 같은 나이 암석이 같은 극성을 보였고, 역전된 층이 정상 층과 광물 구성이 일관되게 다르지 않았다고 말하므로 정답은 C이다. A는 아이슬란드·하와이라는 실제 지명을 쓰지만 냉각 속도는 지문에 언급되지 않는다. B는 극성과 나이를 연결한다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 정상·역전 구간이 번갈아 나타난다고 할 뿐 역전 층이 더 오래되었다고 하지 않는다. D는 칼륨-아르곤 연대 측정을 언급하지만, 자철석이 기록된 방향을 잃는다는 내용은 지문에 없고 오히려 방향을 고정한다고 설명한다.
g.explanation_en: The correct answer is C. The text says that once the flows were dated, rocks of the same age from distant continents had the same polarity, and reversed layers did not consistently contain a different mix of minerals than normal ones. A names real sampling sites from the text, but the text never mentions how fast the lava cooled. B sounds reasonable because it links polarity to age, but the text describes normal and reversed intervals alternating over time, not reversed layers being older. D mentions potassium-argon dating, but the text says magnetite locks in the field direction, not that the grains lose it over time.
g.design: 세부 정보를 묻는 문항으로, 근거가 되는 두 단서(같은 나이 암석의 극성 일치, 광물 구성 차이 없음)를 연결해야 한다. 오답 A, B, D는 지문에 나오는 지명, 연대-극성 관계, 칼륨-아르곤 연대 측정을 각각 끌어와 부분적으로 그럴듯하게 만들었다.

c.instruction: 노트에 연구 결과를 설명하는 확정적 진술과 통계적/잠정적 진술이 함께 제시된 상황에서, 주어진 목표에 맞는 확실성 수준의 문장을 선택하는 문제를 만들어라. 오답은 각각 (1) 잠정적 결과를 확정적으로 과장한 문장, (2) 확정적 사실을 불필요하게 잠정적으로 축소한 문장, (3) 확실성 수준은 맞지만 다른 연구 내용과 혼동한 문장으로 구성하라.
c.seed: earth and space science — Thermohaline circulation shutdown and Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation collapse risk assessment models

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a system of ocean currents that carries warm surface water northward and returns cold, dense water southward at depth.
- Direct measurements from the RAPID instrument array show that the AMOC's average strength from 2004 to 2012 was lower than its average from 2004 to 2008.
- In a 2023 statistical analysis of sea-surface temperature records, Peter and Susanne Ditlevsen estimated that the AMOC could collapse sometime between 2025 and 2095.
- They reported this range with 95 percent confidence and noted that it depends on assumptions about how early-warning signals behave.
- A separate modeling study by René van Westen and colleagues found that a collapse, if it occurred, would cool northwestern Europe by several degrees Celsius per decade.
g.question: The student wants to present the Ditlevsens' finding with the degree of confidence the researchers themselves attached to it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: According to Peter and Susanne Ditlevsen's 2023 analysis, the AMOC will collapse between 2025 and 2095, an outcome their sea-surface temperature records establish.
According to RAPID array data, the AMOC may possibly have been weaker from 2004 to 2012 than from 2004 to 2008, though this decline remains a tentative estimate.
According to Peter and Susanne Ditlevsen's 2023 analysis, an AMOC collapse, if it occurred, would likely cool northwestern Europe by several degrees Celsius per decade.

According to Peter and Susanne Ditlevsen's 2023 analysis, the AMOC could collapse between 2025 and 2095, an estimate given at 95 percent confidence and resting on assumptions about early-warning signals.
g.explanation: 정답 D: 디틀레우센 부부의 결과는 'could', 95% 신뢰구간, 조기경보 신호에 대한 가정 의존이라는 잠정적 성격을 지닌다. D는 이 확실성 수준을 그대로 전달한다. A: 'will collapse', 'establish'라고 써서 잠정적 추정을 확정된 사실처럼 과장했다. B: RAPID 관측 자료는 직접 측정한 확정적 사실인데 'may possibly', 'tentative'를 붙여 불필요하게 약화했고, 디틀레우센 연구 내용도 아니다. C: 조건부·잠정적 어조는 맞지만, 유럽 냉각 결과는 반 베스턴 연구진의 연구이므로 디틀레우센 연구로 잘못 귀속했다.
g.explanation_en: D is correct. The Ditlevsens' result is tentative: the collapse "could" happen, the range comes with 95 percent confidence, and it depends on assumptions about early-warning signals. D keeps all of these qualifications. A turns the estimate into a certainty by saying the AMOC "will" collapse and that the records "establish" it, which overstates the finding. B hedges something that was actually measured: the RAPID array directly recorded the weaker AMOC, so calling it "possibly" true and "tentative" understates it. B also isn't about the Ditlevsens. C uses the right cautious tone, but the cooling of Europe comes from van Westen and colleagues' study, not from the Ditlevsens' work.
g.design: I paired a measured fact (RAPID data) with a probabilistic estimate (the Ditlevsens' 95% confidence range). Each wrong answer matches one of the three traps in the recipe: overstating the estimate, hedging the measured fact, and pinning another study's result on the Ditlevsens with the right level of caution. I didn't use the words "could" or "95 percent" in the question.

c.instruction: 노트에 제시된 서로 다른 두 개의 사실(예: 각각 다른 대상/사건/수치에 대한 독립된 정보)을 하나의 문장으로 자연스럽게 결합하여 주어진 목표(예: 두 대상을 비교하거나 관계를 설명)를 달성하는 문제를 만들어라. 오답은 각각 (1) 한쪽 사실만 담아 목표를 절반만 달성, (2) 두 사실을 결합했지만 목표와 무관한 조합, (3) 노트에 없는 내용을 추가해 사실을 왜곡한 문장으로 구성하라.
c.seed: earth and space science — Volcanic stratospheric aerosols and solar radiation dimming effects on global temperature anomalies

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Large volcanic eruptions can inject sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, where it forms sulfate aerosols that reflect incoming sunlight.
- The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines released about 15 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere.
- In the year after Pinatubo erupted, average global surface temperature fell by roughly 0.5°C.
- The 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens in Washington State released about 1 million tons of sulfur dioxide, much of it into the lower atmosphere.
- Mount St. Helens produced no measurable drop in average global surface temperature.
g.question: The student wants to suggest why two eruptions had different effects on the planet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Mount Pinatubo sent about 15 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere and was followed by a global cooling of roughly 0.5°C, whereas Mount St. Helens released only about 1 million tons, largely into the lower atmosphere, and caused no measurable global cooling.
Mount Pinatubo sent about 15 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, where it formed sulfate aerosols, and was followed by a global cooling of roughly 0.5°C in the following year.
Mount Pinatubo erupted in the Philippines in 1991, whereas Mount St. Helens erupted in Washington State in 1980, about eleven years earlier.

Mount Pinatubo sent about 15 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere and cooled the planet by roughly 0.5°C for a decade, whereas Mount St. Helens released about 1 million tons and slightly warmed the planet.
g.explanation: 정답 A: 두 화산의 이산화황 양·주입 고도(원인)와 기온 영향(결과)을 대조해 효과 차이의 이유를 제시한다. B: 피나투보 한쪽 사실만 담아 비교가 없으므로 목표의 절반만 달성한다. C: 두 분화를 결합했지만 장소·연도만 대조해 효과 차이의 이유와 무관하다. D: '10년간 냉각', '약간의 온난화'는 노트에 없는 내용으로 사실을 왜곡한다(노트는 이듬해 0.5°C 하강, 측정 가능한 변화 없음).
g.explanation_en: A is correct: it contrasts the two eruptions' sulfur dioxide amounts and injection heights (the likely cause) with their temperature effects (the result), suggesting why the outcomes differed. B covers only Pinatubo, so with no comparison it accomplishes only half the goal. C combines both eruptions but contrasts only location and date, which does not explain the different effects. D adds claims not in the notes: a decade of cooling and slight warming. The notes say the cooling happened in the year after the eruption and that St. Helens caused no measurable change.
g.design: 독립된 두 분화 사실을 원인-결과 대조로 결합해야 하며, 질문은 'different effects'로만 표현해 정답 문구와 겹치지 않게 했다. 오답은 한쪽만 다룬 문장, 목표와 무관한 결합, 노트에 없는 내용을 넣은 왜곡으로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 학생이 주어진 하나의 수사적 목표(강조하기, 개관하기, 소개하기 중 하나)를 달성하기 위해 노트의 여러 항목 중 어느 것을 포함해야 하는지 판단하는 문제를 만들어라. 오답은 각각 (1) 목표보다 지나치게 세부적인 정보만 담은 문장, (2) 목표보다 지나치게 포괄적이라 초점을 잃은 문장, (3) 목표와 무관한 다른 항목을 강조한 문장으로 구성하라.
c.seed: earth and space science — Soil carbon sequestration in prairie ecosystems and long-term carbon storage potential climate mitigation

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tallgrass prairie plants such as big bluestem can grow roots reaching more than 3 meters deep.
- Much of the carbon these plants absorb is moved underground into roots and soil rather than kept in leaves and stems.
- Carbon held deep in prairie soil can remain there for centuries, whereas carbon in aboveground plant matter is often released within a few years through decay or fire.
- Because of this durable underground storage, some climate researchers view prairie restoration as a promising way to help offset greenhouse gas emissions.
- Prairies also provide habitat for pollinators such as bees and butterflies.
- Restored prairie plots at Minnesota's Cedar Creek research station have been monitored for several decades.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize why prairies matter for addressing climate change. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Tallgrass prairie plants such as big bluestem can send roots more than 3 meters into the ground, deeper than many other grassland species.
By locking absorbed carbon deep in the soil for centuries rather than releasing it within a few years, prairies offer a durable way to help offset greenhouse gas emissions.
Prairies are complex ecosystems with deep-rooted plants, pollinator habitat, long-studied research plots, and soils that hold carbon.
Beyond their role in the soil, restored prairies provide valuable habitat for pollinators such as bees and butterflies.
g.explanation:
정답 B: 기후 변화 대응에서 프레리가 중요한 이유를 강조하려면 탄소가 토양 깊이 수 세기 동안 저장된다는 점(지상부는 수년 내 방출)과 그 결과 온실가스 상쇄에 도움이 된다는 점을 연결해야 한다. B만 이 인과를 담는다.
A(지나치게 세부적): 뿌리 깊이라는 세부 사실만 제시하고 탄소 저장이나 기후와의 연결이 없다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 여러 항목을 나열한 개관이라 기후 측면의 중요성을 강조하지 못하고 초점이 흐려진다.
D(무관한 항목 강조): 수분 매개자 서식지는 기후 완화와 무관한 생태적 가치다.
g.explanation_en:
B is correct. To emphasize why prairies matter for climate change, a sentence has to connect long-lasting carbon storage (deep soil carbon stays for centuries, while aboveground carbon is released within a few years) to the climate benefit of offsetting emissions. B is the only choice that makes this connection.
A is too narrow. It gives only the root-depth detail and never links it to carbon or climate.
C is too broad. It lists many features like an overview, so the climate point gets lost.
D focuses on a note that doesn't serve the goal. Pollinator habitat is an ecological benefit, but it has nothing to do with climate mitigation.
g.design: For the goal of emphasizing, the student has to choose which notes to combine. Each wrong answer misses in a different way: one gives only a narrow detail (root depth), one is so broad it loses focus (a list of every note), and one stresses an unrelated note (pollinators). The question avoids key words from the correct answer, such as "carbon," "soil," and "offset."

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Microseismicity swarms and induced seismicity from hydraulic fracturing operations in shale gas extraction

g.passage: When companies extract natural gas from shale, they often use hydraulic fracturing: water is pumped underground at high pressure to crack the rock and release the gas. This process produces thousands of tiny earthquakes, called microseismic events, that are far too weak for people to feel. Geologists in western Canada studied records from several fracturing sites and found that, in a small number of cases, these swarms of tiny quakes were followed by larger earthquakes strong enough to be felt at the surface. The researchers concluded that the larger quakes happened mainly where the injected fluid reached faults that were already under stress, which suggests that companies could reduce the risk by mapping such faults before choosing where to drill.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Hydraulic fracturing usually causes earthquakes strong enough to be felt, so it should not be used anywhere in western Canada.
Microseismic events are too weak to detect, so researchers cannot tell whether fracturing affects the ground.
Fracturing occasionally leads to noticeable earthquakes, mostly where fluid reaches stressed faults, so locating those faults may lower the danger.
Shale gas is released mainly by natural earthquakes, so fracturing adds little to the amount of gas companies collect.
g.explanation: 지문은 수압 파쇄가 작은 미소지진을 일으키지만, 드물게 이미 응력을 받은 단층에 유체가 닿으면 느낄 수 있는 지진이 발생하며, 단층을 미리 파악하면 위험을 줄일 수 있다고 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '드물게(a small number of cases)'를 '대개'로 바꾸고 전면 금지라는 지문에 없는 결론을 덧붙였다. B는 미소지진이 사람이 느끼기엔 약할 뿐 연구자들이 기록을 분석했다는 내용과 모순된다. D는 가스가 자연 지진으로 방출된다는, 지문에 없는 주장이다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that fracturing causes tiny quakes, that only in a few cases larger felt quakes followed, mostly where fluid reached already-stressed faults, and that mapping those faults could reduce risk, so C is correct. A changes "a small number of cases" into "usually" and adds a ban the text never proposes. B contradicts the text, since the quakes are only too weak for people to feel—researchers did study their records. D makes a claim about natural earthquakes releasing gas that the text never makes.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도에 맞게 지문의 결론 문장에 단서를 직접 드러냈다. 오답은 과잉일반화, 세부 내용 오독, 지문에 없는 주장이라는 전형적 오류로 만들었고, 네 선택지 모두 같은 'X, so Y' 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Atmospheric dispersion modeling of volcanic ash columns and tephra deposition distance predictions

g.passage: When a volcano erupts explosively, it sends a tall column of ash into the sky. Scientists use computer programs called dispersion models to predict where that ash will travel and how far from the volcano it will fall to the ground. These models combine information about the height of the ash column, the size of the ash particles, and the speed and direction of the wind at different altitudes. Large, heavy particles tend to drop out close to the volcano, while fine particles can be carried hundreds of kilometers away. By running these models, scientists can warn airports, farms, and towns about where ash is likely to land, giving people time to prepare.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Scientists have found that wind speed matters more than particle size when ash falls near a volcano.
Scientists have shown that explosive eruptions produce taller ash columns than other kinds of eruptions.
Scientists have learned that fine ash particles are more harmful to farms than large particles are.
Scientists use models built from eruption and weather data to forecast where volcanic ash will settle.
g.explanation: 지문 전체는 과학자들이 기둥 높이, 입자 크기, 바람 정보를 결합한 분산 모델로 화산재가 어디에 떨어질지 예측하고 경고한다는 내용이므로 D가 중심 내용이다. A는 바람과 입자 크기의 중요도를 비교하지만 지문에는 그런 비교가 없다. B는 분출 유형 간 기둥 높이 비교로, 지문에서 언급되지 않는다. C는 입자 크기별 피해 정도를 말하지만 지문은 이동 거리만 설명한다.
g.explanation_en: The whole text explains that scientists combine column height, particle size, and wind data in dispersion models to predict where ash will land and to warn people, so D states the main idea. A compares the importance of wind and particle size, but the text never makes that comparison. B compares column heights across eruption types, which the text doesn't discuss. C claims fine ash harms farms more, but the text only describes how far different particles travel, not how harmful they are.
g.design: Easy: a single explicit main idea is spread across the paragraph; distractors use the same "Scientists have..." frame and mention details from the text but add unsupported comparisons.

c.instruction: 인용문(따옴표 안 문장)과 이를 감싸는 주절, 혹은 병렬로 나열된 여러 절을 함께 제시하고 그 전체에 걸쳐 시제나 형태가 일관되어야 하는 문장을 만들어라. 정답은 인용문/병렬구조 전체 맥락과 시제가 일치하는 형태이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 인용문 시제와 어긋나는 시제 선택, (2) 병렬 구조 중 한 항목만 다른 시제/형태로 만든 것, (3) 문장 내 한 절과는 맞지만 전체 문맥과는 어긋나는 시제를 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: earth and space science — Karst cave system formation and limestone dissolution by carbonic acid in groundwater chemistry

g.passage: In a 2019 field report on the Mammoth Cave system, hydrogeologist Ellen Marsh described how slightly acidic groundwater shapes limestone over geologic time. "Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide as it seeps through the soil," she wrote, "and the resulting carbonic acid ______ calcite along cracks in the bedrock, gradually widening them into passages large enough for a person to walk through."
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: dissolves
dissolved
dissolving
had dissolved
g.explanation: 정답 A: 인용문 안에서 Marsh는 지금도 반복되는 일반적 과정을 현재 시제로 설명한다("absorbs," "seeps"). 'and'로 이어진 두 번째 독립절의 동사도 이와 맞춰 현재 시제 "dissolves"가 되어야 한다. B "dissolved"는 인용문을 둘러싼 주절의 과거 시제("described," "wrote")에만 맞춘 것이다. 그런데 인용문 안의 시제는 인용문 내부 문맥을 따라야 한다. C "dissolving"은 분사여서 주어 "the resulting carbonic acid"에 붙는 정동사가 없어지므로 병렬 구조 가운데 한 항목만 형태가 달라진다. D "had dissolved"(과거완료)는 'wrote'보다 앞선 일로 해석하면 주절과만 어울린다. 하지만 인용문의 현재 시제 일반 진술과 맞지 않고, 뒤에 오는 "gradually widening"이 나타내는 지속적 과정과도 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: Choice A is correct. Inside the quotation, Marsh describes a general process that keeps happening, and she uses the present tense to do it ("absorbs," "seeps"). The second independent clause joined by "and" needs a matching present-tense verb, so "dissolves" is right. Choice B, "dissolved," only matches the past-tense verbs in the frame around the quotation ("described," "wrote"). The tense inside a quotation follows the context of the quotation itself. Choice C, "dissolving," is a participle, so the subject "the resulting carbonic acid" would have no finite verb. That makes one item in the parallel structure a different form from the others. Choice D, "had dissolved," could fit "wrote" if you read it as something that happened earlier. But it clashes with the present-tense general statement in the quotation and with the ongoing process shown by "gradually widening."
g.design: 이 문항은 과거 시제로 된 주절 안에 현재 시제로 된 인용문을 넣었고, 인용문 안에는 두 절을 병렬로 배치했다. 오답 B는 인용문 시제와 어긋나는 선택이고, C는 병렬 구조 중 한 항목만 형태를 다르게 만든 것이며, D는 주절과는 맞지만 전체 문맥과는 맞지 않는 과거완료이다.

c.instruction: 문장 앞부분에 분사구문(예: ~ing, having p.p., ~ed로 시작하는 수식어구)을 배치하고, 그 수식어구가 실제로 가리키는 행위자가 문장 중간이나 뒤쪽 명사구에 숨어 있도록 지문을 구성하라. 정답은 그 행위자를 주어 자리에 정확히 배치한 문장이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어구와 표면상 가장 가까운 무생물 명사를 주어로 착각, (2) 문장 앞부분의 배경 명사를 주어로 착각, (3) 수식어구가 가리키는 행위자와 문법적으로만 비슷한 다른 인물/사물을 주어로 착각하여 만들어라.
c.seed: earth and space science — Auroral substorm magnetosphere dynamics and Kp index measurement of geomagnetic disturbance intensity

g.passage: In March 1989, an intense geomagnetic storm collapsed the power grid of the Canadian province of Quebec within about ninety seconds. Analyzing ground magnetometer records from that night decades later, ______ that the planetary Kp index, which rates global geomagnetic disturbance on a scale from 0 to 9, had reached its maximum value as a series of auroral substorms suddenly released energy stored in Earth's magnetotail.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the magnetometer data revealed to geophysicist Ana Ruiz
geophysicist Ana Ruiz confirmed
the 1989 storm was shown by geophysicist Ana Ruiz
the work of geophysicist Ana Ruiz established
g.explanation:
분사구문 'Analyzing ground magnetometer records...'의 의미상 주어, 즉 기록을 분석한 사람이 주절의 주어로 바로 와야 한다. 기록을 분석할 수 있는 행위자는 지구물리학자 Ana Ruiz뿐이므로 그녀를 주어로 둔 B가 정답이다.
A: 수식어구 바로 근처에 있는 무생물 명사(magnetometer records/data)를 주어로 삼았다. 그러면 데이터가 스스로 기록을 분석한 셈이 되므로 현수 수식어 오류다. Ruiz는 전치사 to의 목적어 자리에 묻혀 있다.
C: 앞 문장의 배경 명사(1989년 폭풍)를 주어로 삼았다. 폭풍은 기록을 분석할 수 없으며, 수동태 때문에 행위자가 by구 뒤로 밀려났다.
D: 행위자와 비슷해 보이는 'the work of ... Ruiz'를 주어로 삼았다. 문법상 주어는 사람이 아니라 work이므로, 연구 결과물이 분석을 한 꼴이 되어 여전히 현수 수식어 오류다.
g.explanation_en:
An introductory participial phrase has to describe the subject that comes right after it. The phrase "Analyzing ground magnetometer records..." describes someone doing the analyzing, and only the geophysicist Ana Ruiz can do that. Choice B puts her in the subject position, so B is correct.
A: This makes "the magnetometer data" the subject, because it is the nonliving noun closest to the modifier. Data can't analyze records, so the modifier dangles. Ruiz is buried as the object of "to."
C: This makes the background noun "the 1989 storm" the subject. A storm can't analyze records either, and the passive voice pushes the real actor into a "by" phrase.
D: "The work of geophysicist Ana Ruiz" looks like it names the actor, but the grammatical subject is "work," not Ruiz. Work can't analyze anything, so the modifier still dangles.
g.design: I opened the sentence with a participial phrase and placed the real actor (Ruiz) where she could be mistaken for a part of the noun phrase inside each option. Each wrong answer uses a different mistaken subject: the closest nonliving noun (the data), the background noun (the storm), or a noun that resembles the actor in grammar only (her work).

c.instruction: 두 개의 절을 제시하되 그 사이의 논리 관계(대조/인과/단순나열 중 하나)가 접속사나 구두점 없이도 문맥상 명확히 드러나도록 구성하고, 학생이 먼저 그 관계를 파악한 뒤 알맞은 구두점·접속사 조합을 고르게 하라. 정답은 논리관계에 맞는 올바른 결합(세미콜론+접속부사, 종속접속사 등)이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 콤마만으로 두 절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (2) 논리 관계가 반대인 접속사(대조인데 인과 접속사 사용 등) 사용, (3) 불필요한 접속사 중복(and+however 등 형태)을 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: earth and space science — Seafloor spreading rates and mid-ocean ridge basalt geochemistry tracing mantle composition evolution

g.passage: Geochemists comparing mid-ocean ridge basalts have found that spreading rate strongly affects how well these rocks record the mantle beneath them. At the fast-spreading East Pacific Rise, large, long-lived magma chambers thoroughly mix melts from many mantle sources, so the erupted basalts are strikingly uniform in composition______ at the slow-spreading Southwest Indian Ridge, small, short-lived melt pockets erupt before they can blend, preserving sharp isotopic differences that reveal patches of ancient recycled crust in the mantle.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , basalts erupted
; therefore, basalts erupted
; by contrast, basalts erupted
, and however, basalts erupted
g.explanation: 먼저 두 절의 논리 관계를 파악해야 한다. 빠르게 확장하는 해령에서는 마그마가 잘 섞여 현무암 조성이 균일하고, 느리게 확장하는 해령에서는 마그마가 섞이기 전에 분출해 조성 차이가 남는다. 따라서 두 절은 대조 관계이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론과 대조의 접속부사(by contrast)로 이어야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A: 콤마 하나만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. B: 세미콜론 사용은 맞지만 therefore는 인과를 나타낸다. 앞 절이 뒤 절의 원인이 아니므로 논리 관계가 맞지 않는다. D: 등위접속사 and와 접속부사 however를 겹쳐 썼다. 접속어가 불필요하게 중복되었고, and는 대조가 아닌 단순 나열을 뜻해 however와 충돌한다.
g.explanation_en: First, work out how the two clauses relate. At the fast-spreading ridge, magma mixes well, so the basalts are uniform. At the slow-spreading ridge, melts erupt before they can blend, so differences are preserved. That makes this a contrast. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon followed by a contrast transition, so C ("; by contrast,") is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B punctuates correctly, but "therefore" signals cause and effect. The uniform East Pacific Rise basalts don't cause the variation at the Southwest Indian Ridge, so the logic is wrong. D stacks the conjunction "and" on top of the adverb "however." That's a redundant double connector, and "and" signals simple addition, which clashes with "however."
g.design: 문맥(빠른 확장=균일한 조성, 느린 확장=조성 차이 보존)만으로도 대조 관계가 드러나게 썼다. 학생은 이 관계를 먼저 파악한 뒤 구두점과 접속어 조합을 골라야 한다. 오답은 콤마 스플라이스, 인과 접속부사, and+however 중복으로 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: technology and engineering — Lithium-ion battery solid electrolyte interface degradation and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy failure prediction

g.passage: As a lithium-ion battery is charged and discharged, a thin layer called the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) forms on its graphite electrode. A modest SEI protects the electrode, but the layer slowly thickens over hundreds of cycles, consuming lithium and raising the cell's internal resistance. Engineers have traditionally tracked this aging by measuring how much charge a cell can still hold, yet capacity often declines only gradually until shortly before a cell fails abruptly. Materials scientist Priya Raman and her colleagues instead applied electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, which sends small alternating currents through a cell at many frequencies and records how the cell resists each one. In tests of 120 cells, a specific shift in the mid-frequency response, linked to SEI growth, appeared dozens of cycles before capacity measurements showed any sharp change, allowing the team to flag cells nearing failure well in advance.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Raman's team found that the SEI layer protects graphite electrodes so effectively that capacity loss in lithium-ion cells can largely be prevented.
Raman's team showed that capacity measurements are more reliable than impedance readings once a lithium-ion cell has passed hundreds of cycles.
Raman's team demonstrated that the thickening of the SEI layer is the only cause of sudden failure in lithium-ion cells.
Raman's team found that an impedance-based signal tied to SEI growth can warn of lithium-ion cell failure earlier than the conventional approach does.
g.explanation: 지문은 기존의 용량 측정 방식은 고장 직전까지 변화가 거의 없지만, 임피던스 분광법에서 SEI 성장과 연관된 신호가 수십 사이클 먼저 나타나 고장을 미리 예측할 수 있었다는 점을 핵심으로 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 SEI의 보호 기능이라는 일부 세부를 과장해 연구의 초점에서 벗어난다. B는 임피던스 신호가 더 일찍 나타났다는 결과와 정반대이다. C는 SEI가 고장의 '유일한' 원인이라고 단정하는데, 지문은 그런 주장을 하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text contrasts the traditional method, capacity measurement, which changes little until just before failure, with impedance spectroscopy, whose SEI-linked signal showed up dozens of cycles earlier. That makes D the best answer. A takes one detail, the SEI's protective role, and exaggerates it, which misses the study's focus. B says the opposite of the finding, since the impedance signal came before any sharp change in capacity. C claims SEI thickening is the "only" cause of sudden failure, and the text never says that.
g.design: For the main idea, you have to connect two pieces: capacity measurement is limited, and the impedance signal comes early. The wrong answers each pull from real details (SEI protection, the comparison of methods, SEI as a cause of failure) but distort or overstate them.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Piezoelectric actuator hysteresis nonlinearity compensation in precision robotic arm control systems

g.passage: Piezoelectric actuators, which change shape when a voltage is applied, are prized in precision robotic arms because they can produce movements smaller than a micrometer. Yet their response is not perfectly predictable: when voltage rises and then falls, the actuator does not retrace the same path, so a given voltage can correspond to different positions depending on the device's recent history. This effect, called hysteresis, can introduce positioning errors of up to 15 percent of the actuator's full range. Engineers have long tried to correct for it with sensors that measure position continuously and adjust voltage in real time, but such feedback loops add cost and can slow a system's response. A team led by engineer Mireille Oduya instead built a mathematical model of how a particular actuator's past voltage inputs shape its current position, then used that model to pre-adjust each command before it was sent. In tests on a micro-assembly arm, this approach reduced hysteresis-related errors by roughly 80 percent without requiring any position sensors.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A method that anticipates a piezoelectric actuator's history-dependent behavior can substantially limit a major source of positioning error without relying on continuous measurement.
A method that measures a piezoelectric actuator's position continuously remains the most reliable way to limit positioning errors, despite its added cost.
A method that reduces the voltage supplied to a piezoelectric actuator can eliminate the history-dependent behavior that makes the device difficult to control.
A method that replaces piezoelectric actuators with less sensitive components can make robotic arms faster, though at the expense of submicrometer precision.
g.design: 이력 현상 설명과 기존 피드백 방식의 한계, 새 모델 기반 사전 보정의 결과를 연결해야 하며, 오답은 지문에 나온 센서·전압·정밀도 요소를 부분적으로 끌어와 같은 문장 틀로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 지문은 압전 액추에이터의 이력 현상이 위치 오차를 만든다는 점을 설명한 뒤, Oduya 팀이 과거 입력을 반영한 모델로 명령을 미리 보정해 센서 없이 오차를 약 80% 줄였다고 전한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 나온 센서 피드백 방식을 언급하지만, 지문은 그 방식의 비용과 속도 문제를 지적하고 대안을 제시하므로 '가장 신뢰할 만하다'는 주장은 근거가 없다. C는 전압을 다루지만, 연구는 전압을 낮춘 것이 아니라 명령을 사전 조정했고 오차도 완전히 없앤 것이 아니라 줄였다. D는 정밀도를 언급하지만 액추에이터를 다른 부품으로 교체한다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that hysteresis makes piezoelectric actuators produce positioning errors, and then describes Oduya's team using a model of past voltage inputs to pre-adjust commands, which cut those errors by about 80 percent without sensors. That makes A the correct answer. B mentions the sensor-feedback approach from the text, but the text points out that approach's cost and speed drawbacks and then presents an alternative, so nothing supports calling it the most reliable. C involves voltage, but the team pre-adjusted its commands rather than lowering the voltage, and it reduced the errors rather than eliminating them. D brings up precision, but the text never says anything about replacing the actuators with other components.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Graphene oxide membrane water desalination and selective ion transport rejection ratio optimization

g.passage: Graphene oxide membranes, made by stacking atom-thin carbon sheets, have long attracted desalination researchers because water slips through the narrow channels between layers while larger dissolved ions are held back. The difficulty is that once the membranes are soaked, the sheets swell apart, widening the channels until sodium and chloride ions pass almost as easily as water. Earlier attempts to fix this by bonding the sheets tightly together did keep salt out, but they also slowed water so much that the membranes were impractical. In a recent study, materials engineer Rafaela Okonjo and her colleagues inserted small amounts of potassium ions between the layers. The ions acted like tiny spacers that locked the channel width at just under one nanometer. Membranes treated this way rejected more than 97 percent of sodium ions while letting water flow at nearly the rate of untreated, swollen membranes, suggesting that the long-standing tradeoff between salt rejection and water flow may not be unavoidable.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Researchers have shown that bonding graphene oxide sheets tightly together is the most dependable way to keep salt from passing through the membranes.
Researchers have found a way to hold graphene oxide channels at a fixed width that appears to keep out salt without sacrificing much water flow.
Researchers have found that graphene oxide membranes swell when wet, which explains why they let water through more quickly than other materials.
Researchers have found that potassium ions pass through graphene oxide membranes more readily than sodium ions, making the membranes useful for separating the two.
g.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 칼륨 이온을 끼워 넣어 층 사이 통로 폭을 고정함으로써, 염분 차단과 물 투과 사이의 상충 관계를 극복할 수 있음을 보였다는 것이다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 단단히 결합하는 방법을 다루지만, 지문에서 이 방법은 물 흐름을 너무 느리게 만들어 실용적이지 않은 이전 시도로 소개될 뿐이다. C는 젖은 막이 팽창한다는 세부 사실은 맞지만, 팽창은 문제점으로 제시되며 글 전체의 요지가 아니다. D는 칼륨이 등장한다는 점만 맞고, 지문에서 칼륨은 통과하는 이온이 아니라 층 사이에 넣은 간격재이므로 내용을 왜곡한다.
g.explanation_en: The text's main point is that putting potassium ions between the layers locks the channel width, which suggests that the tradeoff between blocking salt and letting water through can be overcome. That makes B the correct answer. A focuses on bonding the sheets tightly, but the text presents that only as an earlier attempt that slowed water too much to be practical. C gets one detail right, since the membranes do swell when wet, but the text treats swelling as a problem, and it isn't the main idea. D picks up on potassium but misrepresents its role: the potassium ions are spacers placed between the layers, not ions that pass through the membrane.
g.design: To get this right, students have to connect two pieces of information: the problem (swelling and the tradeoff) and the solution (spacers that fix the channel width). Each wrong answer reuses a real detail from the text (tight bonding, swelling, potassium) inside the same sentence frame as the correct answer, so a quick skim can lead to a wrong choice.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Passive heat pipe capillary pumping mechanism in satellite thermal management systems

g.passage: Satellites face a difficult thermal problem: electronics on the sunlit side can overheat while components in shadow grow dangerously cold, and there is no air to carry heat between them. Many spacecraft address this with heat pipes, sealed metal tubes containing a small amount of working fluid such as ammonia. At the hot end, the fluid evaporates and the vapor flows toward the cold end, where it condenses and releases its heat. What returns the liquid to the hot end is a porous wick lining the tube's inner wall. Through capillary action, the tiny pores draw liquid along the wick in the same way a paper towel soaks up a spill, so the cycle continues without any pump. Because the device has no moving parts and draws no electrical power, engineers value it for missions in which repairs are impossible. Its capacity is limited, however: if too much heat enters the hot end, the liquid evaporates faster than the wick can return it, and that end dries out.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Heat pipes on satellites rely on ammonia because that fluid evaporates more readily than any other substance in the vacuum of space.
Heat pipes on satellites have largely replaced other cooling methods because they can absorb unlimited amounts of heat without failing.
Heat pipes on satellites move heat through a self-sustaining cycle of evaporation and wick-driven liquid return, which makes them reliable but limits how much heat they can handle.
Heat pipes on satellites depend on a wick to move vapor from the cold end back to the hot end, much as a paper towel absorbs liquid.
g.explanation: 지문은 증발·응축과 심지(wick)의 모세관 작용으로 펌프 없이 순환하는 히트파이프의 원리, 그 신뢰성, 그리고 열 용량의 한계를 함께 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 암모니아가 예시로만 언급될 뿐 '다른 어떤 물질보다' 잘 증발한다는 비교는 지문에 없다. B는 지문 끝의 '용량에 한계가 있다'는 내용과 정면으로 모순된다. D는 심지와 종이 타월 비유를 정확히 가져왔지만, 심지가 옮기는 것은 증기가 아니라 액체이고 이동 방향도 차가운 쪽에서 뜨거운 쪽으로 가는 액체이므로 세부 내용이 틀렸으며 중심 내용도 아니다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct because the text explains how heat pipes run a pump-free cycle of evaporation, condensation, and capillary return of liquid through a wick, why that makes them reliable, and how their heat capacity is limited. A misreads ammonia, which is offered only as an example; the text never says it evaporates better than any other substance. B contradicts the final sentence, which says the capacity is limited and the hot end can dry out. D borrows the wick and paper-towel comparison, but the wick carries liquid, not vapor, so the detail is wrong, and it also misses the text's broader point.
g.design: Medium: the correct choice combines the mechanism with its trade-off, while distractors reuse real details from the text (ammonia, the wick analogy) but distort them or overstate claims, so careful comparison is needed to rule them out.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Additive manufacturing metal powder bed fusion and residual stress redistribution in aerospace turbine blades

g.passage: In laser powder bed fusion, a metal turbine blade is built layer by layer as a laser melts fine alloy powder. Because each new layer cools and contracts on top of layers that have already solidified, strong residual stresses become locked inside the part. Engineers at one aerospace firm found that a post-build heat treatment did not simply erase these stresses; instead, it ______ them, shifting the highest tension away from the blade's thin trailing edge and spreading it more evenly through the thicker root, where the material could better tolerate it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: intensified
concealed
eliminated
redistributed
g.explanation: "did not simply erase"라는 대조와 이어지는 설명(가장 큰 인장 응력을 얇은 후연부에서 두꺼운 뿌리 쪽으로 옮기고 고르게 퍼뜨림)이 응력의 위치와 분포가 바뀌었음을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 열처리가 응력에 변화를 줬다는 점은 맞지만, 응력을 '더 고르게 퍼뜨렸다'는 설명과 반대된다. B는 응력이 사라진 것은 아니라는 점과 들어맞는 것처럼 보이지만, 지문은 응력이 가려졌다는 것이 아니라 실제로 옮겨졌다고 말한다. C는 지문이 '단순히 없애지 않았다'고 명시한 내용과 정면으로 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The contrast "did not simply erase... instead" plus the description that follows (moving the highest tension from the thin trailing edge and spreading it through the root) shows the stresses changed location and distribution, so D is correct. A fits the idea that the treatment changed the stresses, but it contradicts the stresses being spread "more evenly." B seems to match the point that the stresses didn't disappear, but the text says they were actually moved, not hidden. C directly contradicts the statement that the treatment did not erase the stresses.
g.design: To answer, students have to link the "not simply erase" contrast with the following description of stress being moved. Each distractor matches part of the context (the stresses change, the stresses still exist, the heat treatment is meant to remove stress), so the options have to be compared carefully.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Microfluidic lab-on-chip device droplet manipulation and PCR amplification miniaturization for diagnostics

g.passage: Conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR), which copies DNA so that trace amounts can be detected, typically requires benchtop thermal cyclers and sample volumes measured in tens of microliters. Engineers developing microfluidic "lab-on-a-chip" devices have shown that splitting a sample into thousands of picoliter droplets, each heated and cooled as it moves through channels etched in a chip, can ______ this process: the same amplification occurs, but in a device small enough to hold in one hand and with each cycle finishing in seconds rather than minutes.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: condense
replicate
supplant
complicate
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤에서 같은 증폭이 일어나지만 손바닥 크기 장치에서 더 짧은 시간에 끝난다고 설명하므로, 과정을 동일하게 유지하면서 크기와 시간을 줄인다는 뜻의 A(condense)가 정확하다. B(replicate)는 같은 증폭이 일어난다는 부분과는 맞지만, 지문의 핵심인 소형화와 시간 단축을 담지 못한다. C(supplant)는 새로운 방식이라는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 같은 증폭 과정이 유지된다고 했으므로 PCR 자체를 다른 것으로 대체한다는 의미는 맞지 않는다. D(complicate)는 장치가 더 작고 빨라졌다는 설명과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: After the colon, the text says the same amplification happens, but in a handheld device and with cycles that take seconds instead of minutes. That means the process is kept the same while being shrunk in size and time, so A ("condense") is the precise choice. B ("replicate") matches the idea that the same amplification occurs, but it misses the key point about miniaturization and speed. C ("supplant") might seem plausible because the device is a new approach, but the text says the PCR process itself is kept, not replaced by something else. D ("complicate") goes against the description of a smaller, faster device.
g.design: The answer requires linking the blank to both clauses after the colon (the same process, but smaller and faster). B fits only the first clause and C fits only the "new technology" idea, so you have to compare them against the full context to rule them out.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Self-cleaning titanium dioxide nanocoating photocatalytic decomposition under UV radiation exposure

g.passage: Some modern buildings stay clean with very little scrubbing because their windows and walls are covered with an extremely thin layer of titanium dioxide. This coating is far thinner than a human hair and cannot be seen. When sunlight strikes it, the ultraviolet part of the light energizes the titanium dioxide, which then breaks down dirt, grease, and other materials made of carbon that have stuck to the surface. The coating also causes rainwater to spread out in a smooth sheet instead of forming droplets, so the rain rinses away whatever has been broken down. In this way, sunlight and rain together do much of the cleaning work that people would otherwise have to do.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A titanium dioxide coating keeps buildings clean mainly by blocking rain from ever reaching windows and walls.
A titanium dioxide coating helps surfaces clean themselves by using sunlight to break down grime that rain then washes off.
A titanium dioxide coating keeps buildings clean mainly by making surfaces too smooth for dirt to stick in the first place.
A titanium dioxide coating helps surfaces stay clean only when people scrub them regularly after rainstorms.
g.explanation: 지문은 이산화티타늄 코팅이 자외선을 받아 오염물을 분해하고, 빗물이 넓게 퍼져 분해된 것을 씻어 내어 햇빛과 비가 청소를 대신한다고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 코팅이 빗물을 막는다고 하지만, 지문에서는 오히려 빗물이 표면에 얇게 퍼져 씻어 낸다. C는 먼지가 애초에 붙지 않는다고 하지만, 지문은 표면에 붙은 먼지를 분해한다고 말한다. D는 사람이 정기적으로 문질러야 한다고 하지만, 지문은 거의 문지르지 않아도 된다고 한다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that the coating uses the ultraviolet part of sunlight to break down dirt, and that rain spreads into a sheet and rinses that material away, so B is correct. A is wrong because the coating does not block rain; it makes rain spread across the surface so it can rinse it. C is wrong because the text says dirt does stick to the surface and is then broken down, not that dirt never sticks. D is wrong because the text says these buildings need very little scrubbing, since sunlight and rain do most of the work.
g.design: 핵심 과정(자외선 분해+빗물 세척)을 직접 서술하고, 오답은 같은 문장 틀로 비 차단·부착 방지·사람 청소라는 흔한 오해를 담았다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Composite laminate interlaminar fracture toughness and Mode I delamination crack propagation resistance testing

g.passage: Composite laminates are made by stacking thin layers of fiber-reinforced material and bonding them together. One common weakness of these materials is delamination, in which the layers begin to separate. To measure how well a laminate resists this kind of failure, engineers often use a test called the double cantilever beam test. A small crack is placed between two layers at one end of a sample, and the two arms of the sample are slowly pulled apart. By recording the force needed to make the crack grow, engineers can calculate a value that shows how much energy the material absorbs before the layers split further. Higher values mean that a laminate is better at holding its layers together.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Engineers use a pulling test to make composite laminates stronger by adding extra layers to each sample.
Engineers have found that the double cantilever beam test causes composite laminates to fail more often than other tests do.
Engineers use a specific test to measure how well composite laminates resist the separation of their layers.
Engineers prefer composite laminates to other materials because their layers never separate under force.
g.explanation: 지문은 복합 적층재의 약점인 층 분리(delamination)를 소개한 뒤, 이 분리에 대한 저항을 측정하는 이중 외팔보 시험의 방법과 의미를 설명하므로 C가 중심 내용이다. A는 시험이 재료를 더 강하게 만든다고 하지만, 지문에서 시험은 측정 수단일 뿐이다. B는 이 시험이 다른 시험보다 파손을 더 많이 일으킨다는 비교를 말하지만 지문에 그런 비교는 없다. D는 층이 절대 분리되지 않는다고 하지만, 지문은 층 분리를 흔한 약점으로 제시한다.
g.explanation_en: The text introduces delamination, a common weakness of composite laminates, and then explains how the double cantilever beam test measures resistance to it, so C states the main idea. A says the test makes laminates stronger, but the text presents the test only as a way to measure strength. B makes a comparison with other tests that the text never makes. D claims the layers never separate, which contradicts the text's description of delamination as a common weakness.
g.design: 쉬운 어휘로 '목적-방법' 구조를 제시하고, 오답은 시험의 기능 왜곡·근거 없는 비교·지문과 반대되는 진술이라는 전형적 오개념으로 구성했다.
